body:
## Code changes
- Gate phase-start announcements to actual foreground interval transitions; no repeated 'Work' prompts on mid-interval recovery or after long suspension.
- Require a naturally finished, unskipped timer before reporting completion; add pure regression tests for these guards.
- Honor Lapis's saved `startSound`, `announceRounds`, `announceExercise`, and `announceNext` voice options; add tests for bell/voice/silent modes.
- Cache parsed timer snapshots once per loaded Coach workout rather than re-parsing on each timer tick.
- Prevent duplicate save submissions, persist newly-created assignment IDs into draft sessions, reuse the same assignment when retrying a failed log insert, and validate a matching log exists on duplicate-key errors.
- Prevent changing client association while retrying a pending saved assignment.

## Outstanding checks
Draft and unmerged. Requires Jenkins `cd app && npm test && npm run typecheck`, staging SQL migrations from prior PRs, and Android/iOS background audio/notification tests.

## Dependencies
Stacked on Coach PR #14 -> #13 -> #12 -> #11 -> #10. Separate standalone Lapis PR #4 is parallel. No database changes in this PR.

## Known limits
If the initial assignment INSERT succeeds server-side but the network drops before the ID returns, the client still cannot recover that unknown ID without a server-side idempotency key; this PR handles the common case where the ID was received and the subsequent log write failed. Full standalone Lapis voice parity and multiple concurrent timer sound-mixing still need device verification.

author: devanfer02
body:
## Summary

On my phone, a search with 19 rows from Jul 2025 to Oct 2026 showed four problems with the price chart. The line and dots were too heavy, ten years of prices would squeeze into one card width, tapping a dot did nothing, and there was no Y axis. I redrew the chart and bumped the version to 2.0.1 so it ships as a patch release.

## What changed

- **Chart** (`ui/search/PriceLineChart.kt`, replaces `ui/shared/PriceLine.kt`)
  - 1.5 dp line, 3 dp markers. Markers drop out when points average under 12 dp apart; the latest point always keeps one.
  - Y axis with 3 or 4 round gridlines that start near the lowest price, not at 0. A price moving between 35 rb and 41 rb used to look flat on an axis from zero.
  - First, middle and last date under the plot.
  - Tap or drag selects the nearest point by date. A guide line, a ringed marker and a label above the plot show its date and price. Tapping the same point again clears it.
  - TalkBack reads the chart as one adjustable control: swipe up or down to step through points ("28 Jul 2025, Rp 100.000"). Next and Previous price actions are there too.
  - Plot is 136 dp (was 88). Axis text is capped at 130% like other slot labels, so 200% font keeps the shape.
- **Range chips** (`ui/search/PriceCard.kt`, `SearchScreen.kt`): 6M, 1Y, 3Y, All, counted back from the latest purchase. A chip only shows if its range holds 2 or more points and fewer than the next longer range. Opens on 1Y when that chip shows, otherwise All. Lowest, highest, change and the spoken summary follow the range. The pick is kept per item with `rememberSaveable`.
- **Assembly** (`ui/search/PriceChartAssembly.kt`): `ranges`, `defaultRange`, `inRange`, `priceChart`, `priceAxis`, `nearestPoint`, all pure. Over 18 months with more than 60 priced days, the chart averages each month (half up, `Long`), so ten years of weekly shopping is 120 points instead of 520. Lowest and highest always name the real day.
- **Axis labels** (`ui/theme/Format.kt`): `formatIdrAxis` now prints exact ticks (`2,5 rb`, `38,9 rb`, `1,25 jt`) instead of rounding. This also fixes Stats, where a 2.500 tick read `3 rb`. It is still the only axis formatter.
- **Version** (`app/build.gradle.kts`): `versionCode` 2 to 3, `versionName` 2.0 to 2.0.1.
- Design notes and the spec change are in `openspec/changes/price-chart-rework/`.

## What I tried and dropped

- Averaging by month whenever the range spanned 18 months. On the emulator, 3Y with four rows merged two October prices into one value that matched neither, while the figures underneath named the real lowest. Now it also needs more than 60 points.
- Offering every range that cuts the history. With rows yearly since 2016 and two in late October, 6M and 1Y were the same two points. A range now has to hold fewer points than the next longer one.
- `SegmentedTabs` for the ranges. A full-width bar right above Daily/Monthly/Yearly read as a second set of tabs, so the ranges use `FilterChip`, the same as the item chips.

## Caveats

- The line is 1.5 dp and markers are 3 dp, under the 2 px line and 4 px dots I normally use for charts. 2 dp on a 420 dpi phone is over 5 px and looked heavy in practice.
- A big jump (phone at 2 jt, 18 jt, 38 jt, then 5 jt) stays on a linear axis of 0, 20 jt and 40 jt, so the 2 jt and 5 jt points sit close to the bottom. I kept it linear because a log scale would make the jump look smaller than it was.

## Test plan

- [x] `:app:lintDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug` green locally: 1069 tests, 0 failed, 3 skipped. 15 new: 14 in `PriceChartAssemblyTest` (ranges, monthly points, Y ticks, the phone jump, nearest point) and 1 in `FormatIdrTest`.
- [x] Emulator (API 35): searched `minyak goreng 2l` (13 rows, 2016 to 2026) and `handphone`. Checked light and dark, each range, tap and drag, and font scale 2.0.
- [ ] CI "Tests, lint and debug build" passes
- [ ] After merge, the master run's `saku-release-apk` reports versionName 2.0.1

author: rennf93
body:
Follow-up to [trail #229](https://entire.com/gh/rennf93/-/trails/229) ([change 366](https://entire.com/gh/rennf93/-/trails/229/changes/roboco/366)): a Claude session limit kept spawning agents back into itself until it reset.

The fleet hit the five-hour limit on 2026-11-04. Every agent's own output said when it would end: `"status":"rejected","resetsAt":1793780400,"rateLimitType":"five_hour"`, which is 08:20:00Z. The park, though, lasted only `_RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER_S` (300 s). After that the probe "succeeded":
- with no `anthropic_api_key` set (the NAS has none), `_do_probe` trusts elapsed time;
- with a key, `GET /v1/models` answers no matter what the subscription window says.

From the 06:25Z deploy to 08:22Z the dispatcher logged 43 probe lifts and 93 spawns, and all 93 ended in `Session/usage limit detected in agent output; parking provider`.

`_maybe_park_for_exit_error` now parks for `_session_limit_retry_after(agent_id)`. That function reads the largest `resetsAt` in the dead run's container log, and in its transcript, where the event is JSON-escaped. It parks until that time plus 30 s. With no future reset reported it falls back to the 300 s floor, and it caps a nonsense value at eight days, the longest window Claude reports. `_too_early_to_probe` already holds the probe until `activated_at + retry_after`, so the probe itself is unchanged.

Also in the touched test file: its nine trailing comments are lifted onto their own lines (the conventions check flagged them).

## Verified
- Without the fix, 7 tests fail (`7 failed, 27 passed`): the reset from the log, the escaped transcript, three floor cases (no event, a past reset, no `resetsAt`), the cap, and the park wiring. With it: `34 passed`.
- The parking, rate-limit and decisions-parking runtime suites: `149 passed`.
- ruff format, ruff check, mypy and conventions on the changed files: clean. `verify_codebase_map.py`: `0 errors (none); 0 warnings (none)`.
- The full `make quality` runs in CI.

body:
## Summary
The app now refreshes on its own when the collector writes new snapshots. It watches the data directory (ADR 0001: no push, the collector stays independent) and emits the Tauri event `store-changed`, which the overview listens to.

## Changes
- `app/src-tauri/src/watch.rs`: `notify` watcher on `paths::data_dir`, filtered to `tamias.db` and `tamias.db-wal`, 500 ms debounce, 60 s fallback timer; watches the parent while the data dir does not exist; watcher errors are logged and fall back to the timer; thread owned by app state, stopped and joined on exit; injectable emitter and watcher for tests
- Only content writes and removals count as writes, so the app's own read-only open (which recreates an empty `-wal`) cannot trigger a reload loop
- `today` fails with `CommandError { message, busy }`; a busy store keeps the current view and retries on the next event
- Frontend: `core/store-events.ts`; the overview reloads on `store-changed`, late answers of older loads are dropped
- New dependencies: `notify` 8.2.1, `serde`

## Verification
On macOS: `cargo test -p tamias-app` (27 tests, 13 new in `tests/watch.rs`), clippy, fmt, `pnpm lint`, `check`, `format:check`, `test` (44 tests) clean. author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
## What changed and why `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` was set to the Supabase **secret** key instead of the public anon key. Because Next.js inlines every `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable into the browser bundle, Supabase rejected requests with "Forbidden use of secret API key in browser" and the secret was exposed to anyone who inspected the bundle. `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` also held a placeholder, breaking admin features (adding employees, changing roles). Both variables have been corrected: - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` → public anon key (safe for the browser) - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` → service-role key (server-only, admin-guarded code) A build-time guard was added to `next.config.mjs` that stops the build with a clear error if any `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable contains a Supabase secret or service-role key, preventing this class of mistake from reaching production again. The example env file was updated to document which key belongs in which variable. > **Recommended action:** Revoke the previously exposed secret key in the Supabase dashboard (Settings → API Keys) if that hasn't been done yet. ### Notable changes - **`next.config.mjs`** – build-time check that aborts if a secret key is found in any `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable - **`.env.local.example`** – clarified which Supabase key goes in each variable

body:
## GD-31J.27bq — stacked DRAFT on PR #181

### Implementation (READ-ONLY, not wired to production capture)
- Added `RecoveryPinnedLinuxParentProbe.cs`: accepts an **already held SafeFileHandle** for a directory, retains its native reference through the returned lease and opens a narrowly validated child basename **relative** to that pinned handle using `syscall(openat2)`. Strict `RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_XDEV`, with `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`. No insecure `open`/path-based fallback for unsupported Linux kernel/architecture.
- Uses handle-bound `statx(AT_EMPTY_PATH)` to verify complete directory type, UID == `geteuid()`, exact owner-only **0700**, inode/device/mount ID, and same parent observations before/after child open. The parent handle remains pinned until the lease is disposed. The initial parent itself **is not yet proven to originate from a trustworthy filesystem anchor**.
- Added `RecoveryWindowsPinnedParentProbe.cs`: opens an **existing** directory for diagnostics with `CreateFileW(FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS | FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, READ_CONTROL|FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES)`, rejects final reparse points and keeps its OS handle until lease disposal. Windows ancestor traversal remains path-based and race-prone.
- Added `RecoveryWindowsParentSecurityProbe.cs`: read-only `GetSecurityInfo(SE_FILE_OBJECT, OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION|DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION)` on that held handle, `ConvertSidToStringSidW` and proper `LocalFree` plus full native file ID. Its **denial-only** gate rejects incomplete ID, mismatched/malformed owner SID or NULL DACL, and *still refuses capture* for a matching owner and present DACL until a real ACE/effective-token-privilege audit is designed and tested.

### Test specifications only (NOT executed)
- 7 MSTest cases in `RecoveryPinnedLinuxParentTests.cs` for statx owner/mode, no-follow basename restrictions, pinned directory observation and symlink denial.
- 9 MSTest cases in `RecoveryWindowsParentSecurityTests.cs` for Owner SID/DACL denial, malformed identity, handle-bound reading, reparse point and pinned-directory diagnostics.
- 9 Python source-only contract methods, acceptance runner registration, five manual **not-run** gates (Astra/openat2, UID/mount alias, Windows SID/DACL, full Windows ACE/token privileges, hostile parent rename). Stacked recovery source chain extended.
- Russian technical report `docs/GET_DOCUMENT_GD31J27BQ_PINNED_PARENT_SECURITY_2026-11-04.md`.

### Verification and unresolved P1
GitHub compare against BP: **10 commits / 9 files**, and source read-back **27/27 static structural predicates**. **No dotnet build, MSTest, Python unittest, CI, native P/Invoke call, Windows/Astra/SMB validation, mount namespace test, SIGKILL or race-fault injection executed.**

**These probes are deliberately NOT registered with `OfficeRecoveryStore.CaptureAsync` or `RecoverySharedVolumeCoordinator`; Windows/Linux capture identity adapters still `SupportsVerifiedRootAndLockIdentity=false`.** No documents, WORM, GUP-2 or native SaveAs changed. Neither a pinned handle, matching inode, owner SID, 0700 mode nor present DACL guarantees writer isolation until trusted anchor and full permissions/effective rights are proved. No path-based auto-delete or recovery promotion.

Keep **Draft / `releaseReady=false`** and do not merge or deploy before offline platform certification and independent security review.

author: chiangs
body:
## Why

The owner chose React with Tailwind as the standard for prototypes, to keep the CSS and the code pane small. It has to work in the preview with no dev server, and outside Fenmyr with Vite.

## What changed

- **The starter.** The React starter's `main.tsx` imports `src/styles.css` (`@import "tailwindcss";`). `App.tsx` follows the default guidance: every value and class list is named before the return. The board's name is quoted with `JSON.stringify`, so "Ann's flow" stays one string.
- **In the preview.**
  - Tailwind's browser build (`@tailwindcss/browser`, MIT) ships in `web/dist/proto-tailwind.js` like React.
  - The bundler drops the `tailwindcss` import and inlines the stylesheet as `<style type="text/tailwindcss">`, so Tailwind makes the CSS from the classes and any `@theme` inside the frame, offline.
  - The preview's CSS is generated as the page runs, not at build time, so it can differ slightly from a real build.
- **Outside Fenmyr.** `prototypes/` gets `vite.config.ts` with `@tailwindcss/vite`, and `package.json` lists `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/vite`. The README says `npm run dev -- <folder>`.
- **Instructions.** `myra.md` and the builder's instructions say to style with Tailwind and to put theme values in `@theme`.
- **Housekeeping.** THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES gains `@tailwindcss/browser`, and knip knows it's used through the build.

## How to test

- `node tests/preview.ts` checks that a `p-4` class gives 16 px of padding in the frame, and that the starter's Tailwind base applies.
- `node tests/prototype.ts` checks the starter's named title.
- `npm run check:fast` and `npm test` pass. `npm run visual` reports only `settings-helpers`, as listed in `tools/visual-expected.json`.

body:
## Summary

Before `enforceHashes` can be switched on, 33 honest players carry `CustomSkinLoader-Common.jar` with a unique SHA-1 per install (a launcher rewrites the jar), so no hash can ever verify it. This is the client half of the namespace-approved rule; the relay half (dp-relay `dev/namespace-approved`) ships the same rule under the same key.

- **Rule** (`UnapprovedModIntegrity.namespaceVerified`): a file whose hash is not approved still counts as VERIFIED when every id it declares (exempt ids skipped) is a key of `namespaceApproved`, its package fingerprint is non-empty, and every package key equals a root or starts with `root + "."` for a root of one of its declared ids. One foreign package falls back to today's tiers. The engine's `tierOf` is untouched; hash still wins first.
- **Curated list**: `approved_mods.curated.json` gains `namespaceApproved: {"customskinloader": ["customskinloader"]}` + `namespaceApprovedWhy`. `generateApprovedMods` bakes it and fails the build if a listed id is not an approved id.
- **ApprovedModList**: parses `namespaceApproved` from the baked resource, the relay payload and the disk cache (relay overlays baked); accessor `namespaceApproved()`.
- **Fallback hint** (option 2): a listed id whose file still fails shows "Install from Modrinth/CurseForge" in the Unsupported Mods popup (blue, like the Essential update line) and the login notice sends `chat.dungeontrain.free_play.install_from_store` naming the mod. Two new lang keys in all 22 locales, provenance stamped, credits resynced.

**Mod-impact check:** no new dependencies, mixins, registries, worldgen or packets. One new key in the baked JSON and the relay's HTTP JSON (no `PROTOCOL_VERSION` change).

#31에 이어서 두 가지를 추가합니다: 플래시 전환 기법, 그리고 미리 정의한 이징 프리셋.

## 1. 플래시 전환 (transition-flash-streak)

사선으로 빠른 선이 지나가고 특정 색으로 번쩍이는 효과입니다.

- 추가 파일: `references/shots/transition-flash-streak.md`, `templates/shots/transition-flash-streak.mjs`
- 선: 흰색·브랜드 색 선 4가닥이 −28° 사선으로 지나갑니다. 각 선은 0.18초에 화면을 건너고, 선 사이에는 2프레임 시차를 둡니다. 마지막 굵은 선이 가운데를 지나는 순간이 컷입니다.
- 번쩍임: 프레임 가득 Shape입니다. opacity는 컷 2프레임 전 0, 컷에서 0.9, 컷 4프레임 뒤 0입니다. 소재는 최고점에서 바뀝니다.
- 갱신한 문서: shots/README, director §8, TREATMENT에 "플래시"를 넣었습니다.
- 샘플: `samples/transitions`를 다시 렌더했고 갤러리 항목도 갱신했습니다.

## 2. 이징 프리셋

- **`references/easing.md`**
  - 용도별 모션 토큰 12개(enter, exit, move, snap, whip, glide, drift, pop, anticipate, wobble, drop, count): 토큰마다 이징 이름과 권장 길이가 있습니다.
  - 곡선 31종 표: linear 1종과 10계열 × In/Out/InOut입니다.
  - 고르는 규칙:
    - 들어올 때 Out, 나갈 때 In, 화면 안에서 옮길 때 InOut
    - 넘치는 곡선은 작은 요소에만, 광고 하나에 한 계열만
    - opacity에는 Back·Elastic을 쓰지 않음
  - 전환 클립 `easing` 사용법
- **`motion.mjs`**: `EASE`(토큰 표), `EASING_NAMES`, `ease(토큰|이름)`. 모르는 이름이면 에러를 냅니다. 엔진은 모르는 이름을 조용히 선형으로 바꾸기 때문입니다.
- **`validate.mjs`**:
  - 전환 클립의 `easing` 이름을 검사합니다.
  - opacity 구간에 넘치는 이징이 걸리면 경고합니다.
- **`to-admaker-import.mjs`**: `am-*` 전환을 앱 서버 인코딩용 xfade 이름(fadewhite, circleclose, zoomin, smoothleft)으로 바꾸고, 클립별 값과 easing이 서버 렌더에서 빠진다고 경고합니다.
- **SKILL.md, engine-recipes**: easing.md로 가는 링크와 `am-*` 전환 팩 안내(`values`, `easing`)를 넣었습니다.

토큰 표는 엔진의 `MOTION_TOKENS`와 같습니다(kingsae1/admaker-plugin#24). JSON에는 토큰이 아니라 이징 이름이 들어가므로 3.0.7 엔진에서도 그대로 재생됩니다. `am-*` 전환과 전환 클립 `easing`은 #24가 들어간 엔진부터 동작합니다.

## 확인한 것
- 플래시 전환
  - 엔진 3.0.7 렌더 하니스(Preview 스틸, Exporter mp4)로 렌더하고, 밀집 시트를 초당 30장으로 뽑아 확인했습니다.
  - `validate.mjs`를 통과합니다.
- 이징
  - `ease()`와 `EASING_NAMES`를 node로 확인했습니다.
  - `validate.mjs`와 `to-admaker-import.mjs`를 `am-*` 전환 4종이 든 테스트 프로젝트로 돌렸습니다. 검사는 통과했고, 전환 4개 모두 xfade 이름으로 바뀌며 경고가 나왔습니다.
- 앱 미리보기와 서버 렌더는 확인하지 않았습니다.

body: Stacked on #52. The docs added six stress methods on 2026-10-12. This first half reads, creates, updates and deletes stresses; running them, cancelling runs and adding a found countertest to the tests come in #54. The wrapper had no way to reach stresses at all. New in `polygon_api`: * `Polygon.problem_stresses(problem_id, stress_index=None, pin=None)` and the `Problem.stresses(stress_index=None, pin=None)` shortcut, returning a list of `Stress` objects in the order of their indices. With `stress_index` the list holds only that stress, as the API returns a list in that case too. * `Polygon.problem_save_stress(problem_id, stress_index=None, script_pattern=None, solution_names=None, time_limit=None, memory_limit=None, total_time_limit=None, testset=None, group=None, ignore_validators=None, description=None, pin=None)` and the `Problem.save_stress(...)` shortcut, returning the saved `Stress`. * `Polygon.problem_delete_stress(problem_id, stress_index, pin=None)` and the `Problem.delete_stress(stress_index, pin=None)` shortcut. * `Stress`, `StressRun`, `StressCountertest`, `StressSolutionReport`, `StressRunStatus` (PENDING/RUNNING/FINISHED), `StressRunVerdict` (OK/FAILED/CRASHED) and `StressSolutionVerdict`, all exported. `StressSolutionVerdict` has the eight verdicts the docs list for a report and the two they say the model also allows, TIME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_OR_ACCEPTED and TIME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_OR_MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. All three are enums because the docs spell their value sets out in full. ```python stress = problem.save_stress(script_pattern='gen 10 [5..100] abacaba', solution_names=['wa.cpp'], total_time_limit=30000) problem.save_stress(stress.index, description='') # update: clear the description only stress, = problem.stresses(stress.index) ``` `problem.saveStress` creates a stress without `stressIndex` and updates the stress with one. A creation needs `scriptPattern` and `solutionNames`, which the wrapper checks with a `ValueError`, since the check doesn't depend on the state of the problem. On update, an argument left as `None` is not sent and keeps its value. An empty `testset`, `group` or `description` clears it, and `Request` drops only `None`, so `''` reaches the API. `solution_names` takes a list or a comma-separated string, like the other comma-separated parameters. A save discards the result of the previous run, so the returned `Stress` has `run=None`, and a running stress is not cancelled by a save or a deletion. The docstrings point to `problem.cancelStresses` for that. The fields the docs mark as absent when unset are `None`: `testset`, `group` and `run` of a `Stress`; `verdict`, `comment` and the statistics of a `StressRun` that is not FINISHED; `countertest`; the `input` of a countertest rejected before its input was received; and `output`, `answer` and `comment` of a report. Tests: parsing of every object, every status and verdict, a running stress with only a status, a failed run, and a countertest without input; the request contents of all three methods and their shortcuts, a creation, an update sending only what it changes, and the empty values that clear fields; the `ValueError` cases; the pin rows; and four tests through the local API server: the example `problem.stresses` response from the docs, a creation with a non-ASCII description, an empty description surviving the multipart encoding, and a deletion answered without a `result` field. `flake8` clean, `pytest -q`: 1055 passed. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

## Summary

Supersedes #99 by @koteitan, which this PR builds on and credits as co-author.

Notes that only some relays have could not be found.
- An nevent's relay hints were ignored when adding it.
- A list's hints were never read when viewing or editing it.

### Reading hints

- **Adding an nevent:** the relays it hints at are asked too.
- **Viewing or editing a list:** the relays its notes hint at are asked too.
  - The hints come from each note's e tag and from the nevents in the content, which can hold several.
  - The relays that more notes hint at come first.
- **A client of their own:** hinted relays get a separate rx-nostr client, used for this request only.
  - It closes when the request ends, so hints never join the shared relays.
  - Its relays are closed first, and it is disposed once none is still connecting. rx-nostr 0.9 throws when a socket that was still connecting reports its error after `dispose()`.
- **Limits**, because hints come from anyone's list:
  - At most 8 hinted relays per request.
  - Only `wss://` URLs without credentials.
  - Only public host names: no IP addresses, `localhost`, single-label names, or `.local`, `.localhost`, `.internal` and `.home.arpa` hosts.
  - At most 255 characters, the most an nevent can hold.
  - Hints are normalized: no trailing slash on the path, no trailing dot on the host, no fragment. The query is kept.

### Writing hints

- The relay that returned a note comes first among its hints, so a list saved with a dead hint now points to a relay that has the note.
- Each e tag gets the first hint.
- The nevent in the content gets the first 3, so editing and saving a list keeps the hints that matter. Without a cap, an nevent with many hints, plus the relay that returned it, could exceed nostr-tools' 5000-character limit and fail to save.

### Checking events

A relay can answer with any event, under any ID. `rx-nostr`'s `verify()` checks the signature against the event's own hash, not against the ID it claims.
- **Forged notes:** a relay could show a note signed by anyone under a requested ID.
- **Hidden notes:** a bad copy that arrived first used up the ID in `uniq()`, so the real note was dropped.
- **Malformed events:** a relay that sent `null` as the event threw in the filter, which left the list page on a spinner and the editor's notes tab empty.
- **Now:** both note stores keep only requested kind 1 event objects whose ID is their hash, then verify them, then drop duplicates.
- **Editor:** if loading a list's notes still fails, the notes tab opens with them shown as not found, so the list can still be edited and saved. A failed request in the recent reactions tab likewise shows what it found instead of loading forever.
- This gap was already on `main` for the default relays. Hints made it reachable from any relay named in anyone's list.

## Validation

- `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, and 142 unit tests passed.
- **New tests:**
  - `decodeNoteId`, using the nevent from #99;
  - `normalizeRelayHint` and `relayHints`: the query, trailing slashes and dots, local hosts, the length limit;
  - `LongFormContent`:
    - compose with hints, and the 3-hint cap;
    - `noteReferences` from e tags and content nevents;
    - a compose round trip;
    - `noteRelays` ranking;
  - `notesStore`/`noteStore`:
    - the hinted client, which is closed and disposed, and is not created when the shared relays cover the hints;
    - the 8-relay limit;
    - the relay that returned each note;
    - a forged ID;
    - an event that was not requested;
    - a tampered copy and a bad signature arriving first;
    - `null` and string events;
    - dispose waiting for a relay that is still connecting;
  - the editor: added and listed notes found on a hinted relay, the returning relay put first, and failed requests in both tabs.
- In headless Chromium, with a throwaway nsec login and every relay mocked, a note that only `wss://hint.example.com` has:

| Step | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Add its nevent | "Failed to get a note." | the note |
| Saved e tag / content nevent | `['e', id]` / no relays | `['e', id, 'wss://hint.example.com']` / the hint |
| List page, then edit page | "Failed to get a note." | the note |
| Hint sockets afterwards | none | each closed; none opened on the home page |

- A second run in headless Chromium:
  - **Setup:** hosts resolve only to local stand-ins: one relay that accepts and never answers, and one that resets. The default relays answer 300 ms late.
  - **Dead hints first:** an nevent hinting `[hang, reset, hint]` finds the note, and the list is saved with `wss://hint.example.com` in its e tag.
  - **Bad hint relays:** for an nevent whose hint relay sends a forged note, and one whose hint relay sends a tampered copy first, the editor and the list page show the genuine notes.
  - **Many hints:** someone else's list with 40 different hints opens 8 hint sockets, all closed afterwards.
  - **Malformed events:** a hint relay that sends `["EVENT", sub, null]` before the genuine note: the list and edit pages show the note.
  - **Page errors:** none. Earlier versions of this change threw `ObjectUnsubscribedError` for hint relays that were still connecting, and a `TypeError` for a `null` event.
- No test reached a real relay.

## Not changed

- **Timeout:** a hint relay connects from scratch within the same 1-second timeout, so a distant one can miss it.
- **Re-adding:** an added note that was not found cannot be added again with a better nevent until it is removed.
- **Links:** note links and "Failed to get a note." still show `note1…` without hints.

author: xunzhuo
body:
Adds an opt-in `capture_tool_results` setting so Router Replay can store client tool results for development and audit. The default keeps today's redaction.

Closes #5806

## Purpose

Router Replay keeps only a client tool result's call ID and status, and removes tool results from a captured request body, whether or not the tool-result PII scan from #3560 runs. A team debugging an agent's tool loop cannot see what a tool returned.

This PR adds `capture_tool_results`, default `false`, to `global.services.router_replay` and to the decision `router_replay` plugin overlay. It inherits like the other capture fields.

- **When on:** each `client_tool_result` step stores the result text in `output` with `content_redacted: false`, cut to `max_tool_trace_bytes` and flagged `truncated` when cut. A captured request body keeps its tool results. A trajectory's tool message carries the captured result, with `content_truncated` when cut, and Insights shows it. Only `output` is set (not `raw_output`), so the existing per-field bound applies.
- **Refused at load:** `capture_tool_results: true` is rejected wherever the global defaults or a decision's effective settings set `capture_personal_data: false`. The error names the global section or the decision. The runtime also requires both settings, so a policy built outside loading stays redacted.
- **Unchanged:** principals without `replay.detail` still receive tool outputs, request bodies and trajectory content redacted; a new test now covers that read path. Masking routes still record no request trace or body.
- **Surfaces:** Go config and canonical defaults, the generated config schema and OpenAPI, the CLI model, the Dashboard config editors (router defaults and DSL plugin fields), the reference `config/config.yaml`, the Insights record trace, and docs (Router Replay tutorial, configuration, Router API).

Owned by #5806 and `wg/enterprise-environment`. Record size across stores is #4989's scope. The docs ask operators to set `max_tool_trace_bytes` when they enable this, because `0` stores results whole.

## Test Plan

From `src/semantic-router`:

```bash
go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configschema/ ./pkg/dsl/ ./pkg/configsnapshot/ ./pkg/routerreplay/... -count=1
go test ./pkg/extproc -run 'ToolResult|ToolTrace|Trajectory|TestBuildReplayRoutingRecord|TestReplay' -count=1
go test ./pkg/apiserver -run 'TestRouterReplayViewerRedaction|TestRouterReplayManagementRoute' -count=1
```

```bash
make config-schema-generate api-docs-generate     # no diff after regeneration
node website/scripts/generate-configuration-catalog.mjs --check
cd src/vllm-sr && python -m pytest tests/test_plugin_parsing.py -k RouterReplay
cd e2e && go test ./testcases/ ./pkg/verification/ -count=1
cd dashboard/frontend && npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test:unit
make e2e-test E2E_PROFILE=router-replay
```

The new `router-replay-tool-result-capture` E2E case sends a chat tool loop to a recipe with `capture_tool_results: true` and `max_tool_trace_bytes: 32`. It asserts that a `replay.detail` reader gets the first 32 bytes of the result, flagged `truncated`, with the full result in the request body and in the trajectory. It also asserts that a reader without `replay.detail` gets the step redacted with its status and no body, and that a recipe without the option keeps its captured body but not the result.

## Test Result

- All Go, CLI and E2E-framework commands above passed. The schema, OpenAPI and configuration-catalog generators leave no diff.
- New tests:
  - The load-time refusal covers the global conflict, a decision that inherits withheld personal data, and a decision that withholds personal data while inheriting capture.
  - Capture covers opt-in, default and withheld personal data; the byte bound and `truncated` flag go through the real recorder; trajectory mapping includes older records that stored results in `text`.
  - Viewer redaction is covered at both the redaction package and the management API.
- Dashboard: `type-check` passed, `lint` reported no errors (68 existing warnings), and `test:unit` passed 225 files / 1,168 tests, including the two new record-trace cases.
- `make e2e-test E2E_PROFILE=router-replay` on a disposable kind cluster: 14/14 passed, including `router-replay-tool-result-capture`.
- `make test-core-unit`, the Router Contracts inventory run as a non-root user so read-only-directory and Helm checks do not skip: passed.

author: volpestyle
body:
Supported joined hosts expose their own heavy-work governor through the authenticated encrypted join channel. Owner resource CLI/API operations resolve canonical joined IDs, read that host's specs/holders/queues, and configure its existing local registry. Heavy commands execute locally and continue if the home/link disappears.

`fleet_capacity` accepts `includeMachineResources: true` for a per-machine full/light/server count summary. Every entry is explicitly `source: "host-reported"`, `advisory: true`. The host's measurement time is preserved as `observedAt`; receipt time never replaces it. Each joined response must echo the current request nonce. Missing/mismatched correlation, missing time, age over five seconds or a clock over one second ahead makes the reading unavailable with no free capacity counted. The host can misreport its own numbers; admission stays with its local governor. Legacy responses retain their existing shape; holder identities remain in the owner-only resource route.

Portal, Watch, stale policy and revocation refuse resource operations. Policy writes recheck under the native registry lock, including outages during the CLI's first two seconds. Existing screen freshness timing is preserved.

This is the approved first slice of #325. macOS and native Linux use the existing POSIX governor; Windows and WSL explicitly report `unsupported-platform` without creating a join governor. No PC contact, provisioning, daemon/service restart or KH2 lock change. Offline policy remains desired policy and can be applied by setting it again online. #325 remains open for Windows/WSL shared admission, native process ownership and real competing-build crash/cancel acceptance.

Exact re-review head: `6667cb8c8b35efd3315bca360f95139ec8bac615`. The latest follow-up is one two-file commit after reviewed `3f740673ed1901ea6e9cf7a66b57398b09de32a8`; no rebase or other changes. **Independent private re-review approved; current landing status below governs the merge.**

Validation through `clankie heavy --`:

- All 77 tests in machine join, machine resources, capacity, fleet settings, joined screen and native governor history suites pass. Native integration ran on Darwin. The same test supports native Linux, but Linux was not executed on this Mac; Windows/WSL tests prove refusal with synthetic platform facts.
- Real loopback encrypted join, real local CLI admission and shared native registry: one holder plus one waiter; both jobs finish after the join observer disconnects. Capacity opt-in is exercised through actual operator-service dispatch/schema.
- New stale-report integration captures a genuinely idle host snapshot, then holds its only slot with a real job. Replaying the cached authenticated report cannot produce a free slot. It covers old nonce, expired/missing/future timestamps and expiry between adapter and capacity projection, preserving the exact host time.
- New wall-clock slow-sibling integration uses the real encrypted loopback join and native governor: capture a free slot, occupy it with a real job, delay a sibling read until the report is over six seconds old. The aggregate now checks freshness again after `Promise.all` and returns stale/unavailable, preserves the host time and exposes no full/light/server lane capacity. The reviewer’s finding reproduces on the parent; removing only the new guard kills this test. Original source restored. Historical freshness/admission mutation results remain recorded against their respective earlier heads.
- Scoped TypeScript, lint and formatting pass; deadcode, doc links and swallowed-rejection checks pass.
- New-head [quick check](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/actions/runs/41857461796) and [docs build](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/actions/runs/41857461829) are running. Merge remains held for private re-review and green checks.

[Integration regressions](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/blob/6667cb8c8b35efd3315bca360f95139ec8bac615/apps/clankie/test/machine-join.integration.test.ts), [home adapter](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/blob/6667cb8c8b35efd3315bca360f95139ec8bac615/apps/clankie/src/joined-fleet-resources.ts), [host-reported capacity projection](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/blob/6667cb8c8b35efd3315bca360f95139ec8bac615/apps/clankie/src/app/fleet-capacity.ts).

[Raw slow-sibling regression, 77-test output and guard mutation failure](clankie://evidence/sha256/9b264d70a0ad375df46d32b21abac3583c916a32192992844be2355729663edf).

Refs #325

Landing status: private re-review **APPROVE** at `6667cb8c8b35efd3315bca360f95139ec8bac615`. After #851 merged, the lead-requested rebase cleanly replayed all six approved patches onto `2e7ae5bcbc7b8a324457808b531af529a94145b9`; every range-diff entry is `=`. Pushed landing head: `6999bad4371ac2dc7fc80fb9c85c4e13addbbf76`. All 77 scoped tests, scoped TypeScript, lint/format, deadcode, documentation links and swallowed-rejection checks pass on the rebased head. Marked ready. Current-head [quick check](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/actions/runs/41878238582) and [docs build](https://github.com/Volpestyle/clankie/actions/runs/41878238527) are queued; merge awaits green. No further rebase planned.

author: romancg13
body:
## ⚠️ À lire avant de fusionner

**Une recompilation native EAS (iOS + Android) puis un test sur appareil réel restent OBLIGATOIRES.** Cette PR change React Native (0.86 → 0.88) et la plupart des modules natifs : rien de natif n'a pu être compilé ici (ni Xcode, ni CocoaPods, ni JDK sur le poste). Aucune build EAS ni soumission store n'a été lancée. Ne pas fusionner, ne pas publier de mise à jour OTA vers les binaires SDK 57 existants : le runtime natif change.

Le site web n'est pas concerné : ni `package.json` / `package-lock.json` racine, ni `src/`, ni `packages/core`, ni aucun fichier de `tests/paiements-geles.json` ne sont modifiés.

## Ce qui change

Deux commits :

1. **`caec04c` — montée Expo SDK 57 → 58** via `npx expo install expo@~58.0.23 --fix` puis `--check` (« Dependencies are up to date »).
   - expo 58.0.23 · react-native **0.88.1** · react / react-dom **19.3.0** · expo-router 58.0.30 · react-native-gesture-handler **3.3** (majeure) · reanimated 4.7.1 · worklets 0.13.0 · screens 4.30.1 · safe-area-context 5.11.1 · svg 15.16 · babel-preset-expo 58 · @types/react 19.3, plus tous les `expo-*` en ~58.
   - Verrou : entrées périmées `expo-symbols` / `@expo/ui` retirées. En SDK 57 c'étaient des dépendances directes d'expo-router, en 58 ce sont des peers optionnels, d'où l'ERESOLVE de `--fix`.
   - `node-forge` 1.4.2 et `shell-quote` 1.12.0 repris **à l'identique de la PR #52**. node-forge 1.4.3 (publiée ce matin) est écartée, comme dans #52.
   - Code : **typage seul, aucun changement de comportement** (RN 0.88 livre l'API TypeScript stricte par défaut) — `app/onboarding.tsx` (`ScrollViewInstance`), `src/ui/Input.tsx` (`TextInputInstance`), `src/lib/supabase.ts` (`AppState.currentState` typé `string | null | undefined`).
2. **`d5f5fe2` — `overrides` npm glob ^14.0.2 / minimatch ^11.0.1**, limités à `@expo/cli` et `@expo/fingerprint` (voir plus bas), et mise à jour des versions dans `CLAUDE.md` et `docs/mobile-architecture.md`.

## Alertes Dependabot

| Alerte | Avis | Avant (SDK 57) | Après | Levée par |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #21 / #28 decode-uri-component | GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr, GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f | via query-string 7 ← expo-router 57 (**livré dans l'app**) | absent de l'arbre | SDK 58 |
| #26 zod | GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 | outillage Expo CLI | absent / corrigé | SDK 58 |
| #20 uuid | GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq | outillage prebuild | corrigé | SDK 58 |
| — deepmerge (npm audit seul) | GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 | outillage | corrigé | SDK 58 |
| #40 glob | GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 | 13.0.6 | 14.0.3 | **override** |
| #41 minimatch | GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 | 10.2.6 | 11.0.4 | **override** |

`npm audit` dans `mobile/` : **23 vulnérabilités avant → 0 après**.

### Pourquoi un override pour glob / minimatch

Le SDK 58 ne suffit pas pour ces deux-là : `@expo/cli` 58.1.19 (`latest`, `next` et `canary`) et `@expo/fingerprint` 0.21.9 déclarent toujours `glob ^13` / `minimatch ^10`. Les correctifs n'existent que dans les nouvelles majeures (glob 14.0.2+, minimatch 11.0.1+, publiées le 2026-10-27/28, sans rétroportage). Ces paquets ne servent qu'à l'outillage (CLI, prebuild, empreinte) ; rien n'est livré dans l'app.

L'équivalence a été vérifiée **avant / après l'override**, avec les motifs et options exacts du CLI :
- mêmes fichiers de routes (`**/*.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx)`, `+api`, `+middleware`) ;
- même liste de fichiers renommés par prebuild sur le vrai gabarit `expo-template-bare-minimum@sdk-58` ;
- même découverte des `.gitignore` ;
- **même empreinte `@expo/fingerprint`** (`d7ab508a…`) ;
- **bundles iOS / Android identiques à l'octet près** (mêmes hash `e93e87eb…` / `6724d509…`).

Le commit est isolé : un `git revert d5f5fe2` suffit pour retirer l'override. **À retirer** dès qu'`expo` dépend lui-même de ces versions (condition consignée dans `docs/mobile-architecture.md`).

## Revue des ruptures SDK 58 → impact sur l'app

Sources : https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-58 et les CHANGELOG livrés dans chaque paquet (entrées « Breaking changes » entre l'ancienne et la nouvelle version).

| Rupture | Paquet | Impact ClairDossier | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| API TypeScript stricte : refs typées `*Instance`, imports profonds `react-native/Libraries/*` interdits | react-native 0.87/0.88 | 3 erreurs de types | corrigé (types seuls) ; aucun import profond |
| Retraits : `InteractionManager`, `Touchable`, `Modal animated`, props `StatusBar` `backgroundColor` / `translucent` ; `ImageBackground` déprécié | react-native | non utilisés (`StatusBar` d'expo-status-bar avec `style` seul) | aucune |
| Cœur de navigation retravaillé, API React Navigation forkée réduite, `withLayoutContext` déprécié | expo-router 58 | l'app n'utilise que `Stack`, `Tabs`, `Redirect`, `useRouter`, `useLocalSearchParams` ; aucun import `@react-navigation` | aucune — **à tester sur appareil** (onglets, piles, retour, liens profonds) |
| `web.output` par défaut = `server` | expo-router | `web.output: 'single'` déjà explicite | aucune |
| `@expo/ui` / `expo-symbols` deviennent peers optionnels | expo-router | non utilisés | verrou nettoyé |
| `Linking.parse()` ne décode plus deux fois les valeurs de **query** | expo-linking | l'app ne lit que `path` (diff 57/58 : `path` inchangé) | aucune |
| Notifications au premier plan affichées par défaut | expo-notifications | `setNotificationHandler` explicite déjà présent | aucune |
| `File.write()` et `FileHandle.readBytes` / `writeBytes` deviennent asynchrones ; `File.md5` déprécié | expo-file-system | seul `File#createUploadTask` est utilisé (inchangé) | aucune |
| `selectedLens` basé sur `deviceType` | expo-camera | non utilisé | aucune |
| `getLoadedFonts()` | expo-font | non utilisé | aucune |
| expo-secure-store | — | aucune rupture listée | aucune |
| Nouvelle majeure v3 | react-native-gesture-handler | seul `GestureHandlerRootView` est utilisé (toujours exporté) | aucune — **à tester sur appareil** |
| reanimated 4.7 / worklets 0.13 | — | pas d'import direct ; `react-native-worklets/plugin` toujours présent | aucune |
| Cycle de vie UIKit par scènes (SDK iOS 27) ; `requireFullScreen` n'empêche plus le redimensionnement | iOS | CNG (pas de `ios/` versionné) : prebuild génère `SceneDelegate.swift` + `UIApplicationSceneManifest` | aucune — **vérifier la mise en page iPad redimensionnée** |
| R8 activé en release (`android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds=true`) | Android | indicateur déjà présent dans le prebuild SDK 57 de `main` | **tester une build release Android** |
| Safe areas (iPhone Duo, insets horizontaux) | safe-area-context 5.11 | `useSafeAreaInsets` partout | à vérifier sur appareil |
| Node 22.13+ / 24.3+ requis pour l'outillage | — | local 24.19 ; EAS utilise l'image par défaut | aucune |
| Expo Go ne prend en charge que SDK 58 ; nouvelle development build nécessaire | — | — | **refaire le profil `development` EAS** |

## Vérifications (sorties réelles)

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` (mobile/) + `npm ls --all` | OK, code de sortie 0 |
| `npm audit` (mobile/) | **found 0 vulnerabilities** (23 avant) |
| `npm run typecheck` (mobile/) | OK |
| `npm test` (mobile/) | 6/6 |
| `npx expo install --check` | Dependencies are up to date |
| `npx expo-doctor@latest` | **20/20** |
| `npx expo export` iOS / Android (hors ligne, `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` factices) | bundles produits, 5,5 Mo chacun (5,2 / 5,4 Mo en SDK 57) |
| Source map iOS (2 076 sources) | aucune source de decode-uri-component, query-string, zod, uuid, glob, minimatch, deepmerge, node-forge, shell-quote |
| `npx expo prebuild` (copie jetable, SDK 58 vs SDK 57 de `main`) | OK ; permissions Android, `gradle.properties` et `Podfile.properties.json` identiques ; iOS : seuls les identifiants aléatoires du `project.pbxproj` diffèrent ; cible iOS 16.4 = minimum requis par les pods SDK 58 |
| `node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` (racine) | **166/166**, dont `paiements-geles` 2/2 |
| Fichiers de `tests/paiements-geles.json` modifiés | aucun |

**Non vérifié ici :** compilation native (Xcode / Gradle), `

body:
Refs #7

Ajout de la partie contre deux IA, arbitrée par le serveur, avec sauvegarde, reprise et minuteur de tour.

Backend : moteur du jeu en Java pur (règles, commerce, conflits, score, IA, défausse aléatoire à l'expiration du minuteur), API `/api/games/sdv-civilisation/*`, partie gardée en session pour un invité et dans `game_saves` (scellée AES-GCM) pour un compte, score enregistré dans `scores`. Développé en TDD (commits `[TDD rouge]` / `[TDD vert]`), avec tests unitaires, d'intégration (Spring + MockMvc, Supabase simulé) et de contrat ; stubs, mocks, fakes, spies et dummies.

body:
## Description

`requirements.txt` pins `pillow==13.0.0`, which requires Python >= 3.11. The `Python 3.10` job therefore fails on `master` (`No matching distribution found for pillow==13.0.0`), and with `fail-fast` it cancels the 3.11-3.13 jobs. This blocks every PR, including #74.

This PR raises the minimum Python version to 3.11.

### Changes
- `pyproject.toml`: `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, removed the 3.10 classifier
- `.github/workflows/python-package.yml`: removed 3.10 from the test matrix, pre-commit job uses `>=3.11`
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: matrix is now 3.11 and 3.12, Codecov upload moved to 3.11
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: PyInstaller build uses Python 3.11
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under "In Development"

### Not changed
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (`--py310-plus`, `--target-version=py310`, `--py-version=3.10`) is left alone to avoid conflicts with #74. It can follow later.

### Required manual step
The ruleset on `master` requires the status check `Python 3.10`. That job no longer exists, so the check must be changed to `Python 3.11` in the repository settings before PRs can merge.

### Testing
Not run locally (no working copy). Only the CI of this PR applies, and its `Python 3.10` check will stay missing.

author: thesocialdev
body:
# Release v1.8.1

Ships `stage` at `dd7e85d2`. Production runs v1.8.0 (`7d4f4ab8`), with no hotfixes since.

> [!NOTE]
> When this PR opened, Aletheia CI, CodeQL and the staging deploy for `dd7e85d2` (#2701) were still in progress. Confirm that they passed before you merge.

## 🎯 Major Product Enhancements

**Admin Claim Editor: Debates and Sentence Deletion**
Product Areas: Claims, Debates, Admin
- [x] feat(admin-editor): admins can edit sentences in **debates**. Each approved speech on the debate page has a pencil that opens the editor on that speech (`&speechId=`). A debate is edited **in place**: it keeps its id, revision and speeches. Each edited sentence becomes a new `Sentence` doc, swapped into its paragraph with one atomic `$set`, and the approved transcript turn text is updated to match. Debate metadata (title and date) cannot be edited (400 `content-type-not-supported`) (#2701)
- [x] feat(admin-editor): new `delete` sentence op for speeches and debates. A paragraph left empty is removed. The server refuses a sentence with a **published** review (`sentence-has-review`) and a speech that would have no sentences (`speech-would-be-empty`). A review task in progress does not block deletion; the editor asks for confirmation first (#2701)

---

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- [x] fix(admin-editor): in-progress review tasks no longer lose their sentence after an edit. The ReviewTask cascade filtered on `onModel` (never stored) and compared the string `target` with an ObjectId, so it matched no task. The new `targetIdFilter` (`server/common/target-id-filter.ts`) matches both forms, for ReviewTask, ClaimReview and Report (#2701)
- [x] fix(admin-editor): published reports keep their link after an edit. `Report.data_hash` is now remapped, only for the reports of this claim's ClaimReviews (#2701)
- [x] fix(admin-editor): a stale debate view now returns **409** (conflict dialog) instead of 400, and the editor shows translated messages (pt/en) by `errorCode` instead of `[object Object]`. Server messages no longer include sentence ids (#2701)
- [x] fix(mcp): review tasks for debate sentences now use the **speaker's** personality, not the debate's first personality. This affected `start_review_task` and the queue feed (`enqueueClaimSentences`), so the Kanban showed the wrong person. Speech claims behave as before (#2704)

---

## 🔒 Security & Infrastructure

**Deploy Gated on CI**
- [x] ci(deploy): `aws.yml` is now a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`). `nodejs.yml` runs on pushes to `master` and `ufpb-labcheck` too, and ends with a `deploy` job that `needs` every check. A red build no longer deploys (#2702)

After this release, `stage` and `master` have the same file content.

---

## ⚠️ Deploy Notes

- **This deploy is the first gated one on `master` (#2702).** The push of this merge runs the new `nodejs.yml` from `master`, so the production deploy starts only after the full CI passes, about 10 to 17 min after the merge. There is no separate "Deploy to AWS EKS" push run any more: the deploy is the `deploy` job of the **Aletheia CI** run. If a flaky check fails, rerun the failed jobs to resume the deploy. `ufpb-labcheck` stays ungated until this change reaches it.
- **No migrations** in this release (Mongo or Postgres).
- **Sentences edited before #2701** still have their review task or report on the old hash. No migration reconnects them. The `sentenceDiff` hash pairs in the history entries (`kind: "admin-claim-edit"`) could do it later.
- **Open debate tasks created through the MCP before #2704** still show the wrong personality. None was published. To fix one, open the sentence from the debate page and save (draft auto-save or any action).
- **Not tested:** editing a debate while a live transcriber appends turns. Avoid admin edits on a debate that is being transcribed live.
- **Node disk space:** if the larger node volume (≥ 50 GiB) from the v1.7.1 notes is still not in place, before you merge:
  - Check the node conditions: `kubectl describe nodes | grep -A1 DiskPressure`.
  - Remove the old evicted pods: `kubectl delete pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Failed`.
- **Purge Cloudflare after the deploy**, so that cached HTML does not point to old chunks:
  `NODENV_VERSION=22.14.0 cf cache purge -z d18ad38c1d402090a9d26eb19cd09d4a --body '{"hosts":["aletheiafact.org","www.aletheiafact.org"]}' --force`

## ✅ Post-deploy checks

- The **Aletheia CI** run for the merge commit on `master` passes and its `deploy` job ran.
- `kubectl get deploy aletheia -n production` shows `2/2` ready.
- As an admin, open a debate: each approved speech shows a pencil. Edit a sentence and save: the debate keeps its URL, and the sentence's report and classification stay.
- In the editor, the delete button is disabled (with a tooltip) for a sentence that has a published review.
- Logged out or as a regular user, the debate page shows no pencil.

author: zakyirsyaad
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 (foundations) of the main window redesign: a new font, a type scale, and the UI primitives the later phases build on. The only change users can see in the app is the font, and notices now showing as a toast.

**Font and type**
- The interface uses the Mac's system font (SF Pro). Code, commands and paths stay in Geist Mono. Instrument Sans is gone from the app: the package, its import and its preload in `src/lib/fonts.ts`.
- New type scale in `globals.css` and `tokens.json`:

  | Token | Size / line height |
  |---|---|
  | `ui` | 13/18 |
  | `ui-sm` | 12/16 |
  | `caption` | 11/16 |
  | `body` | 14/22 |
  | `micro` | 10/14 |

  `design-system-docs.test.ts` now fails if the two files drift on the font stack or the scale, or if Instrument Sans comes back into `src/`.

**New primitives in `src/components/ui/`**, each with a README and preview under `docs/design-system/components/`:
- `StatusLine`: a status in words with its colored dot. Only `running` pulses, and only when motion is allowed.
- `Chip`: a 24px chip for the top bar, plain or outline. It is a real `<button>` only when it has `onClick`.
- `Tabs`: a tab strip for the inspector, with roving tabindex, wrapping arrow keys, Home and End, and a count shown only above zero.
- `Popover`, `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverOption`: the one popover style. It closes on Escape or a click outside, and gives focus back to the trigger when it closes while focus was inside it. An option's role follows the panel: `menuitem` in a menu, `option` with `aria-selected` in a listbox.
- `Toast`, `ToastStack`: a 340px card, `role="alert"` for errors and `role="status"` otherwise, with one optional action and Dismiss.

**Notices become toasts.** `App.tsx` renders `setNotice` messages as an error toast at the bottom right of the chat area, instead of `NoticeBanner` across the top. The toast is anchored at the composer's top edge, so it never covers Send or Stop. `NoticeBanner` is removed.

This branch also carries the two redesign specs and the phase 1 plan (`docs/superpowers/`), since `docs/redesign-specs` was never pushed separately.

## Notes for the reviewer

- Every notice is shown as `tone="error"`. That matches the old danger banner and keeps `role="alert"`, which about 15 App tests rely on. Three notices are really guidance (no folder, no agent, a dropped file with control characters). `setNotice` should get a tone in a later phase.
- `notice-banners.test.tsx` now pairs `UpdateNotice` with `FailedTurnBanner`, the other danger banner on `NOTICE_BANNER_LAYOUT`, because `NoticeBanner` is gone.
- A whole-branch review found one important issue: the toast covered Send/Stop. It is fixed in `fix: keep the notice toast above the message box`, with a test. Minor follow-ups left for later phases:
  - A `Chip` `label` without `onClick` is not read by screen readers.
  - Warning and info toasts need a pre-mounted live region to be announced.
  - `PopoverHeader` needs a role.
  - The toast's 10px radius has no token.
  - `docs/design-system/adopting.md` still names Instrument Sans.
- Nothing under `src-tauri/` changed, so cargo was not run.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm test` (179 files, 2656 tests)
- [ ] `cd src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test` (no Rust changes)
- [ ] Tried it in `pnpm tauri dev`. Not done yet: check SF Pro, that long session titles and paths still truncate, and that a notice shows above the message box and dismisses.
- [x] Added a line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` (if users would notice)

The design-system cards (Popover, Tabs, Toast, StatusLine, Chip) were checked in a browser with `pnpm design-system`, in both themes.

author: albermonte
body:
Nimiq Pay replaces a user's HTLC, which gives it a new address, but `NimiqProvider` caches `listAccounts()` in a private field that only `disconnect()` can reset. Mini Apps keep the old address and `getBalance` on it reads 0.

`updateAccounts(accounts)` lets the host replace that list. It emits `accountsChanged`, keeps the connection and does not emit `disconnect`. A provider that never listed accounts stays unconnected.

The host side is in nimiq/nimiq-pay-app, which pins this commit. Mini App docs for the behavior are in #7.

Refs APP-348

author: niyaznigmatullin
body: Stacked on #53. The second half of the stress methods the docs added on 2026-10-12. #53 made stresses readable and editable. These start and cancel their runs and turn a countertest a run found into a test, so a stress can be driven through the wrapper from start to end. New in `polygon_api`: * `Polygon.problem_run_stresses(problem_id, stress_indices=None, pin=None)` and the `Problem.run_stresses(stress_indices=None, pin=None)` shortcut. It starts the stresses and returns at once: `problem.stresses` shows their runs. * `Polygon.problem_cancel_stresses(problem_id, stress_indices=None, pin=None)` and the `Problem.cancel_stresses(stress_indices=None, pin=None)` shortcut. * `Polygon.problem_add_stress_countertest(problem_id, stress_index, testset, pin=None)` and the `Problem.add_stress_countertest(stress_index, testset, pin=None)` shortcut, returning the added test. ```python problem.run_stresses([stress.index]) while (run := problem.stresses(stress.index)[0].run).status != StressRunStatus.FINISHED: time.sleep(5) if run.countertest is not None: test = problem.add_stress_countertest(stress.index, 'tests') ``` Both `runStresses` and `cancelStresses` act on every stress of the problem without `stress_indices`. The indices take a list or a comma-separated string, like `test_indices` of `problem.deleteTest`. `problem.addStressCountertest` returns a Test object, so the result goes through `Test.from_json` as the results of `problem.tests` do. That gives a `GeneratedTest`, or a `ManualTest` when Polygon stores a small generated input as a manual test, as the docs say it may. The test keeps the testset and the pin it was added with, so a later `save` sends the same pin. The docstrings carry what the docs say about each call: `runStresses` doesn't restart a PENDING or RUNNING stress, and `cancelStresses` leaves the finished results of stresses that aren't running. Tests: the request contents of all three methods and their shortcuts, with and without indices, as a list and as a string; a generated and a manual added test, and the pin kept on it; the pin rows; and four tests through the local API server: indices sent comma-separated, the FAILED answer of a user locked because of the load on invokers, cancelling every stress, and the added test parsed. `flake8` clean, `pytest -q`: 1093 passed. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

author: codenameakshay
body: ## What this does Day and night lets a Pro user pick a day wall and a night wall. The wallpaper changes at two times, 07:00 and 19:00 by default. - **iOS 16 or later: ships.** The Shortcuts action "Get Prism Wallpaper" has a new source, "Day and night". It returns the wall that matches the current local time. Its new "Time" option (Now, Day, Night) lets a Sunrise or Sunset automation force one wall. A guide sheet builds the two Time of Day automations. - **Android: blocked on the plugin.** `async_wallpaper` 3.6.0 cannot change the wallpaper at two times of day. Every Day and night entry point is hidden on Android. What the plugin needs is below. A plugin release needs your OK. ## How a user gets there - Hold any wall (grid or wallpaper card). Tap the new round "Day and night" action. A sheet offers "Use as day wall" and "Use as night wall". A wall with colour variants also gets "Use the lightest and darkest variant", which picks by the luminance of each variant's main colour. - Settings, PERSONALISE, "Day and night" (iOS 16 or later). - The screen shows both walls in phone previews, the two start times, Apply to (home, lock, both) and the switch. The hold menu is a ring with 6 positions, so Day and night is one action that opens a sheet. The Set screen "More" menu is Android only, so it has no item. ## Design | Piece | Choice | |---|---| | Domain | `DayNightPair` (day wall, night wall, `DayNightTimes`, target, enabled, fromVariants). `DayNightTimes.tryCreate` refuses equal times, so every minute belongs to one slot. | | Time maths | Local wall clock, minutes after midnight. Day runs from the day start up to the night start and wraps past midnight. Dart (`DayNightTimes.slotAt`) and Swift (`PrismDayNight.slot(at:)`) use the same rule and are tested minute by minute, across midnight, DST gaps, repeated hours and time zone changes. | | Storage | One JSON value at `dayNight.pair` in the settings box with the owner id, like auto-rotate. | | Offline | Turning it on copies both walls with `OfflineAssetStore` (or uses the user's own downloaded original for a protected wall), registers them in the `daynight` native asset group, then writes `shortcuts.day_night`. The action reads only these local copies, so it works with the app closed and offline. | | Pro | Same gate as auto-rotate (`autoRotateEntitled`). Same lapse rule: off at app start, one toast, none on sign-out or account switch. | | Navigation | An in-app page (`openDayNightScreen`), like the taste quiz. A routed path must also be on the Cloudflare worker and AASA allowlists, which is an infra change. | ## Android: what the plugin needs Android does not ship in this PR. async_wallpaper 3.6.0 cannot switch at two times of day, so Day and night is hidden on Android. What 3.6.0 has, read from the pub cache source: | API | What it does | Why it does not fit | |---|---|---| | `WallpaperRotationTrigger.timeOfDay` | `WallpaperRotationScheduler.scheduleTimeOfDay` arms one inexact `setAndAllowWhileIdle` alarm at `activeHoursStart:00`. `WallpaperTimeOfDayReceiver` re-arms it each day. | One alarm a day, and only on the hour. Day and night needs two times, with minutes. | | `WallpaperRotationTrigger.interval` | WorkManager periodic work. The first run waits one interval. | Not tied to the clock. A 720 minute interval drifts after Doze and restarts its count at each reboot (`REASON_BOOT` enqueues it again from boot time). | | `runNext` (every trigger) | Moves a playlist cursor to the next source. | Not time aware. One missed or failed run swaps day and night until the next run. | | `WallpaperBootReceiver` | On boot and on a clock change it reschedules triggers. | It does not apply a wallpaper, so the wrong wall stays until the next trigger. | What the plugin needs, as one new API next to rotation: 1. `startDailySchedule(DailyScheduleRequest)` with a list of entries `{minuteOfDay, source}` (two for Day and night), a `target`, and the same URL and file sources as rotation. It caches every source at start, like rotation does. 2. One inexact `setAndAllowWhileIdle` alarm armed for the next entry. No `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`. Doze can delay it by some minutes; Prism shows "around 07:00". 3. Each delivery applies the entry that owns the current local time (not a cursor), then arms the next entry. Day runs from its start up to the next entry, wrapping past midnight. 4. `BOOT_COMPLETED`, `TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED` and `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` apply the current entry and re-arm the alarm. This also closes PERS-1 and PERS-2 for this mode. 5. `applyCurrentScheduleEntry()` for Dart to call when the app opens. 6. One schedule at a time: starting a daily schedule stops rotation, and starting rotation stops the schedule. Status reports which one runs, the current entry, and the next switch time. 7. Kotlin unit tests for the next-alarm and current-entry math around midnight and on DST change days. The Dart side then needs: an `AutoRotateMode` (playlist or day and night) so only one runs, the confirm before one turns the other off, the call on app open, and the `day_night_switched` event for the app-open apply. A plugin release needs your OK. ## Analytics `day_night_enabled` (`target`, `from_variants`), `day_night_disabled`, `day_night_ios_guide_opened`. `make analytics-gen` ran. There is no `day_night_switched` event: on iOS Shortcuts sets the wallpaper and Prism cannot see it, and Android has no switch yet. ## Copy All strings are in the ARB files for the 7 locales. The guide uses each locale's real Shortcuts names (the same names as the existing Shortcuts guide). The new Swift strings ("Day and night", "Time", "Now", "Day", "Night", the summary, 2 errors) are in `Localizable.xcstrings` for all 6 iOS locales. ## Review Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`, high) reviewed the branch before the proof. Boat returned 403, so it ran locally. It fixed: - The action could fetch a wall from the network or return stale bytes after the snapshot changed. It now reads only the published offline copies and cancels on a session change. - A late publish could overwrite a newer edit or outlive a turn-off or account switch. Snapshot writes now share the native path queue. - Sign-out or account deletion that ran late could erase another account's snapshot. - A failed startup refresh left the switch on; a save failure after publish left a live snapshot. - "Open wall" went back instead of opening the wall; iOS 16 got iOS 17 automation steps. It found no time-maths defect. Each fix has a test. ## Proof iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27), build of `test/qa_render/day_night_device_main.dart` at 8e4f7f6c9, after the Codex fixes. Later commits changed only how the screen opens: a fake signed-in Pro user, a real pair published through the real repository. The action runs are the real "Get Prism Wallpaper" intent in the Shortcuts app. | Shortcuts action, Time = Day | Shortcuts action, Time = Night | Guide sheet | |---|---|---| | | | | | Screen, light | Screen, dark | Largest accessibility text | |---|---|---| | | | | The phone previews are a picture of the lock screen, so their clock does not scale with text size. Everything else wraps. Not covered: An

body:
A question an agent asks with Claude's AskUserQuestion reached the Inbox as an **Approval** titled "AskUserQuestion", asking "Use AskUserQuestion?" and blaming the permission mode. The toast said "AskUserQuestion · Approval" with a green tick.

## Changes
- **API** (`inbox::approvals`): an open request of kind `question` is now grouped as `question` and titled with its first question's text. It is still kind `approval`, so it is still answered in its session as before.
- **Notifications** (`NotificationKind::of_inbox`): an approval in the question group notifies as `inbox.question`, so the toast says "Question · PM".
- **Toast**: question notifications show a "?" icon instead of the success tick. This adds an `icon` option to `toast` in `@ui`.
- **Web Inbox**: the new `shownKind` helper makes these items read as a question: the question icon and label in the list and on the kind chip. The item's region is "Question", its card is titled "A question for you" (the same as the conversation), and the why line reads "<persona> asks you in its conversation; the answer goes back to it."
- Updated the user docs (the Inbox's Questions section), the developer docs (architecture) and the changelog.

## Checks
- New assertion in `conversations::questions_take_answers_and_interrupt_expires_open_requests`: the Inbox item has group `question` and title "Which one?". It failed before the fix.
- `of_inbox` unit test for (Approval, Question) → InboxQuestion.

author: hamza0476
body:
## Phase 1 — Security & tenancy hardening

Implements the Phase 1 plan from `docs/DECISIONS.md` / the master plan (findings S1–S10, S7, G-item migrations). Each change was built and tested one at a time before the next.

### Changes
- **P1-1 Migrations:** versioned Drizzle baseline (`drizzle/0000_baseline.sql`), `db:generate` / `db:migrate` / `db:push` scripts, README now teaches migrate-first. Verified: migrated vs pushed schemas identical (50 columns, 14 constraints) on a fresh Postgres.
- **P1-2 Hashed tokens (S1):** session + verification tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; the raw token lives only in the cookie / emailed link. Deploying invalidates existing sessions and outstanding email links once (pre-launch, acceptable).
- **P1-3 Headers + CSRF (S2/S3):** HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Permissions-Policy, and CSP in **Report-Only** mode (learn first, enforce later). All mutating `/api/*` calls get an Origin check in the proxy (compared against the Host header — `nextUrl` normalises 127.0.0.1 to localhost).
- **P1-4 Rate limiting v2 (S4):** Upstash Redis REST backend when `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN` are set (shared across instances), in-memory fallback + failover on Redis errors. `x-forwarded-for`/`x-real-ip` are **no longer trusted by default** (spoofable); `cf-connecting-ip` and `x-vercel-forwarded-for` are trusted (platform-set), generic proxy headers only with `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=1`.
- **P1-5 Demo abuse limits (S7):** max 5 demo-workspace creations/hour per connection (429 after), demo sessions live 1 day instead of 30.
- **P1-6 Password policy (S10):** new passwords (register + reset) need 10–128 chars and must not appear in the Have I Been Pwned corpus (k-anonymity — only a 5-char SHA-1 prefix leaves the server; fails open if HIBP is down). Login is not policy-gated, so existing passwords keep working.
- **P1-7 Tenant guard:** new `requireMembership()` seam in `src/lib/tenancy.ts`; products / categories / workspace routes refactored onto it (behaviour unchanged). This is where the future memberships table plugs in.
- **P1-8 Prefetch-safe verification (S9):** the emailed verify link no longer consumes the token on GET (mail scanners prefetch links). GET redirects to a new `/verify-email` confirmation page; only the button's POST consumes the token. Reset links already used a POST form.

### Tests
- **30 unit tests** (Vitest) — all passing locally and in CI.
- **55 integration checks** across 4 HTTP suites (`tests/integration/`, run via `tests/integration/run.sh <suite>` against a fresh migrated Postgres): auth token lifecycle incl. DB-leak resistance (21), demo limits (8), tenant isolation between two owners (14), prefetch-safe verify flow (12) — all passing.
- Live spot checks: rotating spoofed `x-forwarded-for` values no longer reset the register limit (7th attempt = 429); `password12345` is rejected live by the HIBP check; security headers present on responses.
- Integration suites are not wired into CI yet (needs a Postgres service in the workflow — a follow-up).

### Notes
- No new dependencies; `package-lock.json` unchanged.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` still lists the owner-only steps (Upstash account + env vars) needed to switch rate limiting to Redis in production.
- Lint remains non-blocking with the Phase 0 baseline (21 pre-existing errors); this PR adds none knowingly — CI will confirm.

author: iscasasola
body:
Builds the Setnayan-specs DECISION_LOG row dated **2026-11-04, "A GUEST WHO PASSED AWAY: THE CARD SHOWS ONLY WHAT STILL APPLIES"**, plus the double line the owner saw under Access.

> *"if passed away, there are parts in the guest card that doesn't need to show. Additional Guest, RSVP, Photos, Seat Plan, Note, Access and QR"* · *"i see a double line in between access and not counted for"*

⛔ **Draft · `do-not-auto-merge` · auto-merge not armed. Do not merge until the owner OKs the screenshots.**

## What changed

Edits to the shipped card (`guest-card-body.tsx`). Nothing redrawn.

**1 · A guest who passed away** (`guest.passed_away === true`, never the couple):
- **Not drawn:** Additional Guests · RSVP Status · Papic / Photos · Seat Plan · Note for them · Private note · Access (with its Account row and the Give / Take back seat doors) · the top ticket / QR with its "Their ticket" label, Invite and ⋯ (Write to NFC · New QR).
- **Still drawn:** the name, the status line ("✓ Linked · Not sent · passed away"), Basic Info, Details, the **Passed Away** switch (so it can be switched off) and Delete.
- **Nothing is cleared.** The task asked me to check how `updateGuest` treats fields missing from the posted form. The `writes()` helper does **not** protect them. The autosave sends each save with the card it last *sent* (`base`), and `guestCardMerge` counts a field that was in the base but is missing now as *changed*. So simply not drawing the folds would have made the next save, including the tap that switches Passed Away off, write RSVP → "No reply", and clear meal, dietary, both notes and photo consent / blur / face-recognition. The fix: `AwayCarriers` posts the hidden parts' exact names and values as hidden inputs, so the card posts **the same form either way**. The golden `the-card-posts-the-same-form` (its state 03 is a passed-away guest) is **unchanged**. Not carried: the Table, which was never drawn for a guest who passed away and `updateGuest` already refuses to seat them; and Papic's camera, which saves through its own action, not the form.
- **Switching off brings every part back:** `updateGuest` revalidates the guest pages before its quiet return (`revalidatePath(backTo)` before `if (quiet) return`), so the card redraws with every fold. The guard also renders that redraw and checks the next save writes nothing.

**2 · The double line.** The "Not counted for ▾" box started with its hidden `not_counted_posted` input, so the Form row inside was not the box's first child. Its own top rule (`first:border-t-0`) stayed on, under Access's bottom rule: two hairlines. Fix: the marker now comes *after* the row. The same check found one more: on the **Maker's** cards (no Delete handed in), Passed Away's bottom rule touched the card's own bottom rule. It now draws only when a group follows it. Passed Away and Delete seams checked in light and dark: one line each.

**Lab:** `/dev/guests-lab?part=card&away=1` shows a guest who passed away. Dev-only; the route 404s in production.

## Guard: `a-guest-who-passed-away-shows-only-what-applies.test.ts`

Renders the real card (the shipped kit, Invite, ticket, ⋯ and Delete):
- **(a)** passed away → the seven parts are absent; Basic Info, Details, Passed Away and Delete are present; the status line still reads "Not sent · passed away". The Maker's plain ticket image goes too.
- **(b)** not passed away → all of them are present. The couple has no Passed Away and keeps every part.
- **(c)** hiding clears nothing, measured with the save's own `guestCardMerge` / `guestColumnWritten`, both ways: switched on, then a save with parts hidden; and switched off, then the redrawn card's save. **No guest column is written.** Only the marker-gated Table and Not-counted fields may differ, and their markers are absent. A third test makes sure (c) can fail: the fixture really posts the values, and a dropped field IS caught.
- **(d)** no two hairlines touch. This checks a property of the drawn tree, not a class string: which element draws a top or bottom rule, with `first:` / `last:` applied the way CSS applies them (a hidden input counts as a child), shut folds unseen, and `dark:` rules only in dark. Run over eight states (every part, nothing booked, passed away, RSVP open by itself, no account, the couple, the Maker's card, the Maker's card passed away) in light and dark. Anti-vacuity cases are included.

**Red on the old file → green on the fix.** Sabotage, each seen red and then restored:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| old `guest-card-body.tsx` (origin/main) | **11 red**: (a) + eight (d) seam states (Access ⟂ Not counted; Passed Away ⟂ card bottom on the Maker's card) |
| parts hidden, nothing carried | both (c) red |
| one carrier dropped (`notes`) | both (c) red |
| Not-counted marker moved back above its row | eight (d) states red |
| Passed Away's rule kept with no Delete under it | the four Maker (d) states red |
| **the fix** | **23/23 green** |

(c) is green on the old file because nothing was hidden there. It exists to catch a hide that clears values, and both of those sabotage runs went red.

## Screenshots: `/dev/guests-lab?part=card&linked=1&counted=none`, 390 px, dummy data

Committed on this branch in **`build-sessions/assets/passed-away-card/`** (open a file in the PR's *Files changed* tab to see it; this tool can't embed images in the body):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a normal guest | `before-normal-light.png` | `after-normal-light.png` |
| a guest who passed away | `before-away-light.png` | `after-away-light.png` |
| Access → Not counted → Passed Away → Delete (light) | `before-normal-seam-light.png` (two lines under Access) | `after-normal-seam-light.png` (one) |
| the same seam (dark) | `before-normal-seam-dark.png` | `after-normal-seam-dark.png` |
| passed away: Details → Passed Away → Delete (dark) | — | `after-away-seam-dark.png` |

The dev server's "Issues" badge and the lab's stand-in dock are hidden in the shots. "Not counted for" wrapping to three lines is the lab's inset frame (`ml-12`) at 390 px. That is how it is on main too, and this PR leaves it alone.

## Checks run here

- the new guard: 23/23 · the 589 tests of the guest list, the guests-lab and the lib tests that render the card: all pass
- full `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0
- no migration, no baseline touched, no email, nothing in production; dummy env only

## Preflight
