body:
## P2 · Creative intelligence: all 22 skills drive private orchestration

`/api/agent` now runs every creative turn through one server-only pipeline (`lib/orchestrator.ts`):

1. Strict input schema (`lib/creative-plan.ts`): text, preference, task, visual style, character reference (id, version, provided angles) and audio flags.
2. Lexical safety preflight. A non-allow result returns 422 with the existing shape, and no planner is called.
3. `preparePrivateCreativeRequest` compiles the active skills from the full registry of 22 (`SKILL_REGISTRY_VERSION=1.1.0`).
4. Planner selection:
   - The default is the deterministic planner (pure, no network).
   - The Claude adapter (`lib/llm-anthropic.ts`, structured output via `zodOutputFormat`, cached system prompt) runs only when `llmPolicy()` passes: `LLM_PROVIDER_AUTHORIZED`, `ALLOW_LIVE_LLM`, a model id and a key. Non-Claude ids fail closed, because no other adapter exists.
5. Planner output is untrusted. Invariants enforce:
   - Media kind; camera for images, shot for video.
   - Continuity, anti-drift and anti-teleport.
   - Identity lock overwritten from the request (provided angles only, missing angles flagged).
   - Lip-sync status derived from real audio flags; Tehrani accent only when requested.
   - Hyper-realism off for stylized work.
6. Plan inspection re-runs safety on the expanded media prompt and hard constraints.
7. The public plan is a whitelisted projection, and a leak filter drops any plan that echoes vendor or model names, skill titles or skill ids.
8. A private audit records the skill registry version, active skill ids, tier, route and usage, plus a SHA-256 of the prompt (never the raw prompt). The media prompt stays server-side, read through `getPrivateMediaPrompt(turnId)`.

### Verification (run locally on this branch)
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm test`: 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail. 25 are new in `tests/orchestrator.test.ts`: all 22 skills reachable, leak test, prompt injection, invariants, lip-sync/Tehrani/stylized/character cases, political prompt blocked before the planner, plan inspection, audit hashing, adapter request shape and error mapping against a stubbed fetch.
- `npm run build`: succeeds
- `npm run lint`: 2 errors that predate this PR (`components/theme-toggle.tsx`, `components/character-studio.tsx`); both files are replaced in P0/P1.

### Not verified / known gaps
- No live Claude call was made. Whether the API's structured-output transform accepts every constraint in `CreativePlanSchema` is unverified.
- Public plan text is mostly English, with Persian only in the summary and the clarifying question. The UI phase should localize it.
- The audit and media-prompt stores are in memory: lost on restart and not shared across instances. The media-prompt store isn't owner-bound yet, and needs auth (plan phase 02) before any real use.
- The test script now runs with `--conditions=react-server` so `server-only` modules import under node.

Production LLM use stays off until provider and regional authorization (docs/LAUNCH_GATES.md §2) is confirmed.

Stacked on `feat/character-studio-creative-skills`. P3 (Higgsfield adapter) will stack on this branch.

author: kuschikuschbert
body:
## Why
`tests/people-ids.test.js` passed only on its second try 8 times on 4 Nov 2026 (the weekly flaky report, issue #523, last at 17:13). The 17:13 run was Live click tests run 41789817469, share 2. Its log says the first try took 28 s (12 s on retry) and stopped with `Error: waitFor: timed out` at `people-ids.test.js:84`. No check had failed by then.

Line 84 waits for Bo's role to become Sous chef after `L.pick(p, '#a-r2', 'sous')`. Save is off only when the draft has no changes, so the choice never reached the draft.

The cause is in the app. The shared picker (`js/controls.js`) sends a choice to the select it was opened from. `draw()` replaces the whole page (`S.root.innerHTML`), but the picker stays open on `document.body`. If the admin page draws again while the picker is open, the choice goes to the old select, which is no longer on the page. Nothing changes and nothing says so. The picker for groups of buttons already finds the current button again (`js/controls.js`, group picker). The select picker and the type-or-choose picker did not.

What redraws the People tab in that window: a trace of every People tab redraw on open found three. They were the Kitchen mail read finishing (`js/prep.js:10075`), the Dashboard script arriving (`:4849`) and the Review desk scripts arriving (`:4885`). None of them is a config change. So neither the wait at line 80 nor the `__fake.quiet` lines around the step held them back. Locally they land at 0.7 to 0.9 s, just before the line 80 wait passes (1.3 to 1.5 s). On a busy runner, or a live run fetching scripts from Pages, one can land in the 0.1 to 0.3 s between opening the picker and choosing. A head chef on a phone loses a choice the same way when another phone saves while the picker is open.

## What changes for the team
A choice made in a picker while the page draws again under it now lands on its box. Examples: a role on the People tab, any other select, or a type-or-choose field. Before, it was silently lost. Nothing changes when the page does not redraw.

## Files
- `js/controls.js`: new `liveSource()`. When the picker's box is no longer on the page, the choice goes to the box that took its place. It finds it by the same `id` or `data-` name `draw()` uses to put the cursor back. Nothing is applied when there is not exactly one such box, the box is switched off, or it no longer offers the choice. It never guesses. Used by the select picker and the type-or-choose picker.
- `tests/people-ids.test.js`: new check. Another phone saves the staff list (adds Cal) while Bo's Role picker is open, then Sous chef is chosen. Bo becomes Sous chef in the draft, Save comes on, and the Role box says Sous chef. The `__fake.quiet` lines around the old step are gone. They only held back some redraws, which hid this bug.
- `docs/adaptive-controls.md`: the behaviour contract line.
- `README.md`: one sentence in Adaptive choices and search.

## Tests
Before and after (this cloud container, chrome-headless-shell):

| | Old `js/controls.js` | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New check (another phone saves while the picker is open) | fails 7 of 7 runs, 2 failed of 25 | passes |
| `people-ids` alone | (old file) 18 of 18 | 20 of 20, 0 failed of 25 |
| Six copies of the file at once (about 20 s each) | (old file) 48 of 48 | 48 of 48 |
| Page CPU slowed 6 times (26 to 30 s each, like the 28 s CI run) | (old file) 15 of 15 | 10 of 10 |

The old file never failed here: this container doesn't reproduce the runner's timing between the in-page Firestore stand-in and script loads. The new check removes the timing. It makes the redraw happen while the picker is open, every time. The next weekly report shows whether CI agrees.

- `node --check js/controls.js tests/people-ids.test.js`
- Picker-related files with the fix: adaptive-controls, compact-pickers, inline-choices, council-controls, control-feedback, council-page-resets, council-tables, head-chef, kitchen-sections, mail, order-cutoffs, ping-recipients, transfers, wastage-a, waste-week, section-box, targets, reuse, lists, functions, cutoff-lead-days, admin-nav: all pass except one check in `compact-pickers.test.js` ("Mail priority 390 normal: labels that do not fit retain the labelled picker"). It fails the same way on unchanged `main` in this container. It measures label widths, so it depends on the fonts here, and CI passes it.

## Reads, rules and saved data
None. No new reads, rules, fields or `lk.*` copies. `js/controls.js` is a shell file and already in `SHELL` and both `js/upkeep.js` lists. Saved shell generations refresh by content.

## Rollback
Revert this pull request. Nothing else to undo.

## Left to do
Nothing. Watch the next weekly flaky report: `people-ids.test.js` should drop off it.

author: cocvn157
body:
### Summary
Case classes with more than 22 fields derive a Schema.GenericRecord wrapped in .transformOrFail(fromMap, toMap), where  romMap looks up decoded field values in the ListMap[String, Any] using the original  ield.fieldName.

When a JsonCodec.Config with a non-identity  ieldNameFormat (such as NameFormat.PascalCase or NameFormat.SnakeCase) was used:
1. CaseClassJsonDecoder.unsafeDecodeListMap (used when  ields.length <= 64) inserted entries into the ListMap keyed by spans(idx).field (the formatted JSON wire name) rather than  ields(idx).fieldName, causing  romMap to fail with (Missing field <fieldName>).
2. JsonDecoder.recordDecoder (used when  ields.length > 64) did not apply config.fieldNameFormat to spans when matching incoming JSON field names.

This PR fixes both paths:
- CaseClassJsonDecoder.unsafeDecodeListMap now keys the returned ListMap by  ields(idx).fieldName while matching incoming JSON keys against the formatted spans and liasedFieldIdx.
- JsonDecoder.recordDecoder now applies config.fieldNameFormat to spans for matching JSON wire keys while keying the resulting ListMap by  ields(idx).fieldName.

### Tests
- Added unit tests in JsonCodecSpec verifying NameFormat.PascalCase and NameFormat.SnakeCase round-trip encoding and decoding for case classes with > 22 fields as well as > 64 fields.

author: xnfinite
body:
An audit of the repository as a stranger would install and use it. Each fix below was reproduced first, then checked by two independent reviewers trying to disprove it. Each one has a test that fails on `main` and passes here. The fix commit itself had a second, independent review; its findings are fixed in the second commit. The third commit fixes a Windows-only failure the second commit introduced.

## Fixed (most serious first)

1. **The checker mod never ran in any install** (`hooks/register.ts`). It looked for `icm_check.py` at `<workspace>/skills/...`, and no install route puts the checker there. The plugin route puts it at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/icm-ops/icm-ops/0.3.0/skills/...`.
   - Live headless session on `main`, writing a broken link into a copy of `example/`: the agent got nothing (`NONE`). Same session on this branch: `icm-ops: this write FAILS the workspace checker. - broken relative link in 02-processes/new.md: (missing.md)`.
   - It now runs the plugin's own copy.
   - It records the FAILs a workspace already has before a session's first write there, once per workspace. Before this, the first write would have been blamed for the whole backlog.
   - It still checks the write that creates `00-catalog/`.
   - Its "Full detail" hint is a command that runs, with paths quoted.
2. **`lease.py`: two sessions could each be told they hold one resource.** Break, renew and release read the lease file, then changed whatever was at that path.
   - A deterministic interleaving test (a second real process placed between the read and the change) shows this on `main`: both sessions exit 0, or a release deletes the lease another session just took.
   - Those three steps now hold a short `<resource>.json.lock`. A lock older than 10 s is removed as left by a dead process. A lock that can't be had within 30 s ends in exit 1, not an endless wait.
   - On Windows, an exclusive create raises `PermissionError`, not `FileExistsError`, when the name is a directory or a file still being deleted. The lock create and the lease create now treat that as "there, or going: look again". On other systems it still raises. Without this, every Windows job failed the stuck-lock test with a traceback, and a take arriving while another session dropped its lock or released its lease would crash.
   - The name `config` is refused: taking it moved the mod's `config.json` into `stale/`.
3. **session-leases mod** (`plugins/session-leases/hooks/register.ts`).
   - It never released a push lease when the take had first broken an expired one, because `took` is the second line of the output.
   - It took no lease for a `git push` on its own line of a multi-line command.
4. **probe-first.** A hedge word anywhere in a reply excused an unhedged absolute in another sentence. Now each sentence is judged on its own, and a sentence carries on past "e.g." and "i.e.".
5. **`icm_check.py`.**
   - A stray name in `log_dir` (`2026-xx-yy.md`, `2026-09-31.md`) stood in for the newest log. That hid a log 108 days in the future and moved the truncation guard off the real newest log.
   - A `checked:` with no window hid the stale stamp that followed it.
   - A D-entry past KNOW-BY was told to "mark EXPIRED", which icm-ledger forbids.
6. **Mod tests failed on Linux and macOS.** The fixtures used `C:/` paths, which the harness treats as relative there. Before: icm-gates 2/12, session-leases 11/12. After, on Linux: 12/12 and 14/14. The mod code itself was fine.
7. **Banned-phrase sweep** skipped `hooks/`, `plugins/` and `types/`, which already held one banned phrase. It now covers them, and the phrase is reworded.
8. **Docs.**
   - README:

body:
Martien reported on 4 Nov that all the courses he built had disappeared from test.prospergenics.com.

## What happened
**Nothing was deleted.**
- His five courses (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, AI Software Lifecycle) are still in the jengo-listings system: the listings service returns `total: 5`.
- Their pages and lessons still work, for example `/courses/python/` and `/courses/python/learn/`.
- What changed is this. Since 10 Oct, `/courses/` was the jengo-listings course catalogue. On 25 Oct (PR #29) this theme's own course archive took over `/courses/`. That archive lists only courses made with the theme's course tools, and there are none on test, so the page said "0 courses". Every homepage and menu link to Courses landed there. This was flagged in the audit as cards #6499 and #6524 but not fixed.

**The blog:**
- All 50 production posts are on test, plus 2 more (52 in total).
- But `/blog/` is an ordinary empty page on test, because Settings → Reading has no posts page. So the posts weren't listed anywhere.

## Fix
- **`inc/courses/listings.php`** reads the courses collection from the listings service the plugin uses.
  - Results are cached for 30 minutes, and the last good list is kept, so a short outage never empties the catalogue.
  - `/courses/` shows those courses first, in the theme's card style, counted in "N courses".
  - Each card links to the course page and to "Start learning" (its lessons).
  - Courses made with the theme's own tools are listed after them. Category and level filters still apply to those.
- **`page-blog.php`**: `/blog/` lists the published posts with paging, whatever the Reading setting is.

## Checks
- New `tests/test-2026-content-restore.php` (20 checks): parsing, escaping, caching, the outage fallback and the wiring.
- All `tests/*.php` pass.
- The e2e role matrix passes 295/295.
- In a real WordPress with the courses list taken from the listings service on 4 Nov:
  - `/courses/` shows "6 courses" (Martien's 5 plus the seeded one), each linking to `/courses/<slug>/` and `/learn/`;
  - `/blog/` lists the posts;

The pin validator gains an optional `cuisine`, which installed apps ignore (`Convex-Api: changed` trailer). - `placeEmoji` order: a specific Apple category, then the cuisine, then a food word in the name (only under no category or a broad one), then the broad category, then the save's tags. `CUISINE_EMOJI` is the one table, and name words map to a cuisine through it. - `placeKinds(category, tags, cuisine)` decides the food or drink kind from the cuisine (tea counts as coffee, bakery as dessert). It still adds a non-food category kind, and a coffee or drinks category beside a food cuisine. `mergeVenueKinds` keeps the kept pin's cuisine and fills it from a duplicate only when empty. `cityPins` (city page) and `listMapPlaces` (Map tab) both pass the cuisine through. - The place editor (`currentPlaces`) leaves the cuisine out. ## Verification ### What I ran - `pnpm run check:code` (the pre-push gate): passed. - `node tools/verify-convex-api.mjs origin/main feat/place-cuisine`: the pin shape widened, acknowledged by the trailer. author: marlboro62
body:
## Problème

En mode client, l'écran de choix des PDL partagés appelle `/admin/shared-pdls` sur la passerelle. La passerelle ne partage des PDL qu'avec les comptes administrateurs : pour tous les autres comptes, elle répond 403, et c'est le cas normal.

Ce 403 est pourtant journalisé en trois lignes ERROR / WARNING (adaptateur puis route), ce qui fait croire à une panne de la passerelle. Des utilisateurs l'ont signalé comme une erreur sur le forum.

## Correction

- `MyElectricalDataAdapter._make_request` accepte un paramètre optionnel `expected_statuses`. Quand le statut reçu en fait partie, il écrit une seule ligne INFO (« réponse attendue ») au lieu des logs ERROR, puis lève l'exception comme avant.
- `get_shared_pdls` passe `expected_statuses={401, 403}`.
- Route `list_shared_pdls` : un 401 ou 403 est noté en INFO (« compte de la passerelle non administrateur »). Les autres erreurs (passerelle injoignable, 5xx) restent en WARNING.

## Ce qui ne change pas

- L'erreur est toujours levée et renvoyée au front : l'écran affiche le même message qu'avant.
- Les autres appels de l'adaptateur journalisent leurs erreurs comme avant.

## Tests

Nouveau fichier `apps/api/tests/unit/test_shared_pdls_403_journal.py` :

- adaptateur : un 401 ou 403 est levé sans log WARNING ou ERROR, et un 500 sur un autre appel reste en ERROR ;
- route : un 403 donne un log INFO et un code 403, et un 502 reste en WARNING avec un code 502.

Tous les tests unitaires passent (765), ainsi que `ruff` et `mypy` sur les fichiers modifiés.

author: jeroenjanssens
body:
Modernizes the Data Science Toolbox image while keeping the commands from *Data Science at the Command Line* working.

## Changes

- **Dockerfile instead of Packer and Ansible.** Multi-stage build: the tools that aren't packaged or maintained (vw 9.11.9, tapkee 1.4.0, xsv 0.13.0, pup, fx 40.0.1, json2csv, csvquote) are compiled in builder stages, so no compilers end up in the final image.
- **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS** (was 21.04). R 4.5 with binary packages from Posit Package Manager, pinned to a snapshot date.
- **Multi-platform:** native linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so it runs natively on Apple Silicon and Windows on ARM too. The 2021 image was amd64-only.
- **uv** manages Python 3.13 and the Python tools. `pip` runs `uv pip` in the default virtual environment, so `pip install` from the book still works (without sudo, and without the PEP 668 error).
- **GitHub Actions** builds and tests on native amd64 and arm64 runners. On `master` it pushes `datasciencetoolbox/dsatcl2e:latest` and `:YYYYMMDD`. Pull requests only build and test.
- **Size:** about 560 MB compressed, against 1.02 GB for `:20210628`.

## Backwards compatibility

- Every tool from the book's [list of command-line tools](https://jeroenjanssens.com/dsatcl/list-of-command-line-tools) is included; `tests/smoke.sh` checks them all, plus a selection of commands from the book.
- Older tags stay available; the README tells readers how to pull `:20210628`, the image used for the second edition.
- Same user (`dst`, uid 1000, passwordless sudo), shell (zsh), aliases, and `ENTRYPOINT`.
- Pins needed to keep the book's commands working, all documented in the Dockerfile:
  - csvkit 1.1.0: from 1.1.1 on, `csvstack a.csv <(...)` (Chapter 9) fails
  - `sqlalchemy<2` and `setuptools<81`: needed by csvkit 1.1.0's `csvsql`
  - `pandas<3`: skll 5.1 rejects pandas 3's string arrays as ids
  - Python 3.13: skll needs scikit-learn<1.6
- agate's "Error sniffing CSV dialect" warning is silenced, so `csvlook` output matches the book.
- Tools that changed: `tldr` is now tealdeer (same commands, different formatting), and `fx` is now the Go version (the book's example still works). The coreutils are Ubuntu 26.04's default uutils; 95 of 98 book-style coreutils commands gave identical output to GNU coreutils.

## Known issue

`rush run '<ggplot expression>' > plot.png` writes nothing; see jeroenjanssens/rush#8. The smoke test reports this as a known failure without failing the run. Once it's fixed, bump `RUSH_COMMIT` in the Dockerfile and turn that check into a regular one.

## Before merging

- Add the repository secrets `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`. Merging into `master` publishes `:latest`.

body:
## What Changed

- C# codegen: a child entity of a concrete parent now declares the parent's properties itself and names no C# base class, so each mapped entity keeps all its columns. A child of an abstract parent (with EmitAbstractShapes) emits `class Child : Base` and declares only its own members. Removed the dead special-case guard in the cross-field `Validate` override. Added `EntityExtendsParentTests`.
- Cross-field `validator.comparison` now follows one rule in all five ports. Numerics compare with each other. Strings and temporals compare only with the same subtype (temporals also need matching `@localTime`). Boolean, enum, uuid, uri and inet fields test only eq/ne. Any other pair is skipped, never rejected. Java/Kotlin no longer cast to `Comparable` (create returned 500 instead of 400), TypeScript no longer compares as strings, and Python no longer raises `TypeError`. Ordering on boolean and enum is no longer enforced by generated validators. Added shared conformance cases in `fixtures/validation-conformance/`, documented in its README, and re-synced the owned zod-validators template copies.
- Test stability and coverage: the C# `DependencyCliTests` now joins the serial `OwnedRunnerCollection`, fixing a working-directory race. The codegen-ts compile tests share a 30s timeout from `test/compile-timeout.ts`. The Java Patch cross-field test executes the generated Dto and Patch classes instead of comparing source text. A TS React regression test covers a TPH subtype form binding the refined body schema. Adds a test-scope `jackson-datatype-jsr310` to `codegen-spring` for the conformance runner.
- CHANGELOG entries under Unreleased. No version bump.

## Flaky tests fixed (at the cause, no retries)

- C# Cli `GenCommandTests.Gen_writes_the_hash_manifest_beside_the_metadata_not_in_cwd`: `DependencyCliTests` runs `gen` in process, which changes the process-wide working directory, without joining the serial `OwnedRunnerCollection`; the two classes ran in parallel and one read the other's directory as the cwd (about one run in five). Now serial; 12 of 12 looped runs passed after the fix.
- codegen-ts tests that type-check generated output with the real TypeScript compiler (29 files, including `tph-cross-field.test.ts`): bun's 5s default timeout against a slowest measured 3.3s case under load. Each file now calls `setDefaultTimeout(COMPILE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS)` (30s, defined once in `test/compile-timeout.ts`; a side-effect import would only reach the first file per process). The original timeouts were not reproduced on demand, so this one is justified by measurement.

## Gate runs

Two no-mistakes runs for this PR. Run 1 failed at the test step before any push because GitHub SSH auth was down during a GitHub incident (infrastructure, not code); its review fixes were carried into run 2, which produced this PR. The test step of run 2 was approved past an "inconclusive" live-evidence verdict after the maintainer-requested serial local suites all passed (C# Codegen 1128, Cli 364, Conformance 2222; Java/Kotlin cross-field and conformance; Python 1304; TS cross-field conformance 25, codegen-ts 71, codegen-ts-react 62).

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Codegen and test-only changes, bounded and consistent across all five ports; the prior-round fixes (@localTime comparability, C# eq/ne CLR-type guard, per-file timeouts) check out against the code, and I found no regression I could substantiate.

## Testing

Live-driven: per-file compile timeout probe on the real bun runner (pass). Suite-only, not live: TS validation conformance (85 pass), C# codegen (1128 pass, incl. EqAcrossClrTypes), C# conformance (2222 pass), C# CLI (364 pass). Not driven: Java, Kotlin and Python conformance and unit suites, java-reactor build, integration-tests lanes, full ci-local.sh run. Verdict inconclusive: live-exercisable surface exists but only one scenario was driven live.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 1 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TS validator skips cross-kind comparison (date vs timestamp, instant vs wall-clock) and enforces uuid ne | ⏸️ untested | no | Prior payload recorded only a generated-validator test suite run, not a live product run. Live drive not established. |
| Per-file 30s compile timeout applies in plain bun test regardless of file order | ✅ pass | live | Temporary probe files run with bun test in codegen-ts, both orders; probes removed |
| C# eq/ne across differing CLR types (instant vs wall-clock) is skipped, not rejected | ⏸️ untested | no | Prior payload recorded a generator test suite run, which compiles and inspects output; no live product run was established. |
| C# child of concrete parent declares inherited properties with no base clause (inheritance fix) | ⏸️ untested | no | Covered only by the codegen suite pass; no live run of the inheritance case was established. |
| Java/Kotlin/Python cross-kind comparison skipped instead of ClassCastException/TypeError | ⏸️ untested | no | Java-reactor, Kotlin and Python conformance lanes were not executed. Would need mvn and uv test runs of the validation corpus in those ports. |
| C# CLI GenCommandTests hash-manifest flake fixed by serial collection | ⏸️ untested | no | Prior payload recorded one suite run, not a live reproduction or repeated runs to measure flake rate. |

- Outcome: ⚠️ 2 warnings across 1 run (36m53s)

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

- ⚠️ `server/typescript/packages/codegen-ts/test/tph-cross-field.test.ts:164` - The intent says every codegen-ts test that type-checks generated output with the real TypeScript compiler runs under the shared 30s timeout. tph-cross-field.test.ts does this, but it is not one of the 28 files. It calls `ts.createProgram` at line 123, and its test "the generated entity, queries and routes compile" (line 164) runs that compile. The file never calls `setDefaultTimeout(COMPILE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS)`. Bun scopes that call to the file that makes it, so this test keeps bun's 5s default. On a loaded machine it can still report the timeout flake this change says it fixes. CI passes `--timeout 30000`, so CI does not hit it. A plain `bun test` in the package can. Fix: import `setDefaultTimeout` and `COMPILE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS` from `./compile-timeout.js`, and call it at the file's top level, as the other 28 files do. The file came from #530 and is not in this diff. The gap is in the coverage this change claims. Every other `createProgram` user under test/ already makes the call.

🔧 Fix applied.
1 warning still open:

- ⚠️ `server/csharp/MetaObjects.Codegen/Generators/EntityGenerator.cs:1159` - The eq/ne fallback in the C# comparison emitter requires only the same field subtype, not the same CLR type. `loggedAt eq wallClock` (`field.timestamp` vs `field.timestamp @localTime`) misses the temporal branch because ScalarForField differs (DateTimeOffset vs DateTime). It then reaches `!ordering && l.SubType == r.SubType && lk != Other` and emits `Equals(__l, __r)`. That compares a boxed DateTimeOffset with a boxed DateTime, which is always false, so `eq` rejects every body where both fields are set. `

author: bluecmd
body:
Closes #137

## Root cause

`Fan.get_presence()` in the Seastone 2 `sonic_platform` package runs `ipmitool raw 0x3a 0x03 0x03 N` through `APIHelper.run_command`, which is `subprocess.getstatusoutput`: it drops the trailing newline but keeps ipmitool's leading space, so the reply is `' 00'`. The comparison `output == "00"` was therefore never true and every chassis fan and every PSU fan was Not Present. thermalctld (running since #69/#70) reported "Fan 1-4 Front/Rear is missing" and "PSU 1/2 Fan 1 is missing", so system-health Hardware stayed Not OK and the status LED amber. Upstream sonic-net master has the same line.

## Audit of the other ipmitool consumers in the package

Every other `run_command` / `ipmi_raw` / `ipmi_fru_id` reader was checked for the same problem:

| file | reader | result |
|---|---|---|
| fan.py `get_presence` | `output == "00"` | **broken**, fixed with `output.strip()` |
| fan.py `get_direction` (PSU fan) | `output.split(':')[-1]`, then `model[-2:] == ' B'` | works, but a trailing blank on the FRU line would hide the suffix; now `rstrip()`ed |
| fan.py `get_direction`, `get_target_speed`, `get_status_led`; chassis.py `get_status_led` | `int(output, 16)` | fine, `int()` ignores surrounding whitespace |
| fan.py `get_speed`, `get_model`, `get_serial`; psu.py all sensor reads, `get_presence`, `get_status`; thermal.py all reads | `output.split()[n]` | fine |
| psu.py `get_model` / `get_serial`; component.py BMC version | `split(':')[-1].strip()` | fine |
| component.py ONIE / SSD | regex | fine |
| sfp.py, eeprom.py, watchdog.py | no ipmitool; sysfs reads are stripped | n/a |

## Tests

`platform/broadcom/sonic-platform-modules-cel/seastone2/tests/test_ipmi_text.py` patches `subprocess.getstatusoutput` with a fake ipmitool that answers exactly as the real one does (`' 00'`, `' 46 c0 00 00'`, FRU grep lines) and drives the real `APIHelper`, `Fan`, `FanDrawer`, `Psu`, `Thermal`, `Chassis` and `Component` code. `sonic_py_common` and the `sonic_platform_base` classes are stubbed, so it needs only pytest.

Run in the `sonic-builder-spark1-0` pod, `python:3.13` container:

- test commit alone (e867a60f, code from `origin/202611-master`): **13 failed, 33 passed**. All 8 chassis fans, both PSU fans, the fan drawer and `get_status` are Not Present with `' 00'`; the 13th is the trailing-blank PSU airflow case.
- branch head: **46 passed**.

The tests are registered as package `seastone2-platform` in `.github/unit-tests.json` and added to the default package list of `sonic-tests.yml`, so the unified workflow from #114 runs them. No new workflow file. Not run: the `sonic-tests` workflow itself (needs a dispatch on the runner), an image build, and hardware.

## Hardware check (ixp-lab-sw2, Seastone 2)

```
show platform fan                 # expected: Fan 1-4 Front/Rear and PSU 1/2 Fan 1 all Present, with speed and direction
show system-health summary        # expected: Hardware OK, status LED green
show system-health detail | grep -i missing   # expected: nothing
```
As a quick check without a new image, the fixed `fan.py` can be dropped into the pmon container at `/usr/local/lib/python3*/dist-packages/sonic_platform/fan.py` followed by `docker restart pmon`.

## Noticed while writing the tests, not changed here

- `Thermal.__init__` records the first reading as min/max; if ipmitool fails at that moment the reading is `'N/A'` and every later `get_temperature()` raises `TypeError` on `float > str`.
- `Fan.get_status_led` reuses `status` for the command result, so an unknown LED value returns `True` instead of `'N/A'`.
- `Psu.get_voltage/current/power/presence/status` index into `output.split()` before checking `status`, so an ipmitool failure raises `IndexError`.

## O que muda

**Botão na tela inicial**
- "Baixar para Windows / macOS / Linux", conforme o sistema de quem vê, com um link "Outros sistemas" para a página do Release.
- Não aparece no celular nem dentro do app de computador.
- Aponta para `releases/latest/download/...`, então vale sempre para a versão mais nova.

**Instaladores com nome fixo** (`desktop/electron-builder.yml`)
- `Discordia-Windows.exe`, `Discordia-Mac.dmg`, `Discordia-Linux.AppImage` / `.deb`.

**Workflow do app** (`.github/workflows/desktop.yml`)
- Cria o rascunho do Release antes, os três sistemas enviam para ele, e o Release só é publicado quando os três terminam. Antes ele ficava como rascunho e o link daria 404.
- A versão do app sai da tag (`v1.0.0` → `1.0.0`).
- Sem disparo manual: o build precisa de uma tag.

## Depois do merge

1. Em **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables**, criar `VITE_SIGNAL_URL` (Worker) e `VITE_PUBLIC_URL` (`https://discordia-six.vercel.app`).
2. `git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`.

Até o primeiro Release existir, o botão leva a um 404.

## Testes

- Novo `tests/download.test.ts`: escolha do instalador por sistema e botão escondido no celular.
- `npx vitest run`: 50 de 50 passam.
- `svelte-check`: 0 erros.
- Playwright `1-interface` e `16-desktop`: 4 de 4 passam.

author: deardeng
body:
### Background

In cloud mode, a BE's rowset RPC carries its cloud_unique_id, and MS resolves the owning instance through the registered node information. A decommission state change must keep that registration available while in-flight loads finish.

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: None
Related PR: None
PR Type: Bugfix

Problem Summary: Both start-decommission and completion updated node status by deleting the node and re-adding it in separate transactions. Each transaction independently committed and refreshed the MS cache, exposing a state with the target node missing. A concurrent rowset commit could then fail with "failed to commit rowset: empty instance_id". Update the existing node's status in one transaction and add deterministic regression coverage for both transitions.

### Details

- **Change map:** 202 production lines changed, including the state-update fix, legacy cluster identification, and injection support; 396 test-code lines changed; 7 generated expected-output lines. The two handlers are consolidated, and most additions are tests.
- **Frequency:** Intermittent during concurrent loading and decommission state changes. The new regression fixes the execution order and reproduces the old behavior for both transitions.
- **Root cause:** The delete transaction publishes metadata and a cache snapshot without the node before the add transaction restores it. If that removes the last mapping for the BE's cloud_unique_id and the ID cannot be decoded through the compatibility format, get_instance_id returns empty. The cache lock protects each refresh, but does not make the two transactions atomic.
- **Why existing tests missed it:** The regression issued INSERTs once per second without controlling whether a rowset commit hit this short window. Existing HTTP coverage used cache-only node setup and checked the final response.
- **Fix:** Share a handler that uses ResourceManager::update_cluster to match existing nodes by UID and endpoint within the target cluster, change only their status, commit once, and refresh once. Preserve node identity, timestamps, and node-based HTTP cluster lookup. For named legacy clusters whose persisted cluster_id is absent or empty, resolve the canonical cluster name from the existing node and match that name plus the empty stored ID in the same transaction. Only node-status operations opt into name-based updates; other update_cluster callers still require a nonempty ID. An unmatched batch returns an error before any partial change is published.
- **Legacy metadata compatibility:** HTTP add_cluster accepts named clusters without a stored ID. The initial atomic rewrite incorrectly inherited update_cluster's mandatory-ID precondition, causing both state operations on that valid metadata to return INVALID_ARGUMENT: missing cluster_id=. Earlier coverage omitted the request ID but still persisted a nonempty cluster ID. Add tests where the stored field itself is absent or explicitly empty, including real HTTP add_cluster creation. Both status operations must preserve the entire stored cluster apart from the requested node status; no ID is synthesized or written.
- **Other paths and branches:** Apply the same handler to DECOMMISSION_NODE and NOTIFY_DECOMMISSIONED. This PR targets master; no backports are included.
- **Behavior change:** Status changes retain node registration throughout the update. Requests containing missing or mismatched nodes fail without persisting part of the batch.

### Testing

The regression uses one BE and one bucket so the load must reach the target node:

1. Start a real INSERT and hold its commit_rowset RPC immediately before instance lookup.
2. Run the status update and hold it after its transaction has committed and refreshed the cache.
3. Confirm both gates were reached, then release only the rowset RPC. Require INSERT to succeed and COUNT(*) / SUM(id) to both equal 1 while the state-update request is still held.
4. Clear the gates in finally. For the completion case, first put the node into DECOMMISSIONING while the rowset commit is held.

The injection points control execution order; the node-state implementation determines which metadata is published.

| Implementation under test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed start and completion handlers | Full cloud_decommission passed, including both controlled interleavings and the original 2-BE/3-BE, WAL, continuous INSERT, and FE-restart scenarios |
| Old start and completion handlers | The controlled start case failed with failed to commit rowset: empty instance_id |
| Fixed start handler and old completion handler | The start case and its result check passed; the controlled completion case failed with the same empty instance_id error |

The two old-handler negative controls above were run before the compatibility follow-up. Negative runs used isolated suite identifiers to run beside the positive cluster. SQL, assertions, expected data, and gates were identical; the node-state handlers were switched between fixed and old implementations.

Legacy stored-ID positive/negative verification (the same added tests applied to the previous PR implementation and to the compatibility fix):

| Stored cluster ID / operation | Before compatibility fix | After compatibility fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field absent / decommission_node | HTTP 400, INVALID_ARGUMENT: missing cluster_id= | HTTP 200 / OK; exact persisted metadata preserved except status |
| Field absent / notify_decommissioned | Same failure | HTTP 200 / OK; exact persisted metadata preserved except status |
| Explicit empty string / decommission_node | Same failure | HTTP 200 / OK; exact persisted metadata preserved except status |
| Explicit empty string / notify_decommissioned | Same failure | HTTP 200 / OK; exact persisted metadata preserved except status |
| Atomic cache-publication checks with IP and hostname addressing | Both new parameterized unit tests fail | Both pass; each operation publishes exactly once, retains UID lookup, and leaves other nodes/clusters unchanged |

The HTTP tests create the named, ID-less cluster through the real add_cluster endpoint, verify its persisted ID presence/value, and invoke each state operation independently. The unit tests also omit the request name, exercise a UID shared across clusters, and verify canonical name resolution. Between the negative and positive runs, the HTTP test source changed only by clang-format whitespace; this was checked against the recorded negative-run source hash.

- Four original deterministic unit tests fail with the old delete/add implementation and pass with the atomic fix.
- resource_test: all 21 tests passed under ASAN, including both new stored-ID tests.
- HTTP coverage: all 36 tests passed under ASAN (32 MetaServiceHttpTest cases plus four new stored-ID combinations), using the existing repository LeakSanitizer suppressions.
- The full cloud_decommission positive suite was rerun with the compatibility fix; the old-handler negative controls were retained from the earlier validation.
- The expected .out file was generated by the regression runner and compared in the final normal positive run.
- Repository clang-format 16, build-hygiene, and clang-tidy checks on changed lines passed.

### Notes for Reviewers

MS was built from this source with ASAN and injection points enabled; FE/BE reused an existing test image. No RPC fields or stored metadata formats change. Non-injection builds compile the new checkpoints away.

### Release note

Fix intermittent empty instance_id load errors during cloud backend decommissioning, while preserving decommission operations for named clusters without a stored cluster ID.

### Check List (For Author)

- Test: Regression test, unit tests, and static checks described above
- Behavior changed: Yes (see Details)
- Does this need documentation: No
- Pre-submission status: Ready

### AI Disclosure

- Tool: Codex
- Generated: Code, tests, and this description
- Human review: Pe

author: 4gatepylon
body:
## Summary

A timeline of d1s on layer 50 had the last block reach the merge at 7.8 µs and the span end at 14.7. The merging block then took up to 4.7 µs to merge and 2.6 µs to write 8 rows. The write computed each output's sigmoid gate and scale with IEEE division and full-range `expf`, and the warp combine and both merges used `exp2f`. Each of those compiles to a slow path with branches, in code each merging block runs once. They now use `__fdividef`, `__expf` and the kernel's `fast_exp2` (`ex2.approx.ftz`). All of these round far below bf16's precision; per-test errors match to 3 or 4 digits.

The short shapes get 3 to 8% faster (d1s 16.2 → 15.3 µs, v1s 18.4 → 16.9 µs, d1f 31.7 → 29.6 µs, now level with v56, v1f 36.9 → 35.4 µs). The long shapes stay within noise.

Run `20261104-122845-layer51` (H100 PCIe, 20 repetitions):

| shape | lee_101 v56 (µs) | layer 50 (µs) | **layer 51 (µs)** | layer 51 ÷ v56 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d1s | 11.4 | 16.2 | **15.3** | 1.34 |
| d1f | 29.7 | 31.7 | **29.6** | 0.99 |
| d16s | 17.3 | 21.5 | **21.0** | 1.21 |
| d16f | 255.7 | 212.6 | **212.0** | 0.83 |
| d32s | 23.8 | 26.2 | **25.5** | 1.07 |
| d32f | 497.9 | 411.1 | **410.2** | 0.82 |
| v1s | 15.6 | 18.4 | **16.9** | 1.09 |
| v1f | 28.2 | 36.9 | **35.4** | 1.26 |
| v16s | 22.0 | 27.8 | **27.5** | 1.25 |
| v16f | 217.5 | 252.8 | **252.0** | 1.16 |
| v32s | 28.6 | 37.8 | **37.1** | 1.30 |
| v32f | 428.3 | 476.4 | **474.8** | 1.11 |
## Changes

- `meta_muse_spark100k_challenge/4gatepylon_official_work/muse_attention_decode/fused_attention.py`: `write_gated_output` (with a Performance note in its docstring), `combine_warps`, `merge_slots` and `merge_rows`.

## Decisions

- **Question:** How fast is this version on each scored shape, next to the previous layer and lee_101's v56?
- **Given:** A readable CUDA kernel that fuses all of the attention; a stack where each PR adds a point; local H100 timing.
- **Outcomes:** Median µs per shape, from the same run as v56. The method is the same as #101.

### Procedure

#### D53. Fast math in the epilogue, not in the cache writes

- **Choice:** `__fdividef`, `__expf` and `ex2.approx` for the merge weights, the output scale and the gate.
- **Alternatives:** The same for `store_new_keys`' divisions by the cache scales; seq_len-independent page-table loads for full layers.
- **Rationale:**
  - `store_new_keys` writes the FP8 cache, so it keeps the reference's exact division: an approximate quotient could round some keys to a different FP8 value.
  - Issuing full layers' page-table loads before the request's length arrives made d16f and v16f 5% slower.
- **Revisit if:** the cache contents are known to be unchecked.

## Testing

- `bench_attention_decode.py --test-seed-count 2`: all 16 `TASK.md` tests pass, eager and replayed on fresh inputs, as do all 12 scored shapes.
- `uvx ruff format --check` and `uvx ruff check` pass.

## Stack

Layer 51/57. Based on #136.

## Size

Reviewable lines: 13 (`fused_attention.py`).

author: pablopunk
body:
## Summary

Emoji & Symbols search now gets a second batch of matches ranked by the decision model (jev). Local fuzzy search is unchanged and instant; about 350ms after the user pauses typing, jev-ranked matches appear after the local ones. Searching "cute" used to show five name matches (acute accent, tiger face, ...) and now adds cats, panda, dog, penguin, pleading face and more.

**New extension API primitive:** a list/grid view can set `onSearchChange`. The host runs it debounced, never for empty text, with the trimmed text as `action.value`, and shows the returned `patch.searchResultIds` (ids of items already in the view) after the local matches. Answers for text the user has since changed are dropped, and failures stay silent. Documented in `nevermind-extension-api.d.ts`; dev fixture: *Dev UI: Grid Search Results*.

**How the emoji extension scores:** one decision call answers at most 16 questions and the catalog has about 3,800 characters, so it narrows in three calls: category predicates, then choice-question shortlisting (31 candidates + "none of these" per question), then one predicate per shortlisted candidate. Candidates at probability >= 0.5 (`MATCH_THRESHOLD`) are shown, best first. Flags, Technical and Math stay name-matched only; a chosen category skips the first call; short text (< 3 chars) is skipped and repeats are cached.

Things to know: each search costs up to 3 AI calls against the 30/min per-extension limit, so heavy use makes the second batch silently not appear. `App.tsx` was at its size cap, so `selectionAfterPatch` moved to `view-patches.ts` and baselines were lowered. Also adds `.agents/skills/nevermind-box-signin/SKILL.md` (running the app signed in on a disposable box).

author: farnalabs
body:
## Why

The compose release bundle (FAR-2345) is correctly pinned to the immutable RC tag at cut/recut, because a `vX.Y.Z` image does not exist yet at that point. But nothing ever produced a GA bundle pinned to the GA tag, so a promoted release shipped no usable compose asset.

## What

- New `promote-compose` job in `release-unified.yml`, promote mode only:
  1. Anonymous-pull gate with `DOCKER_CONFIG` pointed at an empty temp dir, pulling `ghcr.io/farnalabs/modulo:v<version>` — proves the exact tag a clean host will pull, and cannot be satisfied by an ambient credential.
  2. Packages the bundle with `--tag v<version>` (rejects a non-`vX.Y.Z` tag).
  3. Regenerates `SHA256SUMS` and the Ed25519-signed manifest covering the GA bundle, then verifies with `sha256sum --check`.
  4. Attaches the compose assets to the `v<version>` release after confirming it exists. No `--clobber`: replacing an asset invalidates every checked download, so a partial promote is repaired by hand.
- RC path untouched — cut/recut still pins `v<version>-rcN` through the single existing implementation.
- Regression test distinguishing RC pinning from GA pinning, plus two promote-mode structure gates.

## One change beyond the literal brief

Promote previously retagged only `<version>` and `latest`. A `vX.Y.Z` image tag did not exist, so a GA bundle pinned to `vX.Y.Z` would reference nothing and the pull gate would fail the release. The retag now also publishes `v<version>`, keeping the existing `<version>` and `latest` tags for Helm.

## Verification (observed)

- `test_package_compose_release.py` 18 passed
- `run_test_suite_quality.py --changed-files` 212 passed
- The two new rehearsal gates were executed directly against the real workflow YAML: pass. That file is `posix_only`, so it skips on this Windows host and runs for real in Linux CI.
- The shipped signing heredoc was extracted from the YAML and executed against a synthetic `release-artefacts` tree: manifest produced with the expected key id and matching digest
- ruff / ruff-format / check-yaml / scoped semgrep / pre-push merge-conflict gate: clean

## Deferred (not claimed green)

- No Docker on this workstation: the anonymous pull, the real retag and a clean-host deploy are unvalidated locally and deferred to Linux CI.
- mypy on the two changed test files reports pre-existing errors only (CI type-checks `src/modulo/`, not tests); no `backend/src` change.

Resolves FAR-2370.

author: cv
body:
## Related Issue

None.

## Description

The Kubernetes GPU autoscaling recipe pinned single-platform `linux/amd64` manifest digests for several images, so `linux/arm64` nodes could not run the chart or the default sandboxes without image overrides. This change pins each image's multi-platform index digest instead. Each new index contains the previously pinned amd64 manifest, so amd64 nodes keep the same image, and adds a `linux/arm64` variant.

| Image | Where | Old digest (amd64 manifest) | New digest (index) | Platforms in index |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ollama/ollama` (tag `latest` → `0.32.3`) | `values.yaml` | `sha256:f040603c11a11f125660eaf848170780e43b68973fc270e26f168536031ac258` | `sha256:ec24bcaa2a810eb74171ce7c517813ef4821ed678988845e8d76cf62467036d4` | linux/amd64, linux/arm64 |
| `nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm` (tag `latest` → `26.03.post1-py3`) | `values.yaml` | `sha256:7be6c2f676c36059a494fe17254e69ae5c677535ba6191044e5fc8e42a91c773` | `sha256:fe21f1b1f3a53886515a191ba6309065a54b3e026fe8a43573e75e4ecdfd530d` | linux/amd64, linux/arm64 |
| `node` (tag `22-bookworm-slim` → `22.23.1-bookworm-slim`) | `values.yaml` (metrics proxy), HPA load-test scripts | `sha256:8607a9064d4a571140998ae9e52a3b3fcf9cff361d04642d5971e6cd76d39e27` | `sha256:6c74791e557ce11fc957704f6d4fe134a7bc8d6f5ca4403205b2966bd488f6b3` | linux/amd64, linux/arm/v7, linux/arm64/v8, linux/ppc64le |
| `ghcr.io/nvidia/nemoclaw/hermes-sandbox` | `scripts/agent-common.sh`, `AGENT-SELECTION.md` | `sha256:28b9578ab9676ef046de37fa6feb9b7b61824b87d77fd08978758bd01c03cb54` | `sha256:45cc0b5e8356ee09cb6e0cd60f281b2470cf5ef482b4bde4bd97f0cbe96bbd17` | linux/amd64, linux/arm64 |
| `ghcr.io/nvidia/nemoclaw/langchain-deepagents-code-sandbox` | `scripts/agent-common.sh`, `AGENT-SELECTION.md` | `sha256:f7ad7ddc95cea260cff02d26b873903805806ccfef5d27436cbec4eba3455eff` | `sha256:94a4a004108faa93fba22ff0e24caf867514f5e2ba35de34211f81c00979de02` | linux/amd64, linux/arm64 |

The tags now name the release that each pinned index belongs to. The previous `latest` tag for vLLM does not exist on `nvcr.io`, and the floating Ollama and Node.js tags no longer resolve to the pinned images. The digest still determines what containerd pulls.

These references were already multi-platform and are unchanged: `ghcr.io/nvidia/nemoclaw/openclaw-sandbox` (pinned index, amd64 and arm64), `nvcr.io/nim/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano:latest` (tag only, index lists amd64 and arm64), `curlimages/curl:8.5.0` (Envoy probe pod), the NemoClaw sandbox base images, and the images from the pinned OpenShell 0.0.85, Envoy Gateway v1.8.3, kube-prometheus-stack 87.19.0, prometheus-adapter 5.3.0, Agent Sandbox v0.5.0, and DCGM exporter releases. No image in the recipe lacks an arm64 variant, so the chart needs no new architecture check.

Other changes:

- `scripts/build-agent-sandbox-image.sh` defaults to the architectures of the current cluster's nodes (or the host when `kubectl` cannot list nodes) instead of always `linux/amd64`, and accepts `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` for mixed clusters. `NEMOCLAW_IMAGE_PLATFORM` still overrides it.
- `README.md` documents the supported node architectures in Prerequisites and makes the minikube download architecture-aware.

## Verification

- [x] `python3 scripts/check_license_headers.py --check`: all 1020 checked source files have SPDX headers.
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_label_taxonomy.py --check`: valid, 63 labels. No governance metadata changed.
- [x] `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: no output.
- [x] Catalog: `build_catalog.py --validate-metadata` and `--check` passed (28 examples). `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` ran 74 tests OK. `node --test scripts/tests/*.test.mjs` passed 14 of 14.
- [x] Recipe checks: `bash -n scripts/*.sh` passed. `helm lint .` passed with `ingress.auth.htpasswd` set. `helm template` for `ollama`, `vllm`, and `nim` rendered the new references. The `scripts/test-*.sh`, `scripts/test-*.py`, and `scripts/test-*.ts` contract tests passed.
- [x] `docker buildx imagetools inspect` on each new digest shows an index that lists `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` and contains the old amd64 manifest.
- [x] Live test on a single linux/arm64 node with an NVIDIA GB10 GPU, using a local kind cluster with no architecture overrides. Envoy Gateway v1.8.3 and this chart used the CPU Ollama path (`gpuScaling.perPodGpu=0`, `nodeSelector`/`tolerations` cleared, `inference.model=qwen2.5:0.5b`, ServiceMonitor disabled because the cluster had no Prometheus Operator). The kubelet pulled the arm64 variants of the Ollama and Node.js indexes. With the Bearer inference API key, `POST /v1/chat/completions` returned HTTP 200 through the metrics proxy Service and through the Envoy OpenShell route. Without the key, both returned HTTP 401.
- [x] vLLM on the GPU: Docker resolved the pinned `nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.03.post1-py3@sha256:fe21f1b1…` index to its arm64 image. On the GB10 it served `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-FP8` with the chart's `vllm serve` arguments, except `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.3` because the GPU shares host memory. A chat completion with `tool_choice=auto` returned HTTP 200. This used `docker run --gpus all` because the kind node had no NVIDIA device plugin.

Not verified: the vLLM and NIM paths inside Kubernetes with a GPU device plugin on arm64, NIM on arm64 (it needs NGC credentials, and NIM selects a model profile for the GPU at startup), HPA and DCGM scaling on arm64, and `build-agent-sandbox-image.sh` against a registry. The node-architecture detection was tested in isolation.

author: swilly22
body: **Describe the changes in the pull request** 1. **Current state** — During RDB load, a graph's indexes are populated one at a time on the main thread (the v20 decoder's finalization), which serializes index construction and dominates load time for graphs with many indexed labels / relationship-types. 2. **What is the change** — - New, **default-off** `PARALLEL_INDEXING` config. When enabled, the v20 decoder populates all pending node + edge indexes **concurrently** via OpenMP instead of serially. - Each index is a disjoint RediSearch spec and the graph isn't query-visible during decode, so population uses a lock-free add (`Index_PopulateUnsafe` → `Index_Index{Node,Edge}Unsafe` → `RediSearch_SpecAddDocumentUnsafe`) under `SYNC_POLICY_NOP`; index enable/activate stay serial on the main thread. - Bumps the RediSearch submodule to the merged lock-free-add + thread-local-pools commit (FalkorDB/RediSearch#32). - The live-index path, prev decoders, and async indexer are unchanged. 3. **Outcome** — ~**4.6×** faster index construction on reload (24 indexes × 50k nodes, 11-core host), with lock contention eliminated (profiled: 57.6% → 0% mutex wait). Correct across all index types (range, fulltext, vector, edge), verified end-to-end via dump + reload. **Which issues this PR fixes** Closes #3671 **Main objects this PR modified** 1. `src/serializers/decoders/current/v20/decode_graph.c` — parallel populate loop (OpenMP, NOP matrix policy, serial enable/activate) 2. `src/index/index_construct.c`, `index_node.c`, `index_edge.c`, `index.h` — `*Unsafe` populate/add variants 3. `src/configuration/config.{c,h}` — `PARALLEL_INDEXING` option 4. `tests/flow/test_persistency.py` — parallel reload flow test 5. `deps/RediSearch` — submodule bump **Mark if applicable** - [x] This PR introduces API changes (new `PARALLEL_INDEXING` config) - [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes (RDB format unchanged) --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up RDB reload by constructing a graph's indexes concurrently during decode via a new, default-off `PARALLEL_INDEXING` config. Index construction previously ran serially on the main thread, which dominated load time for graphs with many indexed labels or relation types. - When enabled, the v20 decoder populates pending node and edge indexes on separate OpenMP threads, using a lock-free add path since each index owns a disjoint RediSearch spec and the graph isn't query-visible during decode. - The parallel path is gated to a blocking load on the Redis main thread; decodes on other threads (e.g. `GRAPH.COPY` on the cron thread) keep the serial, locked path. - Parallel workers skip the per-batch graph read lock, which otherwise resets the shared matrix-sync policy, so the caller-pinned `SYNC_POLICY_NOP` survives the region. - Index enable and activation stay serial on the main thread; the live-index path, older decoders, and async indexer are unchanged. - Bumps the `RediSearch` submodule to the merged lock-free-add and thread-local-pools commits, plus a thread-safe Chinese tokenizer init guard for parallel workers. - Adds config and persistence flow tests covering the new option, including module-arg defaults. - Closes #3671. Written for commit ec4e61a66d7d311ac829ae3884ebd688028aedff. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
### ⚡ Bolt: Optimize splash screen delay & prevent Handler leak

#### 💡 What
- Reduced hardcoded splash screen delay in `Splash_Screen.java` from 3000ms to 1000ms.
- Passed explicit `Looper.getMainLooper()` to `Handler` to resolve deprecation warnings and ensure execution on the main Looper.
- Saved `navigateRunnable` and cleaned it up in `onDestroy()` using `handler.removeCallbacks(navigateRunnable)` to prevent activity context leaks.
- Created `.jules/bolt.md` documenting performance learnings.

#### 🎯 Why
- An artificial 3-second delay on app startup severely degraded Time-to-Interactive (TTI) and user perception of performance.
- The parameterless `new Handler()` constructor is deprecated and risks leaking activity context if the user leaves the screen before the delay elapses.

#### 📊 Impact
- Reduces cold startup delay by 2000ms (66% faster transition to login/signup screen).
- Eliminates potential activity context memory leaks on early exit.

#### 🔬 Measurement
- Launching the app transitions to the `Login_Singup_page` screen after 1 second rather than 3 seconds. Verified with unit tests and `./gradlew assembleDebug`.

author: voipmonitor
body:
A server started with an API key (Flare `--api-key-file`, vLLM `--api-key`) answered lil-bench's first `/v1/models` probe with 401, so the run stopped with "The server does not answer".

```bash
lil-bench --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --api-key-file /path/to/flare-api-key
docker exec --privileged -it -e LIL_BENCH_TOKEN=lilb_... -e LIL_BENCH_API_KEY <container> lil-bench
```

- **Input:** `--api-key-file PATH` or `LIL_BENCH_API_KEY`. `--api-key VALUE` is refused, because every process list would show it.
- **Requests:** lil-bench sends `Authorization: Bearer` with its own requests (`/v1/models`, `/version`, `/metrics`, idle checks, server telemetry), never after a redirect, and hands the key to `llm_decode_bench` as `LLM_BENCH_API_KEY`, now the default of its `--api-key` (the tool-eval path passes it on as `TOOL_EVAL_API_KEY`). A missing or wrong key gets its own error panel.
- **Never uploaded:** credential values in the recorded vLLM and Flare commands and options become `***` (an `--api-key-file` path stays), lil-bench's argv masks `--token` and `--api-key`, any other copy of the key in the result or the terminal output is masked, and `llm_decode_bench`'s startup diagnostics leave out secret-named variables such as `VLLM_API_KEY`.

docker.local-inference-lab.ai already strips the same patterns on upload.

Tests: 434 passed. The new `tests/test_api_key.py` covers a local server that answers 401 without the key, redirects, redaction, and a full run whose stub benchmark echoes the key.

author: tipprb
body:
### Summary
Fixes #1337.

When processing internal shielded SPL transfers (`ext_amount == 0`), input notes are nullified and output commitments are appended without any tokens moving into or out of the asset vault (`payout = 0`, `fee = 0`).

In `paraloom-wallet` (`lib/paraloom/transactFlow.ts`), internal shielded transfers pass `ext_amount = 0` and `recipient = "00".repeat(32)` (`Pubkey::default()`).

Previously, `TransactSpl` defined both `recipient_token_account` and `fee_token_account` as `Box<InterfaceAccount<'info, TokenAccount>>` with `token::mint = mint` and `token::authority = authority` constraints:
1. When `recipient_token_account` is `Pubkey::default()` (the System Program), Anchor fails account validation before instruction execution with `AccountOwnedByWrongProgram` (3007).
2. If `#[account(mut)]` is enforced on `recipient_token_account` when `Pubkey::default()` is passed, Anchor fails with `ConstraintMut` (2000) because the System Program is executable and cannot be marked writable.
3. If the settling validator `authority` has not pre-initialized an Associated Token Account for `mint`, Anchor fails account validation with `AccountNotInitialized` (3012).

### Changes
- In `programs/paraloom/src/lib.rs`:
  - Relax `recipient_token_account` and `fee_token_account` in `TransactSpl` from `InterfaceAccount<'info, TokenAccount>` to `UncheckedAccount<'info>` without `#[account(mut)]` so `Pubkey::default()` / uninitialized accounts are accepted during internal transfers.
  - In `transact_spl`, inside `if ext_amount < 0 { ... }`: validate that both `recipient_token_account` and `fee_token_account` are writable, owned by SPL Token or Token-2022, deserialize as valid `TokenAccount`s for `mint`, and that `fee_token_account.owner == authority`.
- In `programs/paraloom/tests/transact_spl_test.rs`:
  - Added unit test `transact_spl_accepts_uninitialized_token_accounts_for_internal_transfer` verifying that internal transfers (`ext_amount == 0`) succeed past account validation when default / uninitialized accounts are passed for `recipient_token_account` and `fee_token_account`.
  - Added unit test `transact_spl_withdrawal_rejects_uninitialized_fee_token_account` verifying that external withdrawals (`ext_amount < 0`) strictly enforce valid initialized SPL token accounts.

author: peterzhu2118
body:
We use 64KB heap pages in the default GC and 12 heaps. This means that a Ractor will use at least 768KB regardless of how much it fills each heap. This is a waste of memory. Instead, we can take advantage of mmap memory and only provide OS page size so it does not cause the other OS pages to be committed.

Using this small script:

```ruby
ractors = 1_000.times.map do
  Ractor.new do
    Ractor.receive
  end
end

puts `ps -o rss= -p #{$$}`
```

On macOS, it uses 153MB of memory before and 104MB after. On Linux, it uses 346MB of memory before and 244MB of memory after.

| ![before-light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6b6202e-46ee-4f5a-8b82-932c1713cc51) | ![after-aur-light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67ab568d-4f20-4d39-b216-72f3da4ac05d) |
| ![before-dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df9b697c-f361-4ac4-b960-cb149ac6afe4) | ![after-aur-dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/399c10a7-1800-4a2d-aae7-b648d682eb44) |

## Commits

- **Updates install themselves, by Solco's rules.** The rules moved from Solco into [fastframe 0.16.1](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/releases/tag/v0.16.1)'s `fastframe_update::policy` ([crmne/fastframe#69](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/pull/69)). A downloaded release on the same major version installs at the next start, before any window opens (`update::install_kept` hands `Updater::kept` to the helper, which rolls back as for any update). The conditions: **Install updates automatically** is on (`automatic_updates` in `app.json`, on by default); the background agent is running no command (it's asked for its commands); and the person didn't go back from that version (`newest_run`). A new major version, or the switch off, waits for Restart to Update. After an update, the background agent restarts on the new version only once no command runs. Not at quit: like Solco, installing at the next start keeps the helper's start check and rollback. Package installs keep the banner with the command.

- **Notice for package installs.** Nothing is announced until fastframe-update's `Updater::verify` checks the release's `checksums.txt` signature with the compiled-in key and finds a signed, attached download of that version for this computer. `Updater::managed_update` names the package manager, the package and the command. Desktop puts that in its own words and overrides what only its releases need: `.deb` and Flatpak installs come from downloaded files, and the release's own `.rpm` gets a `dnf install <url>`. Commands only carry plain `X.Y.Z` versions and plain names, and the app never runs them. PACKAGING.md, "Updates", has the table.
- **AppImage signing** (separate commit). `packaging.yml` attaches the AppImages after `checksums.txt` is signed. A new `sign-appimages` job in `release.yml` runs after packaging. It checks the published signature, appends the AppImages' lines, signs again with the release key (in the `release-signing` environment, so it waits for the same approval as publishing), checks the AppImages against the new file, and replaces `checksums.txt` and its signature. It only runs on a stable tag, so it hasn't run yet. With it, Desktop's AppImage updates itself through fastframe-update (`appimage_name: Some("chatwithwork-desktop")`). A release without it shows the notice instead.
- **The banner.** `banner.html` runs in an app-owned child web view (`banner.rs`), with commands of its own (`banner_*`). The commands open only the links the updater holds, never one the page names. On Linux, a child web view placed after the window's last layout is now laid out right away, instead of waiting for a frame that a window on another workspace doesn't draw.
- **fastframe 0.16.0, then 0.16.1** ([0.16.0](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/releases/tag/v0.16.0), [crmne/fastframe#68](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/pull/68); [0.16.1](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/releases/tag/v0.16.1), [crmne/fastframe#69](https://github.com/crmne/fastframe/pull/69)). This moves every fastframe crate here from 0.15.4, so 0.15.5 and 0.15.6 come with it (kept downloads, libraries beside a portable app).

## Checks

On Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `mbx clippy --all-targets -D warnings` (the workspace, the app with and without `demo`, the broker), `mbx test -p cww-app` (131 passed), `mbx test -p cww-notification-broker`, `node --test app/tests/*.test.mjs` (54 passed), `python3 packaging/test-packaging.py`, and `actionlint` on `release.yml`. The screenshots come from a `--demo` build against a local feed signed with a throwaway key. Nothing was run on a Mac or on Windows, and no real update was installed at a start: the start path (`install_kept`) is covered by fastframe's tests of `kept`, `handoff` and the policy, and here by unit tests of the view and the switch. Unit tests cover their Restart to Update path, and CI covers their builds. The `sign-appimages` job has not run yet: it runs only on a tag.

author: 708san
body:
## Summary
Part of #4. Add an opt-in strict mode to the best-effort secret-like pattern scan while preserving warning-only behavior by default.

- `build(folder, out)` remains compatible; `build(..., fail_on_secret_like=True)` opts in.
- CLI adds `--fail-on-secret-like`.
- A match in strict mode raises/fails before creating the output directory or replacing either artifact.
- Diagnostics contain only the 1-based ordinal in the deduplicated referenced-asset sequence and detector category. They omit both matched bytes and asset path.
- v0.1/v0.2 manifests and package contents are unchanged.

## Verification
- Added regression tests before implementation; the strict test initially failed because the API option did not exist.
- `python -m unittest tests.test_format.FormatTests.test_package_warns_on_secret_like_referenced_asset_without_rejecting_or_disclosing tests.test_format.FormatTests.test_strict_secret_scan_fails_before_creating_or_replacing_outputs tests.test_format.FormatTests.test_strict_secret_scan_accepts_v01_and_v02_examples tests.test_format.FormatTests.test_package_cli_strict_secret_scan -v` — 4 passed.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 97 passed.
- `python -m compileall -q tools tests` — passed.
- Both validators, normal sample packaging, strict-mode v0.1 packaging, IK/runtime smoke tests, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Functional QA independently reran the focused cases and full 97-test suite — passed.
- Security Auditor found that paths could expose secret-like filenames; changed diagnostics to ordinal-only, added filename canaries, then Security Auditor rechecked and confirmed the finding resolved.
- Architect review: no format/API compatibility change beyond a keyword-only optional flag; default remains warning-only.
- Code Reviewer: no actionable findings.

## Risk and limitations
Strict mode can reject legitimate assets that match a heuristic. The scan only checks raw bytes for known patterns; transformed, encoded, pixel-embedded, and unknown secret forms can pass. It does not certify assets as secret-free. No external dependencies were added.

## Rollback
Revert this PR. The option is opt-in; the default behavior remains warning-only.

body:
## Problem

In our initial launch of `kb`, a script mistakenly removed the hash in the end of troubleshooting guides. This pattern removal was wrong, since it didn't delete several non-matching hashes, plus created discrepancies between our troubleshooting database table.

## Solution

Because we launched already, we need to make sure people with the old hash-less URLs can still access the content by manually listing these mistakes in redirects at kb level. We will remove the pattern matching from docs redirects and special redirects since they are not needed anymore thanks to this.

From now on, URLs hashes will stay as the default URL behavior.

Adapting the project to hash-less URLs would be more complicated and dangerous:
 - We would need to manually run migrations on database tables
 - Update the HEX AI script generating these hashes to actually stop or follow a stricter pattern
 - We would still run onto a potential issue by the reg ex match failing for certain pages

author: giladamar
body:
**Draft — not ready to merge as-is.** Parked here so you can re-evaluate it from a machine with working network access.

## The gap is real

Checked against the live calendar: all 41 stadium-sourced events are DHL Stadium's own bookings, and nothing athletics-related appears anywhere in the 85. It isn't a filtering bug — `api.dhlstadium.co.za` is scoped to that one venue. Green Point Athletics Stadium is a separate City facility ~400 m away with its own booking diary and no connection to that feed.

## Why this is a draft

Every candidate source was blocked by this environment's network policy — gateway 403 on CONNECT for `wpa.org.za`, `capetown.gov.za`, `quicket.co.za`, `athleticsresults.co.za`. **No parser in this PR has ever seen the page it targets.** That is exactly what CLAUDE.md convention 1 says not to trust, so rather than ship a guess, the work splits into the part that is useful regardless and the part that needs checking.

## `probe_sources.py` — the part that is useful regardless

This is the point of the branch. It answers convention 1 for every candidate in one command:

```
python3 probe_sources.py --json findings.json
```

Per source: does the host answer, where does it redirect, does it expose a WordPress REST API, does it publish schema.org Event markup, how often does it name the venue, and — the question that actually decides the design — **can a date be parsed out of what it serves?** For the WordPress candidates it runs the real venue search and prints the matched post titles alongside the dates extracted from them, flagging which would pass the materiality filter.

It also probes the options *not* wired up here — ASA fixtures, Quicket, EntryNinja, the City's event permit notices — so one run evaluates the whole option set rather than just the one I guessed at. It only reads; it writes nothing.

Paste the output back and the design decides itself.

## `athletics_stadium.py` — the speculative part

Reads the two confirmed-WordPress candidates through their REST API. Both use `?p=NNNN` permalinks, so `wp-json` is very likely exposed, and their post titles carry date and venue together — `"WPA Track & Field – 8 October 2022 – Green Point Athletics Stadium"` — which is unusually parseable. Plain-HTML fallback (JSON-LD, then text) for the City venue page.

**Off unless `ENABLE_ATHLETICS=1` or `--with-athletics`.** Merging this cannot change a single published event.

## Two judgement calls worth disagreeing with

**No computed fallback.** The obvious candidates for one — the national primary schools championships and the WP high schools championships — move host city and venue year to year. The WP meet was moved to Paarl at short notice once, *precisely because Green Point was too busy*. A calendar rule would publish confident road closures for a meet 60 km away, so per CLAUDE.md these stay scrape-only: no date read, no event published. If you'd rather have an approximate date than none, that's a reasonable call, but it's a deliberate departure from the repo's existing convention.

**A materiality filter.** The venue seats ~4,500 and runs 20–40 meets a year. A midweek club league meeting is not a traffic event, and publishing it would bury the championships that are. `is_material()` keeps championship/national/provincial/schools/grand-prix/challenger and drops league/masters/time-trial/open-meeting, checking the drop list first so "League Final" stays out. It's a name heuristic because no source publishes expected attendance — **the part most likely to be wrong**, and the probe output should settle whether meet names carry enough signal to filter this way at all. `--material-only=False` bypasses it.

## Safety

The feed is pooled into what gets published but deliberately **not** passed to `check_regression`. An unverified third-party club website must never be able to make the calendar unpublishable — that would undo the point of the fail-closed design. It is summarised as one record in `health.json` under `fetch_athletics_stadium`, so it inherits the existing `last_live` carry-forward and degradation reporting rather than needing parallel machinery. Promote it to a required source only once it has run clean for a few cycles.

New category `Green Point Track`, with `CATEGORY_PRIORITY` placing it between the stadium and the curated city events so a hand-written traffic blurb still wins on a merge.

## Testing

350 tests pass, 30 of them new: the WordPress and HTML parsers against mock payloads, the materiality filter, meet-name cleaning (the UID is hashed from the name, so a title reposted with a different editorial prefix must still resolve to one event), the health record, and — the ones that matter for merging — that the feed is off by default, and that an exploding or empty feed still produces a calendar.

## What I need from you

Run `probe_sources.py` on your desktop and paste the summary. If a candidate reads `USABLE`, I'll wire it up properly and turn the feed on. If none do, the honest answer is that no machine-readable fixture list exists, and the better move is the one no scraper gives you: email the City's venue booking office and the Events Permit Office for the season's confirmed bookings. The Permit Office already tracks approved events — it publicly reported monitoring 39 in a single week — and that route would also catch the school sports days, football and filming that no athletics source will ever carry.

author: charliermarsh
body:
## Summary

A normal Python file could import `pkgutil`, but `from pkgutil import resolve_name` failed with `module "pkgutil" has no static binding "resolve_name"`. This prevented applications from loading a callback named in their configuration:

```python
from pkgutil import resolve_name

handler = resolve_name("plugins.handlers:Handler")
```

We now expose the bundled module’s `resolve_name` through the existing object-runtime export mechanism and use CPython 3.14.5’s resolver. A colon marks the exact boundary between a module and its attributes. Without a colon, the resolver tries to import successively longer module names before looking up the remaining attributes. This matters when a package binds an attribute with the same name as a submodule.

The normal file and a separate `pkgutil.resolve_name(...)` caller matched stock at O0 and O3, including malformed names, missing modules, missing attributes and non-string arguments. The checked import regression verifies that an unrelated bad typed call is still rejected. The existing pkgutil CLI fixture now exercises both access forms. On Ruff, its isolated command compiled at O3 and hit the harness’s 60-second cap on both the parent and candidate. With the cap removed for measurement, the candidate fixture ran to completion in 143 seconds and matched stock. The nonisolated O0 control completed in 27 seconds.

All three pinned `PkgutilTests` name-resolution methods passed at both levels when run with their original bodies and fixture directories. The ordinary upstream unittest module still stops before registration because its test helper requires `_testmultiphase`.

author: clain23
body:
Refs maestra-io/issues-maestra#1649 (apk).

**Flat repositories.** A proxy whose upstream keeps `<arch>/APKINDEX.tar.gz` at its root is now served at `/apk/<name>/<arch>/{APKINDEX.tar.gz,*.apk}`. Amazon Corretto (`https://apk.corretto.aws`) is laid out this way. `thelastpickle/cassandra-reaper` (dockerfiles-bake/k8ssandra) installs its JDK from there, so its `apk upgrade` could not run through NORA (dockerfiles#78). `RepoPath` now carries the directory, `branch/repo/arch` or `arch`. Index, package and upstream paths derive from it, and every segment is validated as before. The Corretto index has an RSA (SHA-1) `.SIGN.RSA.amazoncorretto.rsa.pub` and no DESCRIPTION; it verifies with `amazoncorretto.rsa.pub` from `upstream_keys_dir`.

**Client docs.** The token now goes in `HTTP_AUTH="basic:*:token:$TOKEN"` instead of the repository URL. apk-tools 2.14.6 and older (Alpine 3.21 and older) reject a URL password over about 1 KiB as `invalid URL`, and a GitHub OIDC token is longer; this is the alpine:3.21 failure in dockerfiles#78. Verified locally against packages.maestra.io:

| Alpine | real token in `HTTP_AUTH` | 3000-char value in `HTTP_AUTH` | 2000-char URL password |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.18–3.21 | installs `jq` | sent (401) | `invalid URL` |
| 3.22–3.24 | installs `jq` | sent (401) | ok |

Tests: new `serves_a_flat_repository` (index re-signed, package served, `.x` segment 404). Local run: `cargo test -p nora-registry` 3586 passed, clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `changelog-fragments.sh --check` OK.
