author: driesmarzougui
body:
Adds the review's toy swimmer as a BRT environment, as an alternative to keeping its model inside `experiments/swimmer` (#65). The experiment (CPG, MAP-Elites searches, descriptors, figure) stays in its own repository and imports `biorobot` for the model.

## What's in it

- **`biorobot/swimmer/`**: specification (one dataclass per segment and per joint), MjSpec morphology, `FluidArena`, the `swimmer/head_first_swimming` task, a Van der Pol CPG example and a README.
  - Reward: the head's displacement along -x (head first) per step. Info: `head_first_distance` and `actuator_work` (∫Σ|τ·ω| dt, the review's energy with one physics step per control step, the default).
  - Servo targets span ±2π rad on purpose: the review's CPGs command up to ~4.9 rad, so clipping to the joint range would change the gaits.
- **Core backend check** (`biorobot/core/backend.py`): `unsupported_features(mj_model, backend)` / `check_backend_support`. Creating an environment with a backend that would silently simulate the model wrongly now raises `NotImplementedError` and names the backends that work.
  - The only entry so far: **MJX's JAX implementation ignores `fluidshape="ellipsoid"`** and applies the inertia-based fluid model instead (~13% different fluid forces for the swimmer, no warning). MuJoCo Warp supports it and matches MuJoCo C, so the swimmer runs on `"mjc"` and `"warp"`. With `fluid_model="inertia"` it also runs on `"mjx"`, but that is different physics.

## Reproducing the review's model

**The original MJCF's joint range `"-1.5 1.5"` is in degrees** (no `<compiler angle="radian"/>`), so the review's runs used ±1.5° limits that the servos push far past (joints still reach ~1.8 rad); bending is then resisted mainly by the soft limit constraint. BRT defaults to the documented ±1.5 rad; `joint_range=REVIEW_JOINT_RANGE` reproduces the original, and `test_matches_original_model` checks that it then simulates like the original XML to 1e-10.

Two things still change the review's numbers when switching to BRT:
- The original XML rounded segment lengths to 0.1 mm and stiffnesses to 1e-6 N m/rad; BRT does not round.
- BRT needs MuJoCo ≥ 3.17 (the runs used 3.8.1). On 12 random swimmers, energy and joint excursion moved < 0.1%, but slow swimmers' speeds by up to ~0.03 m/s, so the searches need a rerun.

## Testing

- `pytest -m "not slow"`: 101 passed locally (macOS, MuJoCo 3.17, Warp on CPU), including the new `tests/test_swimmer.py` (original-model parity, task, actuator work, wave direction, MJX refusal, MJX with the inertia model vs MuJoCo C, Warp vs MuJoCo C) and a core test of the backend check. The swimmer is also picked up by the Gymnasium `check_env` test.
- `black --check biorobot tests scripts` is clean.

Not included: a browser demo page for the swimmer.

author: arturobernalg
body:
Fixes #1304.

When a repository has updatePolicy=never for releases but no explicit snapshot policy (which defaults to daily), resolving metadata of nature RELEASE_OR_SNAPSHOT (version ranges, LATEST/RELEASE) merged the release and snapshot update policies into one effective policy by picking whichever had the shorter interval. "never" always lost to "daily", so every build re-fetched maven-metadata.xml for any version-ranged dependency regardless of the configured policy.

DefaultRemoteRepositoryManager.merge() already has this exact pattern for checksum policies (since 2.0.23): the stronger of the two wins by default, with a config flag to opt back into the old "weakest wins" merge. This applies the same fix to the artifact and metadata update policies, via a new UpdatePolicyAnalyzer.getStrongerUpdatePolicy() counterpart to the existing getEffectiveUpdatePolicy().

Testing: updated testGetPolicy to assert the correct ("never") outcome, which fails against the unfixed merge logic, and added three more tests mirroring the existing checksum-policy coverage (stronger-wins default, legacy opt-in flag, session override). Ran the full maven-resolver-impl test suite plus checkstyle/spotless, all green.

No backport: maven-resolver-1.9.x has a single update policy shared by both natures (no release/snapshot split), so this merge doesn't exist there.

body:
Refs #16215

## What

`CArray.list` (so `.Array`) pushes `self.AT-POS($i++)` per element; a typed CArray's `AT-POS` answers a native positional reference (`IntPosRef`/`UIntPosRef`/`NumPosRef`, a `Proxy` with built-in FETCH/STORE routines). Three costs removed:

- `auto_fetch_proxy` reads such a reference's element directly instead of dispatching FETCH through the closure-call machinery (~7.7k Ir/element).
- The straight-line method lane (#16411) binds an `Int` argument to an `int`/`int64` parameter (the `int $pos` candidate selected by `CArray.list`'s native counter); it declined every native-int parameter before.
- `native_pos_ref` interned five symbols per element; now once per process (`OnceLock`).

## Measurement

Callgrind slope, profiling build, second run, N 500 -> 1500, fill + `.Array` per element: 77.7k -> **71.0k Ir** (136.4k before #16411). The fill alone is unchanged (29.8k). The close condition of #16215 is not yet verified against the real dist (needs g++/cmake to build Sort::Fast's native lib).

## Gate

`scripts/dev gate --focus t/nativecall roast/S14-roles t/roles roast/S12-mixin roast/S09-typed-arrays`: pass. `t/nativecall/carray-straight-line-role-method.t` gained list/live-reference cases (23/23, same under `raku`).

author: milidam
body:
## Summary `export(format="tflite", int8=True, data=...)` builds the integer model twice and ships one of them. `onnx2tf -oiqt` emits `*_integer_quant.tflite` (float32 I/O) and then re-quantizes the same graph into `*_full_integer_quant.tflite` (int8 I/O); `_find_converted_tflite(int8=True)` keeps only the second. The I/O dtype does not change the calibrated scales, so the first pass is pure overhead. This PR builds the SavedModel with onnx2tf and runs a single in-process `TFLiteConverter` pass instead — the pattern `_export_tflite_rfdetr` already uses with the onnx2tf Python API. ## Changes - `libreyolo/export/tflite.py` - `_build_saved_model()` — onnx2tf `-fdosm` only, no quantization. - `_int8_representative_dataset()` — yields the loader's preprocessed images as NHWC, one per sample, dropping `CalibrationDataLoader`'s batch padding. - `_convert_saved_model_int8()` — one `TFLiteConverter.convert()`. - `export_tflite()` gains `int8_backend="converter"|"onnx2tf"` (default `"converter"`) and `int8_output_dtype="int8"|"float32"`. - `_onnx2tf_env()` — thread settings for the onnx2tf subprocess, shared with the FP32 path. - `libreyolo/export/exporter.py` — `TFLiteExporter._export` forwards the two new options; the `batch=1` comment now says why calibration cannot be batched. - `tests/unit/test_export_tflite.py` — routing, dataset shape/padding and option-forwarding tests; the three existing `-oiqt` tests now opt into `int8_backend="onnx2tf"`. ## Benchmarks `LibreYOLO9t.pt` (published weights, COCO 80 classes), 640x640, batch 1, 100 calibration images from `coco128`, evaluated on `coco-val2017-mini500` (500 images, COCO annotations) with `libreyolo val()`. | Export | Quantization passes | Wall time | mAP50-95 | mAP50 | AP-small | Size | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | FP32 | 0 | 15.4 s | 0.418 | 0.566 | 0.223 | 8.43 MB | | INT8, `int8_backend="onnx2tf"` | 2 | **23.25 min** | 0.339 | 0.491 | 0.171 | 2.53 MB | | INT8, default (this PR) | 1 | **4.49 min** | 0.336 | 0.490 | 0.168 | 2.48 MB | **5.2x faster, mAP50-95 within 0.003.** The FP32 -> INT8 drop here (-0.079) is the same size as the one in #893's published benchmark (0.442 -> 0.367, -0.075), which is a good sign both were measured on the same footing. The two INT8 artifacts have identical quantization parameters and a bit-identical score tensor; the box tensor differs by at most 8 int8 steps (mean 0.25): ``` input int8 scale 0.0039215688 zp -128 (both) scores int8 scale 0.0039145229 zp -128 (both) boxes int8 scale 0.0050643710 zp -102 (both) ``` Second data point, a 1-class 800x1280 fine-tune with 156 calibration images: 74.2 min -> 11.6 min, mAP50-95 0.625 -> 0.621. ## Reproducing ```bash python -c "from libreyolo.data import load_data_config; load_data_config('coco128.yaml', autodownload=True)" python vision_analysis_benchmark/onnx_parity.py --download-mini500 --families yolo9 --tasks detect python - <<'PY' from libreyolo import LibreYOLO m = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLO9t.pt", device="cpu") m.export(format="tflite", int8=True, imgsz=640, data="coco128.yaml", fraction=100/128, output_path="out/model_int8.tflite") PY python - <<'PY' from libreyolo import LibreYOLO print(LibreYOLO("out/model_int8.tflite").val( data="/coco-val2017-mini500.yaml", split="val", conf=0.001, iou=0.6)) PY ``` `coco128` is used for calibration rather than the mini500 yaml because that yaml points `train` and `val` at the same images; calibrating on it would mean calibrating on the evaluation set. ## Notes - Removing the duplicate pass cannot change accuracy: both passes calibrate on the same data with the same converter settings. The table confirms it empirically. - Calibration still feeds one image per sample. Yielding batches fails inside the converter (`num_input_elements != num_output_elements`), because every sample must match the model input shape — a batch-1 graph cannot calibrate in batches. That rules out the other obvious speed lever. - `int8_backend="onnx2tf"` keeps the previous route, including the onnx2tf >= 2.6.9 floor that YOLO9-E2E is validated against. - The same waste affects any project calling `onnx2tf -oiqt`; a flag to skip the float-I/O variant would fix it upstream. ## Code provenance All code in this PR is original, written for this PR against libreyolo's existing MIT-licensed codebase. No third-party code is vendored, copied or adapted. - `libreyolo/export/tflite.py` — new helpers (`_build_saved_model`, `_int8_representative_dataset`, `_convert_saved_model_int8`, `_export_tflite_int8_single_pass`, `_onnx2tf_env`) and two new options on `export_tflite()`. Two parts follow code already in this file (libreyolo, MIT): the padding-trim logic in `_int8_representative_dataset` mirrors `_write_int8_calibration_npy`, and the SavedModel-then-converter structure mirrors `_export_tflite_rfdetr`. - `libreyolo/export/exporter.py` — `TFLiteExporter._export` signature and forwarding, plus a comment. - `tests/unit/test_export_tflite.py` — new tests, using the fixtures already in that file. Third-party interaction is through public APIs only: - onnx2tf (MIT) is invoked as a subprocess with `-fdosm`, exactly as the existing FP32 path already invokes it. - TensorFlow / TFLite (`tf.lite.TFLiteConverter`, Apache-2.0) is an optional dependency this export path already requires; the patch calls its public API. The converter settings (`Optimize.DEFAULT`, `TFLITE_BUILTINS_INT8` + `SELECT_TF_OPS`, per-channel weights) deliberately mirror what onnx2tf applies for `-oiqt`, so the artifact stays equivalent — that is configuration, not copied code, and onnx2tf is MIT in any case. onnx2tf's two-pass `-oiqt` behaviour was established by reading its source; no code was copied from it. The benchmarks in this description use only public artifacts: the published `LibreYOLO9t.pt` weights, `coco128` for calibration, and `coco-val2017-mini500` for evaluation. No code, data or configuration from a private project is included.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with both previous findings addressed and no new actionable issues found.

Summary

 TFLite INT8 export now builds a SavedModel and quantizes it once. - TFLite INT8 exports finish after one quantization pass. - TFLite INT8 callers can choose the backend and output type.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[INT8 export] --> B{Backend} B -->|converter| C[Build SavedModel] C --> D[Quantize once] D --> E[Write TFLite and metadata] B -->|onnx2tf| F[Run existing quantization route] F --> G[Select full-integer artifact] G --> E ```

author: prastoin
body: Part of twentyhq/core-team-issues#3036 (row 3). Pairs with #29685 for the Lambda driver. Logic functions call Twenty through the public `SERVER_URL`. Behind an authenticating proxy (Cloudflare Access, Google IAP, oauth2-proxy) those calls carry no proxy credential and get rejected. This adds a private address for them, so their requests never cross the proxy and no proxy credential ever reaches app code. ## Changes - `SERVER_INTERNAL_URL` (env only, optional), injected into every run as the reserved `TWENTY_INTERNAL_API_URL`. Defaults to `SERVER_URL`, so nothing changes until it is set. - `resolveApiUrlFromEnvironment` in `twenty-shared/application-runtime`: internal URL if set, public otherwise. - Calls to Twenty now use it: the generated core and metadata clients, `RestApiClient` (including the `/s` fallback when no functions URL is injected), and the SDK helpers (`runAgent`, `kv`, jobs, connections, timeline, billing). - `TWENTY_API_URL`, `TWENTY_SERVER_ROUTES_URL` and `TWENTY_FUNCTIONS_URL` stay public: apps hand them to browsers and third parties, for example as webhook URLs. `getPublicAssetUrl` keeps the public URL too. - Front components never get the internal URL, so they keep calling the public one. - Docs: self-host setup, the injected variables list for app authors, reserved names. ## Rollout - The generated clients live in the server-generated SDK layer, so installed apps pick up the change when their client is regenerated (app sync, schema change). Existing archives keep the old code until then. Regenerating every app's client on upgrade is left for a follow-up. - The SDK helpers and `RestApiClient` are bundled into the app at build time, so apps need a rebuild against this SDK. Old builds keep calling the public URL, as today. ## Test plan - [x] `resolveApiUrlFromEnvironment`: internal preferred, empty falls back, nothing set - [x] Generated client default URL with and without the internal URL - [x] `RestApiClient`: internal URL for API paths and for the `/s` fallback - [x] `kv` calls the internal URL when set - [x] `tsgo` on twenty-shared, twenty-client-sdk, twenty-sdk and twenty-server; oxlint and oxfmt on changed files - [ ] On a local-driver instance: set `SERVER_INTERNAL_URL=http://localhost:3000`, run a function using the core client and check the request hits it

Validation: at base 941aa0f, the focused worker regression failed (6 failed, 11 passed); after the fix it passed (17 passed), alongside 44 worker and 37 queue-head coalescing tests. On exact head f4bb58d7, both named native PostgreSQL 18.6 regressions passed independently on fresh invocation-owned databases; both failed on baseline at the first receipt state. The database raised injected SQLSTATE 40001 after the real handler and before commit. Recovery retained the original operation and issued exactly one plan on claim two; three failures blocked with no plan, review, or grade. Replay and obsolete-token fencing passed. All five fixtures, including one initial import-path collection failure, reported verified cleanup.

A diagnostic assembled saved-review to playable-next-card run passed all 4 browser cases with verified disposable cleanup. It used this PR head’s product source with a task-only Dockerfile adjustment to include the existing local evidence-math and learning-transfer dependencies. author: bboyer4806
body:
Implements [MEA-74](https://webpyro.atlassian.net/browse/MEA-74) (2026-11-03 site review, item #28).

## What was wrong

Import recipes and Import from a link split each ingredient line with `splitIngredient` (`src/lib/ingredient-text.ts`). Three common phrasings came out wrong. Parts are amount, unit, item and prep note:

| Line | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 cloves of garlic | 2, cloves, **of garlic** | 2, cloves, garlic |
| 500g flour | no amount, item **500g flour** | 500, g, flour |
| 1/2cup sugar | no amount, item **1/2cup sugar** | 1/2, cup, sugar |
| 1 (14 oz) can diced tomatoes, drained | 1, no unit, **(14 oz) can diced tomatoes**, drained | 1, can, diced tomatoes, 14 oz, drained |
| 2 cups (212g) medium rye flour | 2, cups, **(212g) medium rye flour** | 2, cups, medium rye flour, 212g |

A CSV import has no review step, so each bad item joined the catalog and grocery suggestions, and a recipe whose amount was lost couldn't scale it.

## Change

- `src/lib/ingredient-text.ts`:
  - An "of" right after the unit is left out, in any case ("1 Cup Of milk"). Only that one: "2 cups cream of mushroom soup" keeps its item.
  - A unit written onto the amount is the unit: 500g, 1.5kg, 1/2cup, 1 1/2cups, ½cup, and a range's last amount (2-3tbsp). It's split off only when the letters are a known or common unit, so "7UP soda" stays one item, as before.
  - Text in parentheses right after the amount or right after the unit goes in the prep note, after any range and before the text after the comma.
- `docs/design.md` section 7 (Import recipes) describes the new rules, with "1 (14 oz) can of tomatoes" as an example.

## Decisions to check

**The size goes in the prep note, not the unit.** The plan allows "a prep note or the unit's size". I used the prep note in every case, so "1 (14 oz) can" is 1, can and a 14 oz note, not 1 and the unit "(14 oz) can":

- Units are capped at 20 characters, and a unit with its size, such as "(14.5 ounce) packages" (21), goes over. A CSV import refuses the whole file for one such row.
- The editor's unit field is 5rem wide, so a long unit would be cut off.
- One rule covers both cases. "2 (6 oz) salmon fillets" has no unit for the size to belong to.

The cost: the size shows after the item, as in "2 can diced tomatoes, 14 oz", and isn't scaled. That's right for a can's size, but someone could read it as the total.

**Parentheses after the unit too.** The plan names parentheses after the amount. The recipe pages in `src/lib/test-pages` put them after the unit at least as often: King Arthur's "2 cups (212g) medium rye flour" and Sally's "1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar" gave items like "(212g) medium rye flour". The same rule now covers both places. It's one line to drop if you'd rather keep to the plan.

**No list of new items before importing.** The plan says to consider listing the new item names in the import's confirmation step. The only such step today is for recipes already in Recipes, so this would add a step to every import that has new items. On a household's first import, that's every item in the file. I left it out; it could be its own ticket.

## Assumptions

- Anything in parentheses in those two places goes in the prep note, not only sizes: "2 cups (packed) brown sugar" gets the note "packed". Checking for a number first would leave those in the item.
- "of" is dropped only after a unit. With no unit, as in "2 of the eggs", it stays in the item.
- "2 cups of" alone is 2 cups with no item, which the import reports as needing an item, instead of an item called "of".
- The Import recipes help is unchanged. It describes the format to write, and these rules read more ways of writing it.

## Not changed

Two phrasings in the same test pages still split badly. Both are outside this ticket:

- "1 and 1/3 cup (167g) all-purpose flour" (Sally's) reads 1 as the amount and the rest as the item.
- Parentheses after the item, such as "⅓ cup soy sauce ((80ml))" (Preppy Kitchen), stay in the item. MEA-40 covers the item and prep note split.

## Tests

- `src/lib/ingredient-text.spec.ts`, three new tests: "of" after the unit; a unit written onto an amount or a range, with "7UP soda" untouched; and parentheses after the amount, with and without a unit, and after the unit.
- Updated expectations that recorded the old split: allrecipes' "2 (12 inch) pre-baked pizza crusts" in `src/lib/recipe-schema.spec.ts`, and King Arthur's "2 cups (212g) medium rye flour" there and in `src/routes/(app)/recipes/new/page.server.spec.ts`.
- By hand: 10,000-character lines built to make the new patterns backtrack (long digit runs, open parentheses, repeated "of") each split in under 2 ms.

author: cpcloud
body:
## TL;DR

Forge left some squash merges uncounted even though the squash held exactly the pull request's code: stacked pull requests, and pull requests that got one more push after the merge. Landed-work analysis now credits such a squash when its files prove it.

Benefit: user-facing. More merged pull requests count toward landed work.

## Why

Forge credits a squash to its pull request only when GitHub's commit list for the pull request covers every commit between the squash parent and the pull request head. Two shapes fail that check:

- **Stacked pull requests.** Each branch merges its parent branch, and GitHub lists far fewer commits than the branch holds. The result was `source_incomplete`.
- **A push after the merge.** The head moved past the commit that was squashed. The branch also holds a merge, so the existing tolerance for this race, which needs a linear branch, did not apply. The result was `source_correspondence_unproven`.

## How

When the commit list does not prove a squash of a branch that holds merges, Forge checks the files instead. The squash counts when its tree is exactly the clean three-way merge of the pull request head, or of a listed commit, onto the squash parent:

```
git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<base.sha> <squash>^ <commit>   # must equal <squash>^{tree}
```

The merge base is GitHub's `base.sha`. Forge already read it for long commit lists and now passes it to the analysis. For a stacked pull request it is the parent pull request's head, and the plain merge base conflicts there. Without a usable `base.sha`, Forge uses the merge base of the squash parent and the commit, and requires that base to be unique.

## Reviewer notes

- **Unproven stays unproven.** A conflict, a squash with different files, or an empty squash keeps the reason it has today.
- **Rebase guard kept.** A squash that could be the last commit of a longer rebase stays unproven, as the existing witness rule requires. When the list omits commits, the guard also checks the omitted commits the head reaches past the squash parent and the reported base. A complete list adds no extra Git calls.
- **Linear branches unchanged.** A linear branch can also be a rebase, and its existing listed-part tolerance already decides it.
- **Two existing expectations change.** A squash of a branch with merges whose list omits a commit now counts, because its files prove it. The matching `source_incomplete` case left `TestSquashRequiresSourceChain`; the new stacked test covers that reason.
- **Cost grows with the list.** A failed check tries each listed commit, newest first. Each try counts against the analysis node limit.
- Phillip approved this rule on 2026-11-04; `context/provider-architecture.md` records it. No user doc describes which squashes Forge can prove.

## Tests

Synthetic Git fixtures cover both shapes, for an explicit squash method and automatic detection. Each acceptance case fails without the change. Negative cases: an extra file in the squash, a stack without `base.sha`, and a `base.sha` missing locally.

## Issue

`no-jira`

## Description

After the release deploy to the Azure feed, `job-publish-release` promotes the released modules to the feed's `public` view. Customers get read access to that view only, so it holds what used to go to Maven Central: modules deployed to the feed that carry no zip (a view holds whole package versions, so a plugin would expose its distribution zip). The repository visibility is checked first, and snapshots are never promoted.

- `.circleci/scripts/promote-to-view.sh`: copy of the script of the gravitee orb (6.13.0), which APIM does not use for its releases. It checks every promoted module through the view and fails on any error.

**Security-sensitive:** the job now exports `GITHUB_TOKEN` (same Keeper record as the Helm release job) and uses the Azure Artifacts token to promote packages.

## Additional context

The script is covered by shellcheck and bats in the orb repository, and was run against the real feed on several repositories, including a dry run on `core_4.13.7`. Customer access to the view is closed until guest access is enabled in the Azure DevOps organization.

author: kaeawc
body:
## What was wrong

On an Android Automotive device the driver is usually user 10 and the system user 0 is headless. `installApp` resolved the running primary user, so a fresh install landed on user 0. `launchApp` then targets the foreground user and reports the app as not installed. [#16881](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/16881) (part of [#14915](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/14915)).

## What changed

`InstallApp.prepareAndroidInstall` passes `currentUser: true` to `AndroidUserTargetResolver` on automotive devices, so the foreground user (`am get-current-user`) is the target. An explicit `userId` still wins. Other form factors issue the same adb commands as before.

Choice to review: on automotive, `currentUser` also skips the installed-user preference, so a reinstall of an app installed only for a non-foreground user now installs for the foreground user. An unreadable current user falls back to the primary user.

## Tests

- `test/features/action/InstallApp.test.ts`: five fake-based cases (automotive install targets user 10, current user 0 honoured, unreadable output falls back to user 0, explicit userId 0 wins, non-automotive never reads the current user). The automotive install case fails without the fix.
- `bun test` on both changed suites: 171 pass, 0 fail.
- `scripts/prepush-node.sh --changed`: passed.

## Device evidence

Verified on an `android-34-ext9` `android-automotive` arm64 emulator (serial `emulator-5620`, driver user 10 foreground, headless system user 0), commit `bc7236ba8d8`:

- Before the fix: `installApp` returned `userId: 0`; `pm list packages --user 10` showed the probe package absent.
- After the fix: `installApp` returned `userId: 10`; the package was installed for user 10 only.
- `launchApp` with the fix targeted user 10 with no "not installed" error. The process ran as `u10`, and the activity was resumed on user 10 (`topResumedActivity`).

Not verified on a device:

- `launchApp` returned `success: false` with "Timed out waiting for launch observation" even though the probe was foreground on user 10. This is a launch-observation result, not an install result, and it is not addressed by this PR. It needs a separate look.
- A real AAOS app (the one from the issue) was not used; the test APK was a minimal signed probe.
- iOS is not touched.

Because the launch-foreground acceptance is still open, this PR uses `Part of`.

author: cline-cloud[bot]
body:
## Contexto

Segunda etapa DSV4. Auditoria SEO/AEO/GEO de 04/11/2026, reconciliada contra
`origin/main` (`9a9c43c3`) e contra o que `https://filtraai.com` realmente serve.

Reconciliação (evidência):

- `[LOCAL]` = `[MAIN]` = `9a9c43c3` (working tree limpo, 0/0 de divergência).
- `[DEPLOY]` = produção Render `9a9c43c3` (deployment GitHub `Production`).
- `[PROD]` = apex `filtraai.com` → Cloudflare → Render (`x-render-origin-server: Render`);
  `www.filtraai.com` → Vercel, 301 direto para o apex. `/indice` sai do serviço
  do Índice via Worker; o front Next não serve essa rota.

## Problemas confirmados em produção

1. **P0 — `html lang` errado no HTML inicial.** `/en`, `/es` e `/zh` entregavam
   `<html lang="pt-BR">`. A origem: `scripts/fix-static-html-lang.mjs` só rodava
   com `CLOUDFLARE_PAGES=1` (export estático). O Render roda `next start`, então
   o passe era *skipped* e o idioma ficava para o script inline — invisível para
   crawler sem JS.
2. **P0 — `Cache-Control: s-maxage=31536000` no HTML.** Padrão do Next para
   página pré-renderizada. Com Cloudflare na frente, uma cópia em cache
   compartilhado ficaria até um ano e o deploy seguinte não apareceria.

## O que mudou

- `frontend/scripts/fix-static-html-lang.mjs`: passa a reescrever também o HTML
  pré-renderizado em `.next/server/app/` (o artefato que o `next start` envia).
- `frontend/scripts/validate-html-language.mjs`: guardrail valida o mesmo
  artefato publicado, nos dois modos, e cobre `/`, `/en`, `/es`, `/zh` e páginas
  localizadas internas.
- `frontend/next.config.mjs`: HTML com `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`;
  `/_next/static/*` mantém `max-age=31536000, immutable`; `/api/*` privado e
  `no-store`; `/sw.js` e `/manifest.webmanifest` preservam suas políticas.
- `frontend/scripts/verify-production-seo.mjs`: o gate de produção agora reprova
  `html lang` divergente e HTML com `s-maxage` longo.

## Não alterado (de propósito)

- `/zh` continua `noindex` e fora do `sitemap.xml`/hreflang — política já
  coerente em código e em produção (GSC: `/zh` = "blocked by meta tag", NEUTRAL).
- `llms*.txt`, copy comercial e alegações sobre Google Business Profile já
  estavam corretas em `main`/produção (commit `6a418181`); nada refeito.
- `/indice` já tem quality gate por dados (`minimoParaIndexar` → `notFound()`).

## Testes executados

| Comando | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` (Render, sem flag) | PASS — `.next/server/app/` 158 arquivos, 88 corrigidos, guardrail PASS |
| `CLOUDFLARE_PAGES=1 npm run build` (CI) | PASS — `out/` 159 arquivos, 87 corrigidos, guardrail PASS |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | PASS |
| `npx eslint .` | 0 erros (107 warnings preexistentes) |
| `node scripts/validate-seo.mjs` | PASS |
| `npm run seo:audit` | PASS (107 URLs) |
| `node scripts/test-seo-jsonld-global.mjs` | PASS |
| `next start` local: matriz de headers | HTML revalida; `_next/static` imutável; `/api/*` no-store |

## Verificação esperada após deploy

`node scripts/verify-production-seo.mjs` deve passar, e manualmente:

- `/`, `/en`, `/es`, `/zh` → `html lang` = `pt-BR`, `en`, `es`, `zh`.
- HTML → `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`.
- `/_next/static/*.css` → `max-age=31536000, immutable`.

## Riscos

- O HTML passa a exigir revalidação em todo cache compartilhado: é o
  comportamento pretendido (hoje o Cloudflare responde `cf-cache-status:
  DYNAMIC`, então não há ganho de cache sendo perdido).
- `/sitemap.xml` e `/robots.txt` deixam de sair como `no-store` e passam a
  revalidar (`max-age=0, must-revalidate`). Continua sem risco de versão
  obsoleta e reduz carga na origem.

author: wittywilla
body:
Closes wittywilla/WittyReader#9

## What changed

- **Pages for PDFs and comics.** Their readers save the page on screen (plus how far down it, for a PDF), so the library now counts that page as read: page 6 of 6 is 100% and finished, and page 7 of 117 is 6%, as the reader's own bar says.
- **Words for books.** The EPUB reader's percentage counts words, and the library counted chapters (9% against 15%). The word counts per chapter are kept on the book when it's opened (`words` on the record), and the library uses them the same way. A book is finished in its last chapter with 98% of its words read, because a reader's last page starts a little before the end. A book of pictures (no words) counts pages, and a book not opened since this change keeps the old estimate, capped at 99%, until it's opened again.
- **No lost saves.** `books.patch` read a record in one transaction and wrote it in another, so opening a book and its first saved position could overwrite each other. *First Woman 1* lost its "opened" time this way while testing. It's now one transaction, and a book with a saved position counts as opened even if that was lost.

## How it was tested

- `npx tsc -b` and `npm run build`: clean.
- The built app on `http://reader.localhost:5193`, with a library made before this change:
  - *Pepper&Carrot 1*, read to page 6 of 6 before: now shows the *Finished* tick (it said 83%).
  - *Pride and Prejudice* at chapter VIII: the reader says 9%, the library now says 9% (it said 15%). Then Contents → *Uncopyright*, to the last page: the reader says 100%, the library shows *Finished* and *Continue reading* moves on to the next book.
  - *Apollo* at page 7 of 117: 6% in both.
  - *First Woman 1*, whose "opened" time had been lost: shows 33% (page 5 of 15) instead of *New*.

## After the code review

- A book is finished in its last chapter once less than about two pages' worth of words (600) are left, instead of at 98% of the book, which a long last chapter could keep out of reach.
- A book whose opened time was lost can still be the one to *Continue reading*.
- Left as they are: progress is worked out several times per render (only matters for very large libraries), and could be stored when it's saved instead of derived.

## Not tried for real

- The desktop app, and browsers other than Chromium. Nothing here depends on either.

## Version and changelog

Changelog and version are in the milestone's version pull request, so these pull requests don't conflict.

author: cotswoldsmaker
body:
Owl's log reader is called Owl in Terraform too. Terraform renames its four resources in the state, so nothing in Google Cloud is destroyed or made again. This is Phase 2 of the [alert watcher is called Owl plan](https://github.com/bailey-medics/quillmedical/blob/main/docs/docs/plans/2026-11-04-the-alert-watcher-is-called-owl-plan.md).

**Size:** small. One Terraform file, renamed, and a certificate authority file moved with it. It changes how App production is reached, which is why it needs care.
**Look hardest at:** the Terraform plan comment on this pull request. It must show four moves and some description changes, and no destroy.
**Check for me:** that the plan shows no destroy before this merges.

## Decisions to check

- **Google Cloud keeps its IDs.** The service account stays `alert-watcher-logs`, the workload identity pool stays `alert-watcher`, and the certificate's subject stays `quill-alert-watcher`. A new account ID would mean a new account email. A deleted pool's ID cannot be used again for 30 days. A new subject would mean issuing a new certificate.
- **The `import` blocks stay, pointed at the new addresses.** They first adopted the pool and its provider. The resources are already in the state, so the blocks do nothing now.

## Risks

- **A wrong path to the certificate authority would destroy the pool.** The pool's `count` checks that `infra/environments/app/owl-ca.pem` exists. If the path were wrong, the plan would show the pool and its provider destroyed. That is why the plan comment matters.
- **A missing `moved` block would replace a resource.** Each of the four has one, and `terraform validate` passes.

## What has changed

- **`infra/alert-watcher.tf` is now `infra/owl.tf`.** Its resources are `owl_logs`, `owl`, `owl_x509` and `owl_certificate_acts_as_log_reader`.
- **The display names and descriptions say Owl.** Google Cloud changes these in place.
- **The certificate authority is `owl-ca.pem`.** It is the same file, under a new name.

author: odaiameera
body:
## What was wrong

Scheduled agent jobs had three problems with their Telegram reports, and the screenshots show the cause of a fourth:

1. **Cut off mid-message.** `runner.ts` cut the agent's answer to 1,500 characters (`turn.message.slice(0, 1500)`), so the newsletter summary stopped at "Here's Wh".
2. **Markdown shown raw.** The agent is told to write Markdown. The runner escaped it as plain text and sent it in Telegram's HTML mode, so `**bold**` and backticks showed as literal characters.
3. **"Silent" jobs weren't silent.** The runner always sent the agent's final reply, and the agent didn't know that. The hourly Elaine watch wrote "So I didn't send a Telegram message", and that sentence was itself the Telegram message.
4. **No current time.** The agent was told the date but not the time. At 23:01 it tried a reminder for 22:15, then 22:30, and both were refused as past. It was using `remind_me` to deliver its own report, because it didn't know its reply goes to Telegram.

## The fix

- **`telegram/format.ts` (new):** converts Markdown into Telegram HTML (b, i, s, code, pre, blockquote). Lists get • or their own numbers, headings become bold, and tables become lines. Text from the model never passes through as HTML. Raw tags are escaped, and a link shows its address (`your bank (https://…)`) instead of hiding it. Long reports are packed into messages that fit Telegram's limit, split between paragraphs and list items, with at most 5 messages; the last one says if the report was cut.
- **`jobs/runner.ts`:** sends the whole answer through the converter, then lists the changes one per line as plain text. The digest's summary is read as Markdown, but the fallback list of senders and subjects stays plain text. If the first message is delivered and a later one fails, the failure is logged (`report_cut`) and the report counts as sent.
- **`stay_quiet` tool:** offered only to jobs. When the agent calls it, nothing is sent, and the agent's answer is kept as the job's last result in Settings → Agent ("Nothing sent: …").
- **`runtime.ts`:** the per-request system block now gives the local time. For jobs it also says that the final reply is the report, that a reminder should never be used to deliver it, and when to call `stay_quiet`. The cached system block is unchanged.
- **Reminders** are converted from Markdown the same way.
- README and roadmap updated.

## Tests

- New `format.test.ts` covering formatting, escaping, links, quotes, tables, packing and the cut note.
- Job tests: full report over several messages, Markdown output, changes on one line, partial delivery, quiet runs, and digest Markdown vs plain list.
- Runtime tests: the time on the user's clock, the job-only note, and `stay_quiet` offered to jobs only.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/server src/routes/api`: 761 passed. `eslint .` and `tsc` are clean.
- In the sandbox, three component test files fail to load because the `xlsx` tarball from cdn.sheetjs.com is blocked. They don't touch this change.

Out of scope here: Revolut emails rendering blank in the reading view. That's for a separate issue.

body:
## What

Backfills the 2026/27 predictions that Mistral-Ministral and Nvidia-Nemotron-Lightning missed before their first live run on 14.10.2026. The backfill goes to the Blob archive only, never to KV, so backtests can compare all providers on the same matches. Implements the 01.11.2026 story (it lives in the gitignored `docs/` folder).

### Changes

- **Shared prompt**: `lib/api_data.build_odds_summary` (and `prediction_columns`) are now used by both `OddsAPI.process_api_data` and the backfill. Unit tests check that the prompt is byte-identical to the live one, including a literal guard on the existing format.
- **`sport_titles`** in `cfg/api_config.yaml`: maps our league names to the Odds API `sport_title` (`EPL` etc.). Values were checked against the stored `data/api_result` responses. The live workflow keeps taking the title from the API response.
- **`lib/blob_archive.py`**:
  - New path `predictions/backfill/<run_ts>_<base_key>.jsonl`.
  - Each line carries a `"backfill": {"generated_at", "odds_source": logged|reconstructed|mixed, "script"}` marker.
  - Files are listed under `index.json` → `backfill_predictions` (`{run_ts: {provider_key: path}}`), separate from `runs`.
  - New helpers `merge_backfill_index` / `update_backfill_index` and `BlobArchiveReader.backfill_predictions()`. Live `merge_index` keeps that key.
- **`utils/backfill_llm_predictions.py`**:
  - Rebuilds each original run from the other providers' archived prediction files (index read fresh).
  - Each fixture goes to the latest run that offered it before kickoff, if that run came before the provider's first live run. Fixtures the provider missed live are only counted.
  - Odds come from the run's odds files (`logged`), else from the newest archived reconstructed CSV (`--odds-csv` for a local one).
  - Predictions go through `TipGenius.predict_results`.
  - `--dry-run` is the default; `--execute` and `--max-calls` (stops at the first file over the limit).
  - Resumable: indexed files are skipped, and an existing file that is not indexed only gets indexed. A failed HEAD skips the file instead of paying for it twice.
  - Refuses to run, and stops between files, on Tue/Fri 02:00–17:00 UTC.
  - A file cut short by a provider outage is not written, so a re-run can complete it.
- **`utils/eval_providers.py --include-backfill`**: separate "incl. backfill" tables (season, per league, head-to-head). The live ranking never includes backfill predictions.
- **`backfill_blob_archive.py --rebuild-index`**: also restores `backfill_predictions` from a `list` of `predictions/backfill/`.
- **AGENTS.md**: utils table row; Blob layout and index docs.

## Dry run (04.11.2026, read-only, no LLM calls, nothing written)

- 213 fixtures per provider: La Liga 79, Premier League 60, Bundesliga 45, Champions League 29. This matches the story.
- They spread over 13 original runs (14.08.–13.10.2026).
- LLM calls per provider: 213 fixtures, i.e. 213 to 852 requests including retries (426 to 1,704 for both).
- Odds: all 213 come from the reconstructed CSV (no logged odds exist for those runs). No fixture lacks odds; none were missed live.
- Writes after `--execute`: 26 files plus one verified index update per run (~27–35 advanced ops incl. read-back retries).

## Known limitation

A backfilled entry keeps the kickoff the original run offered. In the real data that differs from the final kickoff only for 2 CL matches, by 1 minute (14.10. 18:45 vs 18:46).

## Not done

- `--execute` has not been run. Nothing was written to Blob or KV.
- `eval_providers --include-backfill` was run against the real data: it finds 0 backfill files for now, so its tables equal the live ones until the backfill runs.

## Checks

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check src/`, `pyright` (0 errors), `pytest tests/unit` (97 passed), prettier on the YAML. Review rounds: round 1 had 9 findings (8 fixed, 1 skipped: sharing time helpers across utils scripts); round 2 had 1 fixed (partial file after an outage) and 1 skipped (a second HEAD helper); round 3 found nothing new.


## Index update hardening (added after review)

A fresh `index.json` read was seen to lag behind a recent write (04.11.2026; cause unconfirmed). Changes to handle that:

- `update_backfill_index(entries, expected=...)` refuses an index that lacks files the run saw at its start, so a stale read is never written back. It reads the index back after the put and re-merges, up to 4 attempts with 30 s waits, and logs a WARNING if it still cannot verify.
- The script now writes the index once per run, in a `finally` block, so files written before a crash or Ctrl-C still get indexed.
- Files whose index update cannot be verified are reported as `unindexed`; the next run indexes them without new LLM calls.
- Unit tests cover the stale read, the read-back miss, the bounded give-up and the crash safety net.
- The live workflow's `update_index` is unchanged (see the open question below).

## Open question for Tom

`update_index`, used by the live workflow's `finalize_blob_archive` and by `backfill_blob_archive.py`, has the same stale-read risk. If its fresh read returns an older index, the merge overwrites `index.json` without the newer runs, and only `--rebuild-index` gets them back. It could use the same guard (expected pathnames plus read-back). Left out of this PR on purpose.


## Final review (04.11.2026)

- Fixed: the download cache writes via a temp file plus rename, so an interrupted run never leaves a truncated cached file.
- Fixed: `eval_providers --include-backfill` reads `index.json` fresh, so it sees a backfill that has just run.
- Accepted: a file is still written when some of its fixtures fail validation (same as the live workflow). Those fixtures are listed as failed and are not retried by a re-run.
- Accepted: the stale-read guard only covers reads older than the script's own start read. Don't start `--execute` right after another index write.
- Follow-up (separate PR): the same verified update for the live `update_index`.

author: jjuraszek
body:
## Summary
The pi fix wave in gatekeep-pr now hands each selected file finding to the autonomous `loop-implementer` as one companion-ledger row (one row per blocker, one batched row for `fix nits`) instead of a plan-bound `implementer` applying a pre-drafted edit. Before, a worker told "apply this payload, never re-solve the finding" had no way to pick a different fix when the drafted edit failed its scoped test; now the row's evidence pack is the task, the worker runs its own check, and a reviewer `open` closure line reopens the row with that reason as its prior-failure evidence for the next attempt.
- Retries are bounded by `loopEngine.maxIterationsPerRow` per row and the existing `2 x closureReview.maxFixRounds` round cap, whichever hits first; the escalated-model attempt fires once at the clamped threshold, and the verify-session phase-tracker guards count `loop-implementer` like `implementer`.
- The ledger and its derived spec live beside the run's continuation record, never in the PR branch; description-target and reply payloads keep their current path; sync conflict-stop and base-merge helpers stay on `implementer`; Claude Code keeps the native drafted-payload helper on a shared context block that differs from the pi row task only in its solve/commit tail.
- Hotfix (`skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md`) and `agents/loop-implementer.md` are byte-identical to `main`; prior-review ancestry is unchanged; multi-PR batch mode keeps its admission and queue, carries the ledger and derived-spec paths through the private handoff, and names `loop-implementer` as the execute child's file-finding worker. Spec: `doc/specs/2026-11-04-gatekeep-fix-loop-engine.md`; docs in `doc/implement-engines.md`, `doc/configuration.md`, `doc/personas.md`.
- Verification: scoped - `node --test scripts/gatekeep-fix-loop-contract.test.mjs`; `node eval/run.mjs gatekeep-pr nit-batch-row`; `node --experimental-loader ./extensions/test-support/pi-stubs.mjs --test scripts/gatekeep-fix-loop-contract.test.mjs extensions/phase-tracker.test.ts`; `node eval/run.mjs gatekeep-pr loop-worker`; `git diff --exit-code 5cfd9d35 -- agents/loop-implementer.md skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md`; `node eval/run.mjs gatekeep-pr prior-review-delta`; CI on this push holds the full run

## Test Plan
- [ ] CI (`npm test`) green on this push
- [ ] Run `gatekeep-pr` on a PR with at least one blocker and pick `deliver`: the fix wave dispatches `loop-implementer` with `target: <row>` and commits `loop: row <n> done` on the PR branch
- [ ] Leave one finding open at the reviewer pass and confirm the row reopens with the reviewer's reason and is retried next round
- [ ] Pick `fix nits` and confirm all selected nits land as one row with one commit

author: mattrobinsonsre
body:
`tofu output` and `terraform output` exit 1 against any `cloud {}` workspace:

```
Error: could not read state version outputs: resource not found
```

`GetRootOutputValues` reads `ReadCurrent` and has **no fallback on error**, so
the command fails outright rather than degrading to the full state. Two routes
were unserved, and `docs/tfe-cli-surface.md` did not catalogue them at all —
found by the #2368 survey.

The data was already served natively at
`GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/state-outputs`. Only the TFE-shaped door was
missing.

## Two routes, two tiers — that split is the design

`go-tfe`'s own flow is: `ReadCurrent` for the collection, then `Read` once per
output that came back **sensitive**. So:

| route | gate | sensitive values |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /workspaces/{id}/current-state-version-outputs` | `state:read-metadata` (**read** tier) | omitted |
| `GET /state-version-outputs/{output_id}` | `state:read` (**plan** tier) | revealed |

Gating the collection on `state:read` instead would have 403'd `tofu output`
for every read-only user, *including* on workspaces whose outputs are not
secret at all. This way a read-tier user gets a working `tofu output` and meets
a refusal only on an output that genuinely is sensitive. The reveal being
state-grade is `plan_json_output`'s reasoning (GHSA-gwwq-5v7q-h3f4).

A sensitive value is **omitted** from the collection rather than masked with a
placeholder: `go-tfe` types `value` as `any`, so a placeholder is
indistinguishable from a real value to a client — and the CLI never reads one
from there anyway.

The collection honours the runner allowlist (#344) that the sibling
`current-state-version` route does. A run already permitted to read a
producer's *whole state* may certainly read its outputs, and refusing while the
adjacent route allows it would be inconsistent in the strict direction with
nothing to explain it. The per-output route has no such path, deliberately:
whole state is what `terraform_remote_state` reads, through its own route.

## A second reader, not a change to the first

`state_graph_service.terraform_outputs` masks into the literal `"(sensitive)"`
and discards both the cty type **and** the per-output `sensitive` boolean.
`web/src/components/stack-outputs-panel.tsx` matches that literal and its
header states a sensitive value never reaches the browser — so it is untouched.

`typed_terraform_outputs` sits beside it, and `load_state_document` is now the
one path both take through storage → decryption → parse. `json.loads` runs in a
thread: a state document is routinely tens of MB (principle 13).

## Measured against a real state file, because two guesses were wrong

Both would have shipped silently:

- **`sensitive` is ABSENT, not `false`,** on a non-sensitive output. Assuming
  the key would have raised `KeyError` on every ordinary output.
- **An HCL list literal is recorded as `["tuple", [...]]`,** not
  `["list","string"]`, and a map literal as `["object", {...}]`. So the coarse
  `type` folds tuple/list/set → `array` and object/map → `object`. Getting that
  wrong yields a `detailed-type` the CLI cannot parse, which sends it down its
  full-state fallback rather than failing visibly.

Every output carries a non-nil `detailed-type` for the same reason: a nil on
**any** one makes `GetRootOutputValues` abandon the whole path, so a stubbed or
empty document would report *no* outputs — worse than today's clean failure.

## The synthesised id

`wsout-{state-version-id}:{name}`, because outputs are re-derived from the blob
on every read and no row exists. `list_workspace_tag_bindings` is the precedent
for synthesising one at all — go-tfe's parser silently drops an entry with no
id, which here would make the CLI conclude the workspace has none — and this is
a genuine *extension* of it, because that id is only ever emitted while this one
round-trips. So it is parsed through `parse_id`, never a bare `uuid.UUID` on
request input (`test_id_prefix_tolerance.py` AST-checks for that), and with
`partition` rather than `split` so a name containing a colon is not silently
truncated into a different output.

## Also: `resources-processed`

`true`, as a constant, on the state-version document. It is the honest value:
TFE indexes resources asynchronously and Terrapod has no such phase. Without it
`tfci workspace output list` polls its entire five-minute budget waiting for a
`true` that never arrives. The `resource_count` column cannot source it — NULL
for every Terraform version.

## TFE-only, not dual-mounted

The document carries a cty type, and a Pulumi stack's outputs have none — so
dual-mounting would either lie or emit the nil `detailed-type` described above.
The native `/api/v1/.../state-outputs` already serves every engine, so no door
is missing. Same reasoning that keeps the state-version *writes* TFE-only.

## Verification

Six mutations, each killed by the test named for it, with an unmutated control:

| mutation | killed by |
|---|---|
| reveal sensitive values on the collection | `test_a_sensitive_value_is_omitted_from_the_collection` |
| gate the collection at the plan tier | `test_a_read_tier_user_gets_the_collection` |
| drop the runner allowlist path | `test_an_allowlisted_runner_is_admitted_without_workspace_caps` |
| drop the per-output gate | `test_the_revealing_route_needs_state_read` |
| assume `sensitive` is present | `test_a_non_sensitive_output_has_no_sensitive_key` |
| fold a tuple to `object` | `test_a_tuple_folds_to_array` |

The runner mutation had to be located by **AST**, not a string anchor: the
sibling route's allowlist block is byte-identical, so a text anchor matched
twice and would have mutated the wrong route.

Snapshots: **+4 routes, +1 attribute set, +1 attribute, no removals.**

venv suite: 134 passed across the new tests plus `test_ids.py`,
`test_id_prefix_tolerance.py`, `test_tfe_prefix.py` and both contract tests.
PR CI is the gate.

Closes #2376

---

## Added after the first push: a CLI-contract check

The six mutations above cover the routes. None of them drives the **binary**,
and the binary is the one consumer that cannot be fixed forward -- so
`scripts/cli-contract/run.py` gains
`[State Versions] output reads the state-version outputs`.

The suite already applied a configuration carrying an `output`, and read
outputs out of the state document rather than asking the CLI for them. That is
exactly why nothing noticed `tofu output` was exit 1.

One check covers both routes, because that is how `go-tfe` behaves: it reads
the collection, then fetches each output it was told is sensitive through the
per-output route. A reveal route that refused fails this; an API test asserting
the collection alone would not. It also pins `type`, since a nil
`detailed-type` on any one output makes the CLI abandon the path and fall back
to the full state -- a silent degradation rather than a failure. The
collection's own half (a sensitive value is **omitted**) is asserted through
`ctx.api`, since the CLI cannot show you what it was not given.

The fixture gains a sensitive output derived from the **variable** rather than
the resource, and the live run is what caught that: the `import` check drives
the same configuration in a directory with no applied state, where
`terraform_data.probe.output` is null and interpolating it is a hard error, so
the first version broke a neighbouring check.

**Verified against a live stack: 10 of 10 checks pass**, the new one in 0.5s.

author: camiloazula
body:
The shell guard now judges what several archivers and compressors write and delete that it used to miss.

- `pixz`, `bzip3` and `zopfli` are read from their own source: what each writes (the suffix it adds, a second operand, `-o`), and whether it deletes its input (`pixz` unless `-k`, `bzip3` only with `--rm`, `zopfli` never). The compressor spec now holds per program what used to be fixed: the compress and decompress letters, whether `-c` writes to the screen, the recursive and multiple options, renames, formats and the second-operand rules. In every compressor, the file `-o` names is now judged in test or list mode too.
- Windows' own `compress` (cmd and PowerShell, `compress.exe`) writes its last operand, or with one operand the renamed file beside it (`x.dll` becomes `x.dl_`).
- `arepack`, and `atool -r`/`--repack`, write the second operand (every operand with `-e`), so they are no longer read as writing nothing.
- PowerShell: .NET's `CreateFromDirectory`/`CreateFromDirectoryAsync` (ZipFile, TarFile, or a type held in a variable) is judged as a `Compress-Archive -Path <folder> -DestinationPath <archive>`. `ZipFile::Open`/`OpenAsync` reads its first argument in every mode and writes it unless the mode is written out as Read. ZipFile and ZipArchiveMode are known only by their full name, or its end after a dot.

The same commands aimed inside the workspace stay Safe. docs/design/shell.md and the case files (`compressors.cases`, `archives.cases`) are updated.

Fixes #253

## Review

The review (posted below as a comment) found one blocker and three minor points.

- Fixed, blocker: `[IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open("$HOME\.ssh\id_rsa", 'Read')` had become Safe, where main flagged it. `Open`/`OpenAsync` now judges a read of its first argument in every mode, plus a write for Create or Update, so a credential opened with `Open` is `read_secret`, as with `OpenRead`.
- Fixed, minor: the type is matched by full name, so `[Evil.ZipFile]`, `[Evil.MyZipFile]` and `[Evil.ZipArchiveMode]::Read` are findings.
- Fixed, minor: `zopfli` does not end options at `--`, as its own source shows.
- Fixed, minor: `CreateFromDirectory` also judges the folder it reads, so zipping `$HOME\.ssh` is `read_secret`.
- Declined, minor: adding `pixz`, `bzip3` and `zopfli` to the secret-reader list (`detect/secrets.rs`) and the only-reads list (`effect/operands.rs`). That is about what these programs read, outside this ticket, and main has the same gap for `pigz`, `lzop`, `lzip` and `lbzip2`. It should be its own ticket.

## Gate

`just verify` passed (exit 0) on this branch with origin/main at e2f5ff5 merged in.

```text
TOTAL                                       105830              3928    96.29%        6450               124    98.08%       57478              2051    96.43%           0                 0         -
...
cargo test -p milo-guards-shell --no-default-features --test inline_off --locked
running 1 test
test every_case_holds ... ok

test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.16s

cargo deny check bans licenses sources
bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
```

Across the whole run: 1184 tests passed, 0 failed.

## Left out

Nothing in the ticket is left. Possible follow-ups, not fixed here:

- `([IO.Compression.ZipFile])::Open(path, 'Read')`, with the type in parentheses, still gets the generic "calls .NET to write or open files", because the parentheses are not seen through.
- `$t::Open(...)` where `$t` holds another type, such as `[IO.File]`, is now judged by the path and mode it is given, which is more cautious than before.
- The secret-reader and only-reads lists leave out `pixz`, `bzip3`, `zopfli`, and on main also `pigz`, `lzop`, `lzip` and `lbzip2` (see Review).
- Windows' `compress`: whether it takes options written with `/` is not confirmed, so a `/r` word is read as an operand. Its destination is still judged.

No new rules, so there are no wire names to confirm.

body:
## Summary

Overhauls the visual design system, public website copy, and guest booking/account UX so Lemma Apartments reads as an authentic Lusaka hospitality property rather than a generic SaaS template, and eliminates friction across booking, payment submission, and reservation tracking.

### Visual Identity & Design System
- **Fixed missing Tailwind tokens (`tailwind.config.ts`)**: Defined `lemma.{DEFAULT,dark,light}` and `st.{paid,paidBg}` used across 70+ interactive rings, buttons, and status badges.
- **Warm hospitality palette & editorial typography (`tailwind.config.ts`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/globals.css`)**: Updated `sand` stone neutrals (`#FAF8F5`–`#E6E0D6`) and muted brass `gold` accents, paired **Fraunces** (`--font-display`) headings with **Inter** (`--font-sans`) body/tabular numerals, and removed the `.shine` button shimmer effect.
- **Crisp SVG Brand Emblem (`src/components/public/brand-mark.tsx`)**: Replaced blurry `logo.jpg` thumbnails across the public header/footer, mobile menu, auth screens, receipts, print folios, cleaning portal, and admin sidebar with an inline vector mark (`tone="light" | "dark"`), and cleaned up empty `TPIN` / website trailing separators in `PrintHeader`.

### Public Pages, Navigation & Copy
- **Header, Footer & Menu (`src/components/public/site-chrome.tsx`, `src/components/public/site-menu.tsx`)**: Visually hid the redundant desktop `Menu` button (`md:hidden`) when signed out while keeping full-screen dialog navigation on mobile and for signed-in sessions; added direct `/booking/access` lookup links.
- **Homepage & Catalogue (`src/app/page.tsx`, `src/components/public/home-hero-carousel.tsx`, `src/app/apartments/*`)**: Varied page layouts with a docked availability search bar, a 3-step ZMW booking & deposit guide, and Lusaka essentials; aligned the default stay window to **2 nights** across `/`, `/apartments`, and `/apartments/[slug]`; consolidated sample/stock disclosures into single calm notices; and rewrote AI-sounding copy tropes (*"not a chatbot"*, *"No call centre"*, *"not a gamble"*).
- **About, Contact & Policies (`src/app/about/page.tsx`, `src/app/contact/page.tsx`, `src/app/policies/page.tsx`)**: Added Barlaston Park arrival guidance, Google Maps + WhatsApp location-pin links, safe handling of unconfigured payment account numbers on `/contact`, and plain-language house terms.

### Booking, Visitor Lookup, Auth & Guest Account UX
- **Streamlined Booking Widget (`src/app/apartments/[slug]/booking-widget.tsx`, `src/lib/api/schemas.ts`, `src/components/payments/payment-details.tsx`)**: Made `countryOfResidence` and `nationality` optional in `publicBookingSchema`, moved optional check-in details (arrival time, NRC/passport, residential address) into a collapsible `<details>` block, removed the duplicate price summary box, calmed unconfigured payment messaging, and added a **3-step post-booking progress tracker**.
- **Branded Visitor Booking Pages (`src/app/booking/[id]/*`, `src/app/booking/access/*`, `src/app/api/public/booking-access/route.ts`)**: Wrapped visitor lookup and status screens in `PublicHeader` + `PublicFooter` with human-readable dates/badges, ZMW balance summaries, inline payment-proof upload (`GuestPaymentPanel`), and WhatsApp reception shortcuts.
- **Guest-Friendly Auth & Single-Status Account Portal (`src/app/login/login-form.tsx`, `src/app/register/page.tsx`, `src/app/account/account-client.tsx`)**: Removed stock apartment photos/disclaimers from `/login` and `/register`, reframed `/login` around guest email sign-in (while preserving staff desk handle sign-in), and collapsed the 3 competing status chips per reservation into **one unified status badge** + a **4-step stay progress bar** so bookings with an active payment claim never display an alarming red `Unpaid` badge.

## Verification
- `npm run test:unit` — 19 / 19 unit tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` & `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `npm run build` — 35 / 35 Next.js routes built cleanly
- `scripts/e2e-test.mjs` — 133 / 133 HTTP & SSR end-to-end checks passed

body: Serve the Cadmus API over ConnectRPC on a public companion listener and an always-on loopback listener. One port each carries Connect and gRPC-Web over HTTP/1.1 plus cleartext gRPC over HTTP/2 with prior knowledge. Shared services live in cadmus.api.shared.v1 and are registered on both listeners. cadmus.api.internal.v1 is registered only for loopback, with a no-op Placeholder keeping that path exercised. Handlers queue a command on the main loop and wait on a oneshot, holding a soft-suspend lease while they wait, so they never touch AppContext. File RPCs stay inside /mnt/onboard/.adds on Kobo, and every RPC is logged at trace level with the listener it reached. Publish the OpenAPI document generated at build time by protoc-gen-connect-openapi. Auth lives in the proto annotations, the plugin is built from source in devenv with a Renovate-tracked pin, and info.version comes from the shared git-describe helper. Both listeners serve it at /openapi.json; the internal RPCs stay in the document for plugin/extension authors. Change-Id: dda02a0798fdea55891738d544e83c99 Change-Id-Short: mmpzxpzsqrkm > [!NOTE] > ### Add backend API layer with Connect RPC listeners, file ops, and settings services > - Adds a new `crates/api-proto` crate that generates ConnectRPC types and an OpenAPI document from protobuf definitions in `proto/cadmus/api`, with build-time codegen driven by the shared `build-deps` helpers > - Adds public and private API listeners: the public listener binds a wildcard address, requires a bearer token, acquires a `public-api` Wi-Fi lease, and registers mDNS; the private listener binds loopback port 8474 with no token > - Implements shared RPC services for status, settings catalog/update, and file listing/retrieval, dispatched through a main-loop command channel with a 5-second timeout via the `ask` helper in [handler.rs](https://github.com/OGKevin/cadmus/pull/1174/files#diff-fe763849a2f6146b95a0de863482404b3e5fde4e05ccbe383ef954b9789a7258) > - Integrates the API into the app lifecycle: events are offered to the API handler before the device handler, the companion menu toggles the public listener, and suspend/resume rebind the listener while keeping its token > - Converts `SettingsManager::load`/`save`, TOML helpers, and backup manifest I/O to async using Tokio filesystem APIs; adds an NTP-server deserializer that falls back to Cloudflare when the configured value is invalid > - Behavioral Change: `SettingsManager::load` and `save` are now `async` and return futures that callers must await; event handling order changes because `dispatch_api_then_device` in [app.rs](https://github.com/OGKevin/cadmus/pull/1174/files#diff-bdc45afe0dbc207b96b760693c8e2c366d65f4ae43aefba59498528bc4bdcb64) can consume events before the device handler sees them; the public listener binds port 80 on device and an ephemeral port in the emulator > > > > Macroscope summarized 8ca1345. > >

author: mmanciop
body:
## The problem

`AppBaseURL` derives the web app host from the API host by taking the last two labels and prefixing `app.`. That is right for the regional hosts it was written for — `api.eu-west-1.aws.dash0.com` and `api.us-west-2.aws.dash0.com` both correctly collapse to `app.dash0.com` — but it never rejected inputs that are not regional hosts, and silently produced a wrong host for three of them:

| API URL | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:8080` | `https://app.0.1` | `""` |
| `http://10.0.0.5` | `https://app.0.5` | `""` |
| `https://api.dash0.com.` | `https://app.com.` | `https://app.dash0.com` |
| `https://API.DASH0.COM` | `https://app.DASH0.COM` | `https://app.dash0.com` |

Ranked by how bad the outcome is:

1. **A trailing dot sends users to a third party.** It is legal in a URL and makes the name fully qualified, but it leaves an empty final label that displaces a real one — the last two labels of `api.dash0.com.` are `com` and `""`, so the link points at **app.com**, which is someone else's site. A link to the wrong real domain is worse than a broken one.
2. **An IPv4 API URL yields a dead link.** It has dots, so it is split like a domain. Anyone pointing the client at a `kubectl port-forward`, a local proxy, or an IP-based ingress got `https://app.0.1`. IPv6 was already safe, but only by accident: an address has no dots, so it tripped the label-count guard.
3. **The host was not lowercased.** It resolves either way, since hostnames are case-insensitive, but the link is rendered back to users.

## The fix

Reject IP addresses outright, strip a trailing dot before splitting, and lowercase the result. An empty return already means "no deep link available" to every caller, so an IP-based API URL now omits the link rather than showing one that leads nowhere.

IPv6 is now rejected for being an address rather than by accident of its spelling — the behavior is unchanged, but the reason is.

## What this does not fix

`domainSuffix` still approximates the registrable domain as "the last two labels", so a multi-label public suffix is still wrong: `api.dash0.co.uk` yields `app.co.uk`. Doing that properly means the Public Suffix List (`golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix`, BSD-3-Clause), which pulls in a large embedded table. I left it out because Dash0 does not serve API traffic from such a host today, and the trailing-dot case above was the variant that was actually reachable. Worth revisiting if that ever changes.

## Why now

The Dash0 CLI is about to surface these links much more widely — [dash0hq/dash0-cli#349](https://github.com/dash0hq/dash0-cli/pull/349) adds them to JSON and CSV output, including agent mode. Today a malformed link only shows up in human-readable table output; after that change an AI agent can read one out of a JSON field and hand it to a user as if it were real. That PR does not depend on this one, but this is the moment the blast radius grows.

## Testing

Extended `TestAppBaseURL` with the fully-qualified, uppercase, mixed-case, IPv4 (loopback, private, no-port) and IPv6 (loopback, full) cases. Existing cases are unchanged and still pass.

`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `gofmt` are clean. `make api-compat` reports no incompatible changes and suggests v1.30.1.

The scalper only checked whether a candle closed across VWAP or the EMA and whether the trend agreed. It never looked at the candle itself, so it could buy on a weak candle or chase a move that was already stretched.

author: hyyashu
body:
## Summary

### `safeFetchBytes` (image download, website reader, OAuth client metadata)
Three bugs, all reachable with a URL someone else controls (client metadata is fetched before any login):

1. **Hangs forever when the connection drops after the headers.** The error is reported on the response, which had no listener, and the socket idle timeout never fires on a closed socket. Reproduced on Node 22. An approved image upload could sit in `executing` until the stuck-request sweep marked it `unknown_outcome`, even though nothing was sent to Google.
2. **No overall time limit.** The `timeout` option is an idle timer, so a server sending a byte every few seconds kept the request open indefinitely.
3. **Oversized documents returned as a success.** If the body was already complete when the size check tripped, `end` still fired and the call resolved with truncated (often empty) bytes. `req.destroy(err)` also raised an uncaught exception.

Fix: handle response `error`/`aborted`/incomplete `close`; add one overall deadline; on oversize, reject first and then tear down without an error. A test-only `transport` option lets the new tests run against a local server.

### `create_*_campaign` approval snapshot
The snapshot was every campaign name in the account (up to 10,000). Adding or renaming **any** campaign between request and approval failed the approval as "account changed", and a large blob was stored with each approval. The snapshot now holds only campaigns whose name matches the requested one, case-insensitively, so a newly created clash still blocks the create.

## Tests
- New `src/tests/ssrf-fetch.test.ts`: complete response, connection cut after headers, slow drip vs. the deadline, oversize in one chunk and in several. The oversize test fails on the old code (resolves with truncated bytes, plus an uncaught exception).
- `google-campaign-create.test.ts`: unrelated campaign changes no longer block approval; a same-name clash still fails it.
- Typecheck clean; full suite 504/504 passing.

The `splunk-contentctl-v5-6` config sub-schema said to omit `drilldown_searches` because contentctl generates them from the risk objects. This changes the description wording only, so no version bump. It matches the vendored copy fixed in DetectionFlow/detectionflow#735.

The `splunk-contentctl-ng` schema makes a similar claim about the ng build. That toolchain's source isn't vendored here, so I've left it unchanged.

## Problem

Der YouLess LS120 liefert Zahlen als Strings mit führenden Leerzeichen und deutschem Dezimalkomma (`" 8,100"`). `to_f`/`to_i` schneiden am Komma ab, die Monatssumme war dadurch zu klein (November 2025: 713,0 statt 718,1 kWh). Außerdem wurde `tm` ignoriert: Mit hängender Geräteuhr (2026-09-23) zeigte das Dashboard die Daten vom November 2025 als "Heizung (Monat)".

- `parse_youless_number`: Whitespace entfernen, Komma zu Punkt, Float; `nil` bei nil/leer. Genutzt in Monatssumme und `calculate_sum_of_watts` (nil-Werte werden übersprungen).
- `tm` wird validiert (`today`-Parameter für Testbarkeit):
  - Monat nur, wenn Jahr und Monat von `tm` dem aktuellen entsprechen, sonst `nil`
  - `d=0` nur bei `tm` == heute, `d=1` nur bei `tm` == gestern, sonst `nil`
- `nil` wird sicher weitergereicht: Overview zeigt `– kWh`, `energyflow` nutzt `.to_f`, das Number-Widget `wattmeterheating_sum` bekommt über `day_event_payload` `0.0` statt `nil` (sonst "NaN%").
- `@@last_values`/`restore_last_values` unverändert.

Neue Tests für Parsing, Monatssumme mit null, Stundenwerte, veraltete/Vorjahres-`tm`, Payload-Guard. Gesamte Suite grün.

## Resumen
Nueva página que consume `GET /peliculas/estadisticas` de la API y muestra, por género, el número de películas y la nota media. Incluye un filtro `minimo` (de 1 a 5).

## Cambios
- `estadisticas.html` y `js/estadisticas.js` (nuevos): la tabla se pinta con `textContent`, sin innerHTML. El input `minimo` acepta valores de 1 a 5 y, si la API responde 400, se muestran los detalles de la validación.
- `js/api.js`: nueva función `estadisticas()`. Además, `pedir()` guarda ahora `error.detalles` cuando la API los devuelve.
- `index.html`: nuevo menú de navegación entre Películas y Estadísticas.
- `css/estilos.css`: estilos `.menu` y `.tabla`.

## Cómo probar
No se ha probado todavía en un navegador.
1. Arrancar la API con la rama correspondiente (`npm start`), con `CORS_ORIGIN` apuntando al origen de la web.
2. Servir la web (por ejemplo, con Live Server) y abrir `estadisticas.html`.
3. Sin filtro, la tabla debe mostrar todos los géneros ordenados por nota media.
4. Con `minimo` = 2, solo deben aparecer los géneros con 2 o más películas.
5. Con un valor fuera de rango (por ejemplo, forzando la petición con `?minimo=9`), debe aparecer el mensaje de error de la API.
6. El menú debe permitir moverse entre `index.html` y `estadisticas.html`.

Son hallazgos que ya existían antes de esta PR. No se corrigen aquí:

author: marigold
body:
## 👨 Summary I'm trying to generalize this so the bake process detects it automatically and replaces deploy-queue with Buildkite. It'll be much easier without lightning bakes. I'm not sure how often they're used nowadays, but they don't seem to be working properly anyway. > _Written by Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 — @Marigold at the wheel._ Removes "lightning deploys", the fast path that re-baked a single gdoc when a republish changed only page-local fields. Every gdoc publish and republish now goes through the normal deploy queue and gets a full bake. ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Publish / Republish gdoc"] --> T["triggerStaticBuild"] --> Q["deploy queue"] Q --> B{"Buildkite token?"} B -- "yes (prod)" --> F["Buildkite full build"] B -- "no (staging, local)" --> L["bakeAll"] P -. "removed" .-> X["checkIsLightningUpdate → enqueueLightningChange →
Buildkite LIGHTNING_GDOC_SLUGS / bakeGDocPosts(slug)"] classDef gone fill:#fde8e8,stroke:#c0392b,color:#7b1d1d,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef kept fill:#eef4fb,stroke:#3b6ea8,color:#1b2b40 class X gone class P,T,Q,B,F,L kept ``` **Risk: low.** The lightning path was close to dead. `checkIsLightningUpdate` compared `tags` as raw objects; the DB copy carries `Date` timestamps and the client JSON carries strings, so the check failed for every tagged gdoc. Only ~20 of 644 published gdocs (untagged, mostly about pages) ever took it: 1–5 lightning builds a month against ~24 content deploys a day. The only server behaviour that changes is that the update branch now always calls `triggerStaticBuild`, the same call publishing already uses, and it still honours `BAKE_ON_CHANGE`. What authors and staging users will notice: - The ⚡ on the Republish button is gone; the button reads "Publish" or "Republish". - On a staging server, republishing one of those few untagged gdocs now runs `bakeAll`, so the change takes minutes rather than seconds to appear. **Why now:** an incremental bake that re-bakes only the pages a change affects is coming (#7589). It replaces what lightning tried to do, and one bake mode is a simpler base for it than two entry points. **Companion ops PR:** owid/ops#831 drops the `LIGHTNING_GDOC_SLUGS` branch from `deploy-content.sh`. Merge order doesn't matter: if ops merges first, a lightning build would just do a full bake; if this merges first, the variable is never sent. **Call for the reviewer:** `yarn bakeGdocPosts` and the `slugs` parameter of `SiteBaker.bakeGDocPosts` stay as a dev tool for baking one page locally, though nothing in production calls them with slugs any more. Deleting them too would be a reasonable alternative.
Details Removed: - `checkIsLightningUpdate` and its per-type field maps (`adminSiteClient/gdocsDeploy.ts`) - `useLightningUpdate` and the ⚡ Republish label (`gdocsHooks.ts`, `GdocsSaveButtons.tsx`, `GdocsPreviewPage.tsx`) - the lightning branch in `indexAndBakeGdocIfNeccesary` (`adminSiteServer/apiRoutes/gdocs.ts`), plus its now-unused server-side `checkHasChanges` call; the client still uses `checkHasChanges` via `useGdocsChanged` - `enqueueLightningChange` (`adminSiteServer/apiRoutes/routeUtils.ts`) - the `lightningQueue` path and `isLightningChange` in `baker/DeployUtils.ts` - `BuildkiteTrigger.runLightningBuild` and its only test (`baker/BuildkiteTrigger.test.ts`) - `DeployChange.slug` in `@ourworldindata/types`, and the lightning case in `DeployQueueServer.test.ts` - stale comments in `adminSiteClient/constants.ts` and `GdocBase.toJSON` Edge cases: - A `.queue`/`.pending` file written before the deploy may still hold entries with `slug`. `parseQueueContent` parses them as plain JSON, the extra field is ignored, and they get a full bake.
Testing - Agent, local worktree stack, read-only (no publish clicked, since the DB and Algolia index are shared): the admin preview of a published article shows "Republish" with no bolt, a draft shows "Publish"; the settings drawer and the diff view open, and the console shows no errors from these components. - `baker/DeployQueueServer.test.ts`, lint, format and typecheck pass. - Not exercised: an actual publish enqueuing a deploy. That path is now the unconditional `triggerStaticBuild` call the Publishing branch already used.
