author: stackblaze-adam
body: ## What The installer can now **connect a brand-new VM to existing backups**: the appliance is gone, you build a plain Ubuntu VM, give it one recovery file and the VDDK tarball, and everything comes back. - **First question in the wizard:** "New appliance" or "Connect to existing backups". Connect asks only for the recovery file (or the S3 location, key and encryption password, typed in), the cache disk, the VDDK, and whether to set up the public URL. vCenter, name, jobs, policies, protected VMs and users come back from the backups. - **Recovery file** (`/root/vmexec-recovery.env`, 0600): S3 endpoint, region, bucket, folder and key, the ZeroFS password, and the public URL settings (domain, allowlist, Bunny key) when there are any. Written on a fresh install (also when an interrupted first run generated the password); `deploy/install.sh --write-recovery-file F` writes one for an existing appliance. `deploy/install.sh --recovery-file F` connects without questions. - **One-writer check:** ZeroFS allows one appliance per repository. A running appliance writes every 10 minutes even when idle (measured on Central), so connecting refuses while the repository was written in the last 15 minutes. `s3-usage.py` now reports the newest write. `--force-recover` overrides it when you know the old VM is off. - **The recovery copy:** hourly (was daily), includes the app `.env` and public URL settings, and is **fsynced**. Before, it wasn't: ZeroFS keeps unsynced writes in its local cache, and a hard power-off 50 s after a copy brought back the previous one (no vCenter, no protected VMs). A recovery now also keeps the old appliance's copy in `_appliance/before-recover-/` before the new VM's own copy replaces it. - **Settings outside the database** (`VMEXEC_PROTECTED_VMS`, `VMEXEC_PARALLEL_DISKS`, the name…) are restored on connect. - **Optional public URL** (`--public-domain`, `--allow-from`, `--bunny-key-file`, or the wizard's step 6), in `deploy/public-access.sh`. It replaces the setup done by hand on the three appliances on 2026-11-04: - ufw allows 22 and 443 only from the allowlist - Docker's published ports are dropped on the public card - ARP sysctls for flat L2 segments - VMware Tools `exclude-nics` - Caddy with Let's Encrypt through Bunny DNS-01 (no inbound access needed) - the UI bound to 127.0.0.1 A lock-out guard refuses if the SSH session running it is not in the allowlist. The VM's address itself still comes from the VM build. - **End of a connect:** a summary of what came back (`appliance_setup summary`). - **Fix:** the wizard no longer offers the VM's floppy (`/dev/fd0`, 0 GB, listed first and the default) as the cache disk; `deploy/install.sh` refuses a cache disk under 10 GB. ## Tested (Central, 2026-11-04, throwaway VMs on prefix `central-vm-backups/vmexec-connect-test`) 1. Fresh install on `vmexec-test-a` with the public URL: certificate issued over DNS-01 for a name with no A record; from the VPN, 8000 closed and 443 open. Re-run is idempotent and writes a complete recovery file. 2. `vmexec-test-a` hard powered off right away; connecting `vmexec-test-b` **refused** ("written 0 minutes ago") before touching the disk or writing secrets. 3. After 15 quiet minutes, the **interactive wizard** (driven by `expect`, defaults everywhere) connected `vmexec-test-b`. That run found the floppy bug, and the missing fsync: the database came back from the copy before the last one. 4. After the fixes, `vmexec-test-b` took a backup and its database copy, then was hard powered off **2 s after the copy**. A **freshly cloned** `vmexec-test-a` connected from the recovery file with no other input. Everything came back: vCenter as `vmexec@`, the protected VM and its policy, `VMEXEC_PROTECTED_VMS`, both restore points (including the one written seconds before the kill), the public URL with its certificate, and the old copy kept in `before-recover-…`. 5. A restore from the recovered appliance: `vmexec-test-a` restored as a new VM in 2 min 23 s (Success, registered powered off). Test VMs destroyed afterwards; Caddy left no records in Bunny. Unit test: `tests/test_s3_usage.py` (newest write across pages, empty prefix). ## Found, not fixed here - **Incremental reads hold every changed byte in memory** (`vddk_transport.read_snapshot_extents`: `subprocess.run` captures the reader's whole output, then slices it into a second copy). A VM with about 3.7 GB changed took the worker to 7.5 GB RSS and the OOM killer ended it, on an 8 GB VM. Fulls stream to disk and are fine. This needs its own fix (stream the frames like the full path does). ## After merge platform-provisioner: the role should pass `--public-domain/--allow-from/--bunny-key-file` from the manifest, stop forcing `VMEXEC_BIND=0.0.0.0`, and remove `/root/vmexec-recovery.env` once the vault has the password. Bump the pin. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: alecbibat
body:
## Summary

- **Screensaver**: the mode dropdown is gone. One **SCREENSAVER** button starts the pins tour and stops it on the next click. The other tour modes keep their code but have no way in.
- **Collapsible menu**: a tab on the left menu's edge collapses it; the same tab stays at the screen edge to reopen it. Remembered per browser. The top-bar badges, news ticker and left-docked windows follow the menu's edge.
- **Watch / News / Intel launcher**: hidden from the top right for now. `WidgetLauncher` is kept, and News still opens from the ticker.
- **NWS alerts stand out more**:
  - The polygons are ground-clamped, and Cesium silently drops `outline` on ground-clamped polygons, so alerts had **no border at all**. They now get a bright border in the alert's colour inside a dark casing, drawn above every fill.
  - A county-based alert gets **one outline around all its counties**, not a mesh of county lines. County geometry is now the Census-derived `us-atlas` TopoJSON, bundled with the app (203 KB brotli, versus the 3.2 MB GeoJSON previously fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at runtime). Neighbouring counties share arcs exactly, so `topojson.mesh` merges them. On the live feed, the same 35 county-based land alerts resolve as before.
  - Fill opacity is weighted by severity.
- **Alert notifications**: when a new NWS alert covers a pin or comes within **15 miles** of one, the screen flashes in the alert's colour and a centred popup lists each affected location (inside, or how far away), with a *Show on map* button.
  - A bell in the top bar turns them on and off (per browser, on by default).
  - The first poll is the baseline, so alerts already in effect when the page opens don't fire.
  - NWS updates only notify for locations they newly reach. Tests and cancellations never notify.
  - The flash stays under the WCAG three-flashes-per-second limit; reduced motion gets a single fade.
- **Crisis checklists**: items are **Not started / In progress / Completed**.
  - A click marks an item in progress; a second click completes it.
  - Right-click (long-press on touch, or the context-menu key) opens a menu to set any status. That menu is the only way to reopen a completed item.
  - Works on the editor and the share page.
  - Entries keep `checked` (true exactly when completed), so progress counts, the AAR and old clients read completion unchanged and stored data needs no migration. The endpoints take `{ status }` and still accept the old `{ checked }` body.
- **Wireless Emergency Alerts (PBS WARN) overlay** (off by default): every WEA in force, as warn.pbs.org maps them. That includes state and local alerts (AMBER, evacuations, police activity, 911 outages) as well as NWS and USGS ones.
  - Each area is drawn with a dashed border coloured by WEA class, plus a broadcast marker.
  - The panel shows the exact message sent to phones.
  - An option hides the NWS-issued WEAs, since the NWS layer already draws them.
  - The server proxies the API behind PBS's map (`/api/warn/active`) with a 45 s cache. **That API is undocumented and can change without notice.** On upstream failure the last good answer is served and the sidebar says so.
  - FEMA's own sources don't fit a live layer: OpenFEMA's IPAWS archive is published 24 h late, and IPAWS-OPEN needs a FEMA-issued PIN.

## Testing

- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (1,349 client tests and 531 server tests, including the Postgres-backed suites run against a local Postgres 16), and `npm run build` all pass locally.
- New unit tests cover: the merged county outlines, the shared alert fetch, the alert-near-pin rules (baseline, updates, tests and cancels, 6 h memory), the point-to-polygon distance and circle helpers, checklist statuses (client and server, plus a Postgres route test that also covers the legacy `{ checked }` body), and the WARN normalizer, which was also run over 14 days of live records (563).
- Checked in a browser against the dev server:

author: tahakhanabdalli
body:
**Step 1 of Mason's order on #1363: "yes with the guard updates first".** Merge this, then #1363, then create `staging` and its ruleset. Until then, `staging` doesn't exist and nothing here changes how `main` works.

## What changes
Your agent's review of #1363 raised three points. This PR answers each one.

**1. Merges into `staging` were ungated** (`pr-merge-guard.mjs:506` returned early for any base but `main`).
- Both merge guards (Claude `.claude/hooks/pr-merge-guard.mjs`, Codex `.codex/hooks/production-action-guard.mjs`) now give a merge into `staging` **every gate a merge into `main` has**: no CHANGES_REQUESTED, `--match-head-commit` pinned, no `--auto`, every check green, and the Sol proof where the Sol list needs it.
- The shared list is `GATED_MERGE_BASES = ["main", "staging"]` in `sol-risk-lib.mjs`, so the two guards can't drift.
- The Sol proof stays bound to `origin/main`. `write-codex-push-proof.mjs` is untouched (its base is deliberately not configurable). A proof is therefore accepted for a merge into `staging` only when `staging` already contains the `main` it was reviewed against. This is the existing `proofValidForMerge` rule; nothing new.

**2. Migrations had no defined path through staging** (`migration-landing-gate-lib.mjs:170`).
- The path for now: **migrations don't go through `staging`.**
  - Both merge guards refuse a merge into `staging` whose GitHub comparison has a file in `supabase/migrations/`. Renames count, and if the file list can't be read, the merge is refused.
  - A migration PR targets `main` and is applied live first, exactly as today (ship.md Step 5).
  - The apply gate already refused PRs that don't target `main`; its message now says why.
- This holds until Mason approves the job that applies migrations to the staging database (the CI/CD "live part" in #crx-approvals). Then the live database is never ahead of production code because of staging, and a release PR never carries a batch of applied migrations.
- Bringing `main` into `staging` is a PR `main → staging`, merged by Taha or Mason. After a migration lands on `main`, that PR carries the file, and the guards refuse it from an agent on purpose.

**3. Vercel and Supabase for staging.**
- `staging` gets its own Vercel environment (a preview, never production) and its own Supabase project, `fsnjredpmakbmhwowjjt` (test data only, already loaded and caught up). It never points at the live project.
- The release PR `staging → main` is a merge into `main`, with every gate above.

**Docs.**
- `AGENTS.md` › Safety and Protected Delivery gets one bullet (76 lines, 10,596 bytes, within the guidance budget), and "never push directly to `main`" becomes "`main` or `staging`".
- `.claude/commands/ship.md` gets a "Staging" section with the details.
- Changelog note: `docs/changelog.d/2026-11-04-staging-merge-guards.md`.

**Not in this PR:** blocking a direct push to `staging` in the local push guard. The `staging` ruleset created in step 3 enforces that on GitHub, and AGENTS.md states the rule.

## Proof
Tests were written first and failed before the change:
- `sol-risk-lib.test.mjs` (68 pass):
  - the base list;
  - migration detection, including renames, Windows paths and mixed case;
  - an unreadable, empty or possibly truncated list is refused;
  - GitHub failures are refused.
- `production-action-guard.test.mjs` (full suite passes), end to end through the Codex guard with a fake `gh`:
  - a staging merge on the Sol list is denied without Sol and lands with a valid proof;
  - a staging merge without the head pin is denied;
  - a migration into staging is denied, and the denial says to target `main`;
  - an unreadable PR is denied.
- `pr-merge-guard.test.mjs` (310 pass): the staging check uses the shared list and the hard-gate budget, and runs before any allow point.
- `npm run test:correction-guards` and `npm run test:agent-workflows` pass, as do `check-agent-guidance`, `check-agent-workflows`, `check-doc-drift` and eslint on the changed hooks.
- Note for anyone running these on macOS: a few existing worktree tests fail there because the temp folder resolves to `/private/var`, identically on clean `main`. With `TMPDIR` set to a resolved folder, every suite passes.

— Taha

## Problem
Một task cỡ PR #977 mất ~7,3 giờ phiên (07:53–15:10 UTC 04/11). Đo trên log thật (transcript phiên, `.git/postfix-gate/runs.jsonl`, log merge gate, `task.json` của antigravity-pm):

- merge gate exit 14 vì PR có duyệt test sửa (pm) không được tự đồng bộ base: ~31 phút;
- grok audit: 3 lượt / 44,1 phút, 1 lượt bị giết đúng hạn 20 phút (diff 26 file, +1640/−52).

## Solution

- post-fix-gate: lượt `--scoped` (không `--full/--force-full/--tree/--since`) mặc định không fail-fast, lộ mọi suite đỏ trong một lượt; cờ `--fail-fast` mới; lane_lock coi `--fail-fast` là việc nhẹ. Lượt khác giữ fail-fast (#647).
- merge gate: `sync_candidate` tự gộp base (mọi file hai phía có merge driver) cho PR có duyệt `pm` khi verify chạy post-fix-gate; `true` (comment #643), `pm-unknown`, pm không gate vẫn exit 14. Verify vẫn trong khoá, approved-head vẫn kiểm.
- antigravity-pm: hạn grok = 20 phút + 1 phút/100 dòng diff, trần 60 phút; `ANTIGRAVITY_PM_GROK_TIMEOUT_MS` vẫn thắng; hạn ghi vào log audit.

|---|---|---|

author: staticaland
body:
## What is this change?

The new `merge-risk` plugin holds the `merge-risk` skill from [warpdotdev/common-skills](https://github.com/warpdotdev/common-skills), vendored with vendir. The skill grades a pull request on alignment, impact, verification, rollback cost, and error detection. It then weights the grades into one merge risk: low, medium, or high. The plugin is in the `dev` category. Upstream keeps its MIT license at the repository root, so `LICENSE` is copied in and `ignorePaths` keeps it through a sync. The vendored path is in `.prettierignore`, `.rumdl.toml`, `.vale.ini`, and `lychee.toml`. The plugin has entries in `marketplace.json`, `release-please-config.json`, and the README catalog.

## Why do we need this change?

The marketplace has no skill that rates the risk of a merge before a reviewer approves it.

## Who is this change for?

Users who review pull requests with an agent and want a consistent risk rating.

## What is the merge danger?

**Door:** Two-way. The plugin is not published until the release PR merges.

**What can break:** Repo. A wrong entry fails the structure or manifest checks. All prek hooks pass locally except zizmor, which cannot reach the GitHub API from the sandbox. This change does not touch workflows.

## Which issue(s) does this PR fix?

None.

body:
Charter pillar: autonomy (the code loop must not lock files it cannot work on). Stacked on #6982 (the diff against main shows that PR's commit until it merges; this PR's own change is the second commit, `qnfo-code-orchestrator` 0.39.0 -> 0.39.1).

## Evidence
`GET /work-locks` 2026-11-04 15:00Z: `file:qnfo-research-exec/worker.js` held by `qnfo-code-orchestrator:ct_y1la8qrww2mbak` since 2026-11-03T01:00:53Z, expiry rolled forward every 2 hours (15:56Z, then 17:13Z). `code_tasks`: status `queued`, step `verify`, attempts 1, `lease_until` NULL, `pr_url` NULL, `updated_at` 2026-11-03T01:21Z, `last_error` "patch too large: exceeds verification limit". It duplicates `ct_im100138` (same issue #100138, at step commit). Effect: six queued tasks on that file deferred (`code-task.claim-held` every 2 minutes), every session refused the file by `/work-lock/acquire`, and sessions' PRs 6917, 6937 and 6948 edited it anyway. The task cannot be advanced: `claim()` never hands a queued task to a lane while an earlier unfinished task exists on the same path, so nothing saves its row, while `claimsSweep` keeps renewing the claim of "every unfinished task".

## Change
`claimsSweep` treats a `queued` task with no PR and no save for 3 hours (`CLAIM_STALL_MS`; every step, backoff and deferral saves the row) as stalled: its claim is released at the guard with outcome `abandoned`, recorded on the row (`claim.stalled`), logged as `code-task.claim-stalled`, and never renewed or re-taken by the sweep (the sweep query skips it). If a lane ever runs the task again, `claimEnsure` takes a new claim as for any released task. A task that moves, sits under 3 hours, or owns a pull request keeps its claim. It is the same defect class as CLAIM-HELD-IN-BACKOFF-1, CLAIM-AT-RUN-1 and CLAIM-PUBLISHED-RELEASE-1, for a task the loop cannot advance.

## Verified
`claim-stalled.test.mjs`: **13 checks pass; on the unfixed code 5 pass and 8 fail** (zombie not released, renewed on the way, no event). Four fixtures: zombie 38 h, moving, quiet 2 h, old with PR. Claim suites unchanged against the base: claims-first 26/0, claims-sweep-resilient 5/0, claim-published-release 7/0, claim-ceiling 32/0, dispatch-dedupe 56/0, lease-fence 9/0; claim-backoff (25 failures) and claim-at-run (3) fail identically at the base.

Verify live after the deploy: `GET https://qnfo-deploy-guard.q08.workers.dev/work-locks` no longer lists `ct_y1la8qrww2mbak` on `file:qnfo-research-exec/worker.js`; `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cloud_ops_events WHERE kind='code-task.claim-stalled'` is at least 1.

author: jalehman
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw ID claw refuses its 51st member and each person's sixth browser, which is too small for a shared team server: the OpenClaw team server alone has about 73 maintainers and 46–62 guests.

## User Impact

A claw can now have up to 256 members with up to 10 browsers each, and an owner device certificate can carry up to 10 peer keys. Owner devices stay at 20. No Gateway behavior changes until the OpenClaw ID Gateway code that consumes these constants merges.

## Why This Change Was Made

256 members is the statement list limit (`MAX_LIST`), so a snapshot listing every member still validates and no list format changes are needed. A new test builds a snapshot at every cap and checks that one more member hits the list limit. That snapshot is about 275 KiB of JSON (about 600 KiB if every account id character needs a JSON escape). The Discovery change sizes its snapshot publication limit for this and stops rewriting derived rows one statement at a time.

Deploy order: this loosens limits, so Discovery and the loader should take it before Gateways do. Companion changes:
- openclaw/discovery: snapshot publication limit and derived-row writes
- openclaw/claw-loader: re-vendored protocol

## Evidence

- `vitest` over `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 19 files, 131 tests passed, including the new cap tests.
- Discovery (vendoring this commit): 30 files, 227 tests passed, including publishing a worst-case snapshot and checking relay admission and member listing.
- claw-loader (vendoring this commit): typecheck and 83 unit tests passed; a reviewer smoke test parsed and verified a 280 KB snapshot at every cap.
- Independent review of all three diffs found no P0–P2 issues.
- Test-lines ratchet: the new cap tests add 46 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-claw-limits.txt` (local check against `main` `d7ee885db8f`: OK, slack 17).

author: leroyvn
body:
## Problem

Since 0.2.0rc1, `MonoAbsorptionDatabase.eval_sigma_a_mono()` returns NaN for every in-bounds altitude when the `w` coordinate of a data file is not monotonic. `_bracket_indices()` infers the grid order from its endpoints, so a grid made of sorted chunks joined end to end is searched as if it were sorted, which yields NaN interpolation weights.

This affects the Eradiate komodo mono database (36811 points, 10 decreasing steps). Downstream, the NaN reaches DISORT, which fails with `asymmetric_matrix--convergence problems`.

## Fix

`load_dataset()` now checks that `w` is monotonic. If not:

- In **eager mode**, AxsDB issues a warning, then sorts the dataset with `isel(w=argsort(w))`. On komodo (288 MiB `sigma_a`), peak memory usage is at 685 MiB, and memory returns to 399 MiB once the unsorted data is replaced.
- In **lazy mode**, AxsDB raises a `DataError`. The reason is that a lazily sorted view reads one strided slice per `w` index: a 200-wavelength query on komodo took 45.7 s, compared with 29 ms for a contiguous read.

The warning and error messages tell the user to regenerate the file with ascending `w`. For Eradiate, this means that komodo (and possibly other datasets) should be fixed.

## Performance

Per call, best of 5, on the US standard atmosphere:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| nanomono eager loop | 709 µs | 728 µs |
| nanomono lazy loop | 980 µs | 996 µs |
| komodo eager loop | 997 µs (NaN) | 962 µs |

## Tests

- `test_eval_mono_unsorted_spectral_grid`: an unsorted copy of `nanomono_v1`, in eager mode, warns and matches the sorted database.
- `test_eval_mono_unsorted_spectral_grid_lazy`: the same copy raises `DataError` in lazy mode.

## Follow-up

- The komodo file should be regenerated with a sorted `w` coordinate.
- Not checked: whether other Eradiate mono databases have an unsorted `w`, or whether the CKD path makes similar ordering assumptions.

author: jnszkr
body:
Gives applications control over how JetStream consumers are created and how messages are sent, received and settled, on every transport. Dead letter queues, custom ack handling, authentication headers and retries can now be built in application code, and `jsbroker` no longer has configuration of its own.

## What changes

### Consumers in `jsbroker`
- **Existing consumers**: `jsbroker.From(cons, opts...)` keeps its signature.
- **Factories**: `jsbroker.FromFactory(f, interceptors...)` takes a `ConsumerFactory`, or a function through `ConsumerFunc`. The factory gets the subscription's subject and queue, and returns the consumer with its consume options. `Existing(cons, opts...)` turns a consumer you already have into a factory.
- **No broker configuration**: `jsbroker.New(js)` takes no options, and the broker no longer adds a `ConsumeErrHandler`. `jsbroker.WithErrorHandler` and `jsbroker.Option` are removed.

### JetStream interceptors
A `jsbroker.Interceptor` wraps the delivery of each message and sees the `jetstream.Msg` and the handler's error. It can return a different error to change the outcome, settle the message itself (for example with `NakWithDelay`), or pass a derived context to the handler.

### Client interceptors, for every transport
These are options on the generated constructors, so they cover core NATS pub/sub, request/reply and JetStream:

| Option | Wraps |
|---|---|
| `broker.WithPublishInterceptors` | publishing, including the replies of a `Server` |
| `broker.WithRequestInterceptors` | sending a request and waiting for its reply |
| `broker.WithReceiveInterceptors` | decoding and handling a received message, including requests |

They get the `*broker.Message`, so they can add or override headers, and also change the subject or data. Received messages and replies without headers now get an empty `Header`, so setting one doesn't panic.

## Things to review

- A failed default ack is no longer reported, and consume errors go only to a `jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler` the application passes. An interceptor that settles a message itself gets the ack error.
- JetStream interceptors are set per subscription and only through `FromFactory`, since the variadic argument of `From` is the consume options. They run outside the client's receive interceptors.
- Core NATS has no redelivery, so the error a receive interceptor returns goes nowhere there.
- A `Server` sends handler errors to the requester, so its receive interceptors see `nil` for those.
- Dead-lettering as in the README examples is at-least-once: on JetStream, if the DLQ publish succeeds and the ack then fails, the message can reach the DLQ twice.

## Testing

`golangci-lint`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass. New tests cover factories, dead-lettering on JetStream and core NATS, an interceptor settling a message itself, interceptor order and context, request/reply headers over a real NATS server, request retries, overriding headers, and setting headers on messages that arrive without any. `natsbroker` had no tests before this.

body:
## First usable laptop GGUF acceptance — operational blocker repair (DRAFT)

The real-turn CLI previously called `first_turn_acceptance.run(..., approved=True)` without `installed_receipt` or `require_real=True`. The canonical verifier therefore returned synthetic/unverified source evidence, so real GGUF first-turn qualification **could never succeed**. Conversely, the CLI inferred rights and source safety from truthy report fields without a final installed-source witness.

**Implemented:**
- Require canonical installed GGUF model receipt, strict booleans, exact tenant/subject/model/tokenizer and independently inspected live isolated child/resource lease before inference.
- Pass **the actual installed receipt** with `require_real=True` into the single authoritative `first_turn_acceptance`; require exact source snapshot, fresh generated tokens, committed SQLite replay, trusted model digest and false release grant in the return record.
- For cold-reopen acceptance, fully close first worker, independently activate a new worker, refuse reused stack/worker or changed owner/source epoch, perform exactly one **read-only** SQLite replay and verify the digest with no second model effect.
- Publish the bounded result inside the still-live worker context through `emit_native_jsonl`; preserve private prompt bytes verbatim, deny invalid CLI args/paths/shape before stdin reads, redact errors. A short write or source revocation does not retry uncertain native work.
- Keep canonical Jeeves and governed mirror as identical source blobs; update `AIFT-JEEVES` to exact new source Git-tree SHA.
- Replace older misleading synthetic proof tests with explicit, isolated mock witnesses and 22+ adversarial tests including real-source receipt wiring, cold-reopen independence, rights/owner/source denial, output custody and private-input admission. CI now includes the acceptance tests.

**Qualification holds:** Source-only tests, GitHub checks and model/source report witnesses cannot certify actual model rights, installed consumer weights, physical device pressure, Windows 11/WSL2 or release. This draft and all ancestors remain held until full independent exact-head gates and a real approved GGUF native turn are verified.

author: mackery6969
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Mackery6969"} -->
_Requested by **Mackery** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JwkM9STZ6KtuHT6gx6b24g?thread=cmsg_01JwkM9STZ6KtuHT6gx6b24gLsedKtZwR4xfVCwMyeRt5p)_

## The crash

The host crashed with `0xC0000005 at smg_game.dll+0xd680f, address 0x8` when the other player spun next to them.

In the main CI build (`windows-game-module` from run 41787481248, the one for 86959d9c), `+0xd680f` is the first instruction of `MultiEmitter::create(EffectSystem*)`: `cmp dword ptr [rcx+0x8], 0`, reading `mEmitters.mMaxSize` of a null `MultiEmitter`. The function just before it is `MultiEmitter::createEmitter()`, so something emitted an effect its actor doesn't have.

That was the remote copy's spin light. `NebulaRemotePlayer` started it as `スピンライト`, the local Mario's name for it. But only `MarioActor` renames his effects (`MarioEffect`'s `setEffectName("SpinLight", "スピンライト")` and the rest). A copy's `EffectKeeper` holds them under the names in Mario's effect list (`SpinLight`, `IceMarioSpinLight`, `FireMarioSpinLight`, `BeeMarioSpinLight`, `BeeLuigiSpinLight`). So the copy registered none of them, `getEmitter` came back null, and the first spin crashed the game watching it.

## The fix

- The copies' effect table uses the list names, so `init` registers the spin effects and spins start and stop them.
- Starting and stopping go through `MR::tryEmitEffect` / `MR::tryDeleteEffect`, so an effect a copy lacks is skipped instead of crashing.
- The early stop for the air spin uses the copy's own effect name (Bee Luigi's for him).

No version numbers changed.

## Testing

- `NebulaRemotePlayer.cpp` compiles in the game module build (clang, Linux).
- Not played: there's no disc in the cloud box. Needs a 2-player check: spin, air spin, and Fire/Ice/Bee spins next to the other player. Each should show its spin light on the other player's copy.

author: brett6320-agent1
body:
## Profile selection
When several profiles map to an account, prefer the one starting with `--profile-prefix` (default `hcli-`, env `PROXY_INV_PROFILE_PREFIX`; empty turns it off).

Order: `--account-profile` > `--profile` > single prefix match (several → read-only one among them) > read-only rule > error. `resolve_profile`, `scan` and `scan_account` take a `prefix` kwarg.

**Behavior change:** `hcli-` now beats the read-only rule. For `{hcli-acct-admin, acct-ro}` the tool now picks `hcli-acct-admin` instead of `acct-ro`, so by default it may use a broader role than before. The tool only reads, so nothing breaks. This also diverges from `ou_vpcs`; the README says so.

## Rate limit retry
Reads that still fail with a throttling error or HTTP 429 after botocore's adaptive retries (5 attempts) are retried up to 3 more times with exponential backoff and jitter. This covers each collector, the subnet/VPC/ENI reads and the STS identity check. All are reads, so a retry has no side effects.

## Tests
25 pass locally. New: `test_resolve_profile_prefix`, `test_retry_throttled`.

author: doguto
body:
Closes #267

## 原因
- `ScreenBoundsCache`（プレイヤーの移動範囲・画面外判定・`BattleWallPresenter` の壁の位置などに使う画面端）は、`BattleScenePresenter.Awake` で一度だけ計算されている。
- 新しく読み込まれたバトルシーンのカメラは Viewport Rect が `(0,0,1,1)` のままで、`GlobalScenePresenter.Update` で 16:9 の Rect に補正されるのは**その後**。
- そのため Awake の時点では `camera.aspect` がウィンドウ自体のアスペクト比になっており、ウィンドウが 16:9 でないと画面端が実際の描画領域より広く計算されていた。
  - 縦長のウィンドウなら上下、横長なら左右に可動範囲が広がり、プレイヤーなどが黒帯の中（画面外）へはみ出す。
- Issue の「ポーズ画面でウィンドウを小さくする」→ リトライ等でバトルシーンを読み直すと、この状態になる。

## 修正内容
- `ScreenBoundsCache.Initialize` で、計算の間だけ `camera.aspect` を 16:9 にして画面端を求め、その後 `ResetAspect()` で元に戻すようにした。
  - 描画領域は常に 16:9 に固定されているので、ウィンドウサイズに関係なく正しい画面端になる。
- `GlobalScenePresenter.TargetAspect` に、`ScreenBoundsCache` も同じ値を前提にしている旨のコメントを追加。

### ポーズ画面の装飾が黒帯部分に見える問題（追加）
- `PauseModal` の Canvas は Screen Space - Overlay のため、カメラの Viewport Rect による 16:9 補正の影響を受けずウィンドウ全体に描画される。
- 装飾 `ornament (1)` は X=-450 にオフセット＋Scale 64 で配置されており、16:9 の枠から左へ約 450px はみ出していたため、横長ウィンドウでは黒帯上に見えていた。
- `Global` シーンの `PauseModal/Canvas/AspectFrame` に `RectMask2D`（Padding / Softness = 0）を追加し、16:9 の枠外の描画をクリップするようにした。
  - ボタン本体は SpriteRenderer のため RectMask2D の対象外だが、枠内に配置されているため影響なし。
- `GameOverModal` / `OptionModal` / `TutorialModal` / `BgmNameCanvas` も同様の構成（Overlay + AspectFrame、マスク無し）だが、本 PR では未対応。

この対応のため `Global.unity` を変更しています（RectMask2D の追加のみ）。

## 確認してほしいこと（Unity エディター / ビルドで確認）
- [ ] ウィンドウを 16:9 以外（縦長・横長の両方）にしてからバトルを開始し、プレイヤーが黒帯の中に入れないこと
- [x] ポーズ中にウィンドウを小さくする → リトライ後も同様に、画面外へはみ出さないこと
- [ ] 16:9 のウィンドウでは、これまでと動きが変わらないこと
- [ ] 16:9 以外のウィンドウでポーズ画面を開いたとき、装飾が黒帯部分に表示されないこと

author: ayolyn
body:
Closes #15

### 📌 Summary of Changes
Implements the `update_job_config(env: Env, job_id: u64, new_interval_seconds: u64, new_bounty_per_run: i128)` entrypoint on `JobEngine`, allowing job owners to adjust interval and bounty settings without cancelling and re-creating jobs.

### 🛠️ Detailed Implementation
1. **Entrypoint & Validation**:
   - Added `update_job_config` on `JobEngine` enforcing `job.owner.require_auth()`.
   - Validates `new_interval_seconds >= MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (5 seconds), rejecting lower intervals with `EngineError::InvalidInterval`.
   - Validates `new_bounty_per_run > 0`, rejecting non-positive bounties with `EngineError::InvalidBounty`.
   - Restricts updates to `Active` and `Paused` jobs only; rejects updates on `Cancelled` or `Completed` jobs with `EngineError::JobNotActive`.
   - Updates record in persistent storage and extends instance TTL.
2. **Event Emission**:
   - Added `emit_job_config_updated` in `contracts/job-engine/src/events.rs` publishing `((symbol_short!("job_upd"), job_id), (owner, new_interval_seconds, new_bounty_per_run))`.
3. **Unit Tests**:
   - Added `test_update_job_config_and_subsequent_execution` in `contracts/job-engine/src/test.rs` verifying:
     - Invalid interval rejection with `EngineError::InvalidInterval`.
     - Zero/negative bounty rejection with `EngineError::InvalidBounty`.
     - Live execution rewards reflect the newly updated bounty amount immediately on the next execution.
     - Configuration adjustments allowed during `Paused` state.
     - Rejection of configuration updates on `Cancelled` jobs.

 Waits and stacks now have distinct jobs, as you described. A wait is for a separate feature that needs another task's code merged first. A stack is for pieces that ship at once. Waits: the triage classifier's `waits_on` question allows only three kinds, `needs_its_code`, `asked_for` and `shared_rewrite`. author: yobazy
body:
The Playwright MCP writes `.playwright-mcp/` into the checkout it runs in, and git doesn't ignore it. Those untracked files count as uncommitted changes, so moment auto clean up (#138) skips the worktree, and the Clean up button asks for **Clean up anyway**.

This adds `.playwright-mcp/` to `.gitignore`. Checked with `git check-ignore`. Only `.gitignore` changes, so there's nothing to build or test here; CI runs as usual.

author: gunkl
body:
Fixes #1325

## What the occupant experiences

**Before:**
- Two thermostat changes within 5 minutes (for example Cool, then Off) logged only the first. The household-promise check then said Climate Advisor "ended your manual thermostat change 13 min early", which made the nightly fail. The newer change was never checked as protected.
- Moving the setpoint while the thermostat was Off was treated as a manual change. That is impossible on real thermostats (owner ruling).

**After:**
- Every distinct change is recorded and checked.
- A whole-house-fan timer change while the fan is running (1 h → 4 h) is checked as protected too. That was a real gap found by the mirror check: a Climate Advisor stop during that run would not have been flagged.
- A setpoint-only change while Off is ignored.

## Changes

- **Generator** (`tools/sim_harness/generator.py`): an occupant Off carries no setpoint, so nothing generates the impossible input. No random draws changed, so other events of every seed are identical. A scan test enforces it.
- **Coordinator:** a setpoint-only change while the live mode is Off is ignored, with no override, confirmation or grace (DEBUG log).
- **Removed** (only served the impossible case; reachability traced):
  - `_occupant_mode_when_ca_holds_off()`;
  - the #1131 and #1157(b) handling;
  - the #1313 occupant-mode restore chain;
  - `_protected_change_source()`.

  Mode-change protections are unchanged: #1165(a), `handle_manual_override_during_pause()`, #1133/#1146/#1147/#1148/#1152, and #1308/#1312/#1314.
- **`override_detected` dedup:** only an identical repeat (same source, detected mode, new mode and setpoint) within 5 minutes is suppressed.
- **`promise_journal.derive_episodes`:** a superseded `grace_cancelled` (continues False) closes only override episodes, thermostat or fan, that started at or before the cancelled grace. It never closes a newer change's episode.
  - Why the old semantics were wrong: they attributed a cancel to an episode the cancelled grace never protected.
  - Negative controls keep P4 able to catch a cancel of the newer change's own grace, and a missing grace followed by a Climate Advisor write.
- **Docs:** `grace-periods-spec.md`, `household-promises-spec.md`, `08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md`, `00-PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.md` anchors, `activity-report-table.md`, `06-LOGGING-GUIDELINES.md`.
- **Release:** 0.8.59 (CHANGELOG, fix history).

## Verification

- **Tests:**
  - unit: dedup, both fan modes and both paths; journal, thermostat and fan mirror with real engine order;
  - coordinator guard;
  - generator scan;
  - seed 8002000056;
  - HA tier: `tests_ha/test_second_change_p4_1325.py`.
- **Revert checks:** each layer (generator, guard, dedup, journal thermostat and fan) fails its tests when reverted.
- **Full local run** after the last production change: unit 12,080 passed (7 skipped, 1 xfailed); HA 462 passed; golden integrity OK (93); ruff clean.
- **After merging current main:** the merge was clean with no overlapping files, so CI validates it.

body:
## Summary
- Switch from `containrrr/watchtower` to `nickfedor/watchtower`. The original repo was archived in December 2025 and its image has not changed since January 2024. The fork is actively maintained (v1.24.0) and keeps the same opt-in label and environment variables.
- Drop `DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.40`: the fork negotiates the API version (v1.56 on Docker 29). With the pin, an increase of Docker's minimum API version would have broken Watchtower silently.
- Run at 05:00 instead of 03:00, after the nightly backups and the unattended OS upgrades with their reboots, which also started at 03:00.
- Add the opt-in label to Watchtower itself so it updates itself.
- README: link to the fork, new schedule, and an "Updates" section.

## Verification
- One-off `--run-once --monitor-only` run of the fork on the host, with the current settings: it connects to Docker API v1.56, detects new images, and the Telegram notification arrives.
- markdownlint passes; `docker compose config` validates with `.env.example`.

author: mcrha
body:
The xml:lang often uses the BCP 47 form of the language, which is different from the locale (CLDR), thus when for example the XML file has `xml:lang="zh-CN"`, the passed in locale "zh_CN" into the `xb_builder_add_locale()` won't match the attribute.

As the `xb_builder_add_locale()` explicitly expects locales, the conversion should happen in it, not by the callers.

The conversion is based on the information from:  
https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/49/tr35.html#unicode-locale-identifier-cldr-to-bcp-47

-----------------------

This fixes https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-software/-/work_items/2920

author: parthashirolkar
body: ## Why The iOS keyboard drew a full letter layout, but its only real job is to start a Dictation in the app's keyboard session and insert the transcript. The letter keys took up space and made it look like a regular keyboard. Agent Mode also couldn't be reached from the keyboard at all. ## What changed **Keyboard UI (`KeyboardViewController.swift`).** The letter keys are gone. The home screen has a status line with the session countdown, a **Dictate** row (blue), an **Ask the agent** row (vermilion), and backspace. The globe key only appears when `needsInputModeSwitchKey` asks for it. Tapping a row turns the whole keyboard into a recording screen: - The row's surface springs out to fill the keyboard. - Its icon tile becomes a 96pt stop button. - Cancel and Delete slide out from behind the stop button. - Level bars and a timer fade in. The motion uses critically damped `UIView.animate(springDuration:bounce:)` with `.beginFromCurrentState`, so a tap mid-animation retargets instead of jumping. Reduce Motion switches to cross-fades. Buttons press in on touch-down. Level bars only redraw when the app sends a reading, so nothing animates continuously. Colors come from `DESIGN.md`. **Session protocol (both `KeyboardSessionProtocol.swift` copies, kept identical).** - `Command` carries a `mode` (`dictate` | `agent`). - `State` carries `mode`, `agentReady`, and `level`. - `insertion` only returns text for `dictate`, so an agent transcript can never be typed at the cursor. **App side.** - `KeyboardSessionHost` streams normalized mic levels over the socket at 15Hz while recording. It only uses the socket, never the JS bridge. - An agent request is held in `transcribing` until JS admits it through `resolveKeyboardAgentRequest`. The keyboard shows "Sent to the agent" only after the run has actually started. A busy or unconfigured agent, or 10s with no admission, shows an error instead. - `controller.ts` runs admitted requests through the existing Agent Mode path (approvals, saved answers, activity). In-app recording is blocked while a keyboard session is active. - `agentReady` is computed in `useMobileApp.ts`. When it is false, the agent row is dimmed and explains why. Agent runs started from the background use notifications instead of a Live Activity, because iOS won't create one from the background. No before/after screenshots or motion video yet: this was built on Windows with no simulator. They will come from the Release IPA below. ## Testing 1. `bun test mobile/src/__tests__/keyboard-agent.test.ts mobile/src/__tests__/controller.test.ts`: all pass. 2. `bun run --cwd mobile typecheck` and `bun run --cwd mobile lint`: clean. 3. `cmp mobile/modules/shuddhalekhan-speech/ios/KeyboardSessionProtocol.swift mobile/targets/transcript-keyboard/KeyboardSessionProtocol.swift`: no output. 4. Build a Release IPA with the EAS `sideloadly` profile, install it, start a keyboard session in the app, then open Notes and switch to the Shuddhalekhan keyboard (Full Access on). 5. Tap **Dictate**: the row expands into the shutter and the level bars follow your voice. Tap stop: the text is inserted once at the cursor and the shutter folds back into the row. Repeat in a second app. 6. Tap **Ask the agent**, speak, then stop: "Sent to the agent" appears with your words quoted, then the shutter folds back. The answer arrives as a notification, and approvals still work. 7. Turn Agent Mode off in the app: the agent row is dimmed and tapping it explains how to set it up. Turn on Reduce Motion: the screens cross-fade. 8. Tap Cancel mid-recording, hide and reopen the keyboard, and let the session expire. Each one returns to the home screen with no stuck state. Built by Claude Opus 5.5 (keyboard UI) and Codex (protocol and app side) in Claude Code via T3 Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * The keyboard now offers Dictate and Ask the agent modes, with a live recording tray, input-level meter, and clear controls to stop, cancel, or delete. * Dictation inserts the completed transcript; agent responses arrive by notification. Agent requests show a confirmation before handoff. * Keyboard-triggered agent runs can continue after the microphone session ends, with result notifications when appropriate. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved handling of busy requests, unavailable Agent Mode, failed handoffs, and cancellations so requests receive clear outcomes. * **Documentation** * Updated keyboard workflow guidance and added release verification scenarios.

author: kg3ee
body:
## What
Pre-translate about two scrolls ahead so the next screen is ready when the reader gets there. Extension v1.9.3.

- `content.js`: IntersectionObserver `rootMargin` is now `50% 0px 200% 0px` (two screens below, half a screen above).
- `takeBatch()` ranks the queue by distance: on-screen first, then text ahead in the scroll direction nearest first, then text behind nearest first, detached nodes last. One `getBoundingClientRect` per node per call, cached in a Map; the sort only compares numbers. The small fast on-screen batch is unchanged.
- Scroll direction comes from a passive window scroll listener (about 5 lines); when scrolling up, "ahead" and "behind" swap.
- Look-ahead batches are 30 items / 2,500 chars (was 60 / 5,000) and `CONCURRENCY` is 3 (was 2), so the nearest part of the look-ahead lands sooner.
- Header comment, README (look-ahead text, batch numbers, changelog) and manifest version updated.

## Rate limit check
`background.js` has no per-tab concurrency cap. Its only throttle is `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN = 40` requests per minute across all tabs, and it applies to both the OpenRouter and Gemini paths. It sleeps until a slot frees; it never sends a 429. With 3 in flight and smaller batches a fast model may touch that cap on a long scroll, which only delays the request a little. Left unchanged.

## Verified
- `node --test test/openrouter.test.mjs`: 24 pass, 0 fail. `node --check content.js` ok.
- No-network harness on a 200-paragraph page (viewport 1000x800, never-answering shim, ports finished by hand): rootMargin seen as `50% 0px 200% 0px`; scrolling down sent on-screen 8 first, then below nearest-first, then above nearest-first; scrolling up sent on-screen first, then above nearest-first, then below.

## Not verified
- Real translation speed with a live model (no network, e2e skipped).
- Scrolling up only queues half a screen above (the observer margin is fixed); only the send order flips. Scrollers that are not the window do not update the direction (it stays at its last value).

author: jac-zac
body:
**Problem:** `ensure_master` started a standalone `ssh -fN` master. If the control socket path was taken (e.g. a stale socket), that master stayed connected with no client, and `ControlPersist` never expired it. Each poll leaked one more (~24/hour from the background daemon).

**Fix:** drop `ensure_master`. The poll command itself now uses `ControlMaster=auto` + `ControlPersist=10m`, so it reuses a live master or starts one. If the socket is unusable, it just runs the command and exits. One ssh process per poll instead of up to three. Keepalives and the 60s timeout are unchanged.

**Tested:** `cargo test` passes. Live run against the clusters: connections are reused and expire, and nothing is left behind when the socket path is blocked.

author: krijos
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Spending Scattered Stars at pace made Starfire Shot interrupt itself. A shot fired while a previous one was still consuming would break off at the end of its cast, which reads in play as an abrupt stop in the middle of a rotation.

The chain:

1. Starfire Shot 801978 carries `TargetAuraSpell` 804378, so the engine requires a Scattered Star on the target.
2. `Spell::_cast` repeats `CheckCast(false)` when the cast **completes**, not only when it starts.
3. That reaches `SpellInfo::CheckTarget`, which returns `SPELL_FAILED_TARGET_AURASTATE` when `TargetAuraSpell` is set and the target no longer holds the aura.
4. Starfire Shot's own hit starts the consume chain `572315 → StartConsume → 804716`, whose 500 ms ticks drain the target's remaining stars.

So a shot could lose its star during its own 2500 ms cast and be refused on completion — a cast that was legal when the player started it, with no counterplay.

Nothing in the ability asks for the star to persist through the cast: Starfire Shot reads "Consumes Scattered Stars", which describes spending one, and the requirement's purpose is to gate starting the cast. There is precedent for the engine's repeat being too strict for CoA two lines above in the same function, where `SpellInfo::CheckTarget` already tests `TargetAuraState` only for primary targets under `AscensionTargetAuraStateOnlyPrimary`.

The authored `TargetAuraSpell` is therefore cleared for every Starfire Shot rank in `ApplyContracts`, and the star is enforced once at cast start in `OnSpellCheckCast` under its `strict` flag — which `ScriptMgr::OnSpellCheckCast` receives from `CheckCast`: true from `Spell::prepare`, false from the completion repeat. Casting with no star on the target is refused exactly as before.

## Validation and remaining limits

`starcaller-starfire-shot-survives-star-consumption` fails on `main` ("The shot still completes") and passes here. Built and run on its own as well as merged with the other Starcaller fixes, and confirmed in play by the reporter.

The scenario removes the star with `set_aura` one second into the 2500 ms cast rather than racing the consume, which is the same observable condition and deterministic. `spell_cast_count` counts completed casts, recorded from `ALLSPELLHOOK_ON_CAST` which `Spell::_cast` reaches **after** the abort point, so one means the shot survived and zero means it broke off.

Remaining limits: that the requirement still gates *starting* a cast is left to the engine's own behaviour and is not asserted here. Across all 115 Starcaller scenarios this branch leaves the same five failures `main` already has, none of them touched here.

## Data/source dependencies

No SQL: applied SQL is unchanged, and nothing is added under `data/sql`. No DBC row is added or overridden and no `*_dbc` world table is written — `TargetAuraSpell` is cleared at runtime in `ApplyContracts`, so client and server keep reading identical tables. No credentials, profiles or game archives are included.

---

Opened from a fork, so labels cannot be set here. Suggested: `Bug`, `Starcaller`, `Script`, `CPP Edit`, `Class Fix`, `Tested`.

author: aleskalfas
body:
Closes #2639

## What

A decision lands with what it decides, in one pull request and one review, with no exception to the acceptance gate. A new record's Implications name each edit its change makes to an accepted record, and what the edit makes that record say. A person accepts the record in the change that proposes it, and the edits then follow in that change, as work resting on an accepted record. The person who authorises the merge reads each edit before the change lands. COR-066 gains point 5, which decides this. Point 1 keeps main's text. The new point is a person's to accept ("Records to accept" below).

**Drafted before the acceptance.** The files that carry point 5 out, the decisions reference, `decision-author`, the guide, the use cases, CONTRIBUTING and the changeset, were drafted before the maintainer accepted point 5's wording on this pull request. They follow the wording as accepted.

- **COR-066** (`.pkit/decisions/core/COR-066-accepted-before-landing.md`) gains point 5, "A new record lands with its edits", placed after point 1, and its status stays `accepted`:
  - a new decision record's Implications name each edit its change makes to an accepted record, and what the edit makes that record say, and the decision-record specification says which edits those are and how each is made;
  - the edits follow its acceptance, in its change, and not in a change built on it, which may land later;
  - accepting the record accepts the edits its Implications name, and an edit beyond them that changes what a record decides is a decision of its own;
  - the person who authorises the change to land is shown the edits beside point 3's list, by the component that carries out merges or the change's author, and reads each before the change lands;
  - an edit the record forces on a rule of the project's own rule sets is named and made the same way, under COR-051, and one to a rule set the project receives is proposed where it is kept;
  - it decides nothing against a record the project receives from elsewhere, and nothing rests on the change it needs there until the project receives it accepted.

  The plain-terms line, the Context and the Decision's lead say so, and point 4 has points 1 and 5 bind every project. The Rationale gains "Why a new record lands with its edits", and two alternatives are rejected. The Implications name what carries the point out, and say that no command changes.
- **The decisions reference** (`.pkit/decisions/README.md`) states the rule in one bullet of "The acceptance gate", citing COR-066 point 5. Its sub-items say that each name states what the edit makes the record say, who accepts the edits, that they do not wait for a change built on this one, that the person who authorises the merge reads each beside the list of what the change makes accepted, what happens to a record received from elsewhere, and how an edit to a rule is named and made. "Refining an accepted record" counts a widening among refinements, and lists the edits by what the new record does: a record it refines, by each point narrowed, widened, completed or added; one it overturns in part; and one it replaces whole. The rule that a record supersedes only one of its own namespace keeps its one home, in "Statuses".
- **The reference checks already accept such a change.** No code changed. Tests pin it for a refinement, a partial supersession and a whole supersession, each on a repository the test builds, with the record proposed, then accepted, then the edits made:
  - `test_a_new_record_accepted_in_its_change_then_its_edits_pass_and_are_listed` in `tests/test_decisions_check_diff.py`: `pkit decisions check-diff` fails none of the three commits, and lists the edit to the old record once it is made.
  - `test_rot_finds_nothing_where_a_new_record_is_accepted_before_its_edits` in `tests/test_refs.py`: `pkit refs rot` finds nothing at any step. `test_rot_lists_an_edit_made_before_its_new_record_is_accepted` shows it lists an edit made out of order, for a refinement and a partial supersession.
- **`decision-author`** names the edits in the Implications, each with what it makes the record say (step 8). Before the person accepts the record, it shows them the edits' words, drafted in the conversation or the agent workspace and never committed. It commits the acceptance, then the edits as shown, then the work, and before the merge it shows the edits to the person who authorises it where no component that carries out merges does (step 11). It cites COR-066 point 5 for these, and point 1 for the acceptance. Where a record needs a change to a record received from elsewhere, it surfaces that change to the user rather than make it, since proposing it changes another repository (core rule 19, COR-039).
- **The `architect` agent** makes the edits to the records it owns once its ADR is accepted, and leaves any other edit the ADR's Implications name to whoever makes the change. Its deployed copy, `.claude/agents/architect.md`, is redeployed.
- **batch-plan's** records-first step lets a record that serves one Task ride that Task. A person accepts it in the Task's change before the Task's work (COR-066 point 1) and its edits (point 5) follow. A refused record closes the change and sends the Task back to be planned. A record that changes a foundation's record does not ride a Task: the change goes through a Task of its own (DEC-060 point 5). The pm skill reads COR-066.
- **The decisions guide** (`docs/decisions/README.md`), **UC-037**, **UC-040** and **CONTRIBUTING** follow the order:
  - the guide's reader reads the edits the Implications name, the change makes them in the reader's own records only after the acceptance, and whoever authorises the merge is shown them and reads each before it lands;
  - UC-037 gains variants 1e (a record that narrows, widens or completes another, its Implications saying what each edit makes the old record say, a received record included) and 9c (accept, then the edits in the project's own records, each read by the merge authoriser before the change lands), and 1d points to 9c;
  - UC-040's 2a reads the edits, and its 6a makes those to the project's own records after the acceptance, each read by the merge authoriser before the change lands;
  - both use cases cite and anchor COR-066 point 5;
  - CONTRIBUTING's step for a new core record says its named edits follow the maintainer's acceptance, and anchors COR-066 point 5.
- **The backbone changeset is `minor`.** Every project's new records gain an obligation, and the authoring skill's procedure changes, which an adopter sees (PRJ-002 D2).

Project-management DEC-063's Implications are the precedent.

## Records accepted

COR-066 gains point 5, and point 4 changes; its status stays `accepted`. The maintainer accepted the edit on this pull request. `pkit decisions check-diff` lists it as "point 4 (A project turns the refusal on) altered, point 5 (A new record lands with its edits) added, the text its points stand on altered and its other text altered". Point 1 is not altered.

Point 5, placed after point 1:

> ### 5. A new record lands with its edits
>
> A new decision record's Implications name each edit its change makes to an accepted record, one the new record refines, overturns in part or replaces whole. Each name states what the edit makes that record say, not only where the edit goes. The decision-record specification says which edits those are, and how each is made.
>
> These edits rest on the new record, so they follow its acceptance, in its change. They do not go in a change built on that one, which may land later and leave the records disagreeing until it does. Accepting the new record accepts the edits its Implications name. An edit beyond them that changes what a record decides is a decision of its own, which stays a person's ([COR-064](COR-064-answer-delegate.md) point 6).
>
> The person who authorises the change to land is shown these edits beside point 3's list, in the same way: by the compone

author: haxmarris
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"HaxMarris"} -->
_Requested by **Maxwell** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WizQJXFFg3WDaZ46YPE8cM?thread=cmsg_01WizQJXFFg3WDaZ46YPE8cMAAGNyY5JHg8JYXfDDprzDL)_

This PR covers two rounds of ideas: round 2 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8) and round 3 (1 to 6, plus copying and saving pictures).

## Round 2

### Invite links (server and client)
- `/invite/<code>` now returns a small page with link-preview tags for chat apps: the hearth's name, its picture (or the app icon) and its description. A personal invite's title says "Sam invited you to Den". The page then opens the app as before. Bad or expired codes still open the app with no tags, and they count toward the same guessing limit as `/api/invites/:code`.
- `/api/invites/:code` returns `invitedBy` for personal invites whose creator is still a member, and the invite card says "Sam invited you to". Covered in `organization.test.ts`.

### Accessibility
These fixes come from an axe-core scan of sign-in, a room, Home and Your account, in light and dark:
- Offline member names and the light theme's buttons now meet contrast. `--accent` is one shade deeper (#b9501a).
- `#modal` is a named dialog, and the yes/no layer is an `alertdialog`.
- The theme buttons use radio semantics only.
- The side panels have names, and the message list can be scrolled with the keyboard.
- New messages from others in the open room are read out through a separate polite live region, instead of the whole message list being a live region.

### Screens and speed check (CI)
New job `Screens and speed` in `checks.yml`, which runs `.github/scripts/ui-check.mjs`:
- It opens sign-in, a room (and the chat on phones), Home and settings at computer and phone size, in light and dark, against a demo server.
- It fails on page errors, sideways scrolling on phones, or serious or critical axe violations. Screens are uploaded as the `screens` artifact.
- Speed budget: a cold open on 4G with a 4x slower CPU has to show a room within 3.5s (about 2.1s now) and load under 600 kB compressed (about 415 kB now).

### First week on Home
- New accounts see a "Getting started" list on Home for their first 7 days. Each step ticks itself off and opens the right place when tapped, and the Home button shows a dot while steps are left.

### Phone swipes
- Swipe-to-reply and edge-swipe-back now follow the finger, with a reply arrow and a haptic tap at the point where the swipe counts.

## Round 3

### Copy and save pictures
- Right-click a picture (or hold it on a phone) to get Copy picture, Save picture and Open in new tab. The lightbox has Copy and Save buttons too.
- Copying converts the picture to PNG so the clipboard accepts it. On phones, Save uses the share sheet (which offers Save Image).

### Picture descriptions (alt text)
- A pending picture has a Describe button. The description is stored on the attachment (`attachments.alt`, up to 1000 characters), used as the image's `alt`, shown in the lightbox, and kept when the message is forwarded. Covered in `chat-extras.test.ts`.

### Share invites
- Where the browser or app supports it, a Share button sits beside the invite link's Copy and opens the native share sheet.

### Drafts across devices
- A draft saves to the server (new `drafts` table) about a second after you stop typing, and the server pushes it to your other devices, which show it in that room. Sending the message clears it everywhere.
- Server timestamps decide which draft is newer. An incoming draft never overwrites a room you're typing in. Covered in `chat-extras.test.ts`.

### Send feedback
- Send feedback in the menu: text, an optional screenshot (pick or paste one; shrunk to a JPEG under about 700 kB), and the app and device, which can be unticked.
- It is stored in a new `feedback` table (newest 300; 10 an hour per person) and shown in a new Feedback tab in Server admin, with Mark done and Delete. Covered in `hosting.test.ts`.

### Shaped placeholders
- The 14 "Loading…" texts in lists and panels are now grey shapes like the content coming in (cards, lines or an emoji grid), with `role="status"`.

### Error messages
- About 40 terse server errors now say what happened and what to do, in the app's own words. For example: "That message is gone. It may have been deleted.", "This invite has run out. Ask for a new one." and "Fires aren't set up on this server yet. Tell whoever runs it."
- The client goes by status codes, so no behaviour changes. One test's expected wording is updated.

### What's new
- Added five lines for this round.

## Checks
- `node scripts/check-client.mjs`: OK, ESLint clean
- `npm test` (server): 186 pass. `tsc`: clean
- Checked in the browser: the feedback form and admin tab, placeholders, picture menu and share button on phone width.

author: jordangarrison
body:
## Summary

```text
cloudflare-zero-wire-changes (Python stdlib, packaged in home.packages)
  RSS → pending new/updated/moved briefings → explicit ack
zero-wire skill
  read-only FloSports exposure assessment → action-only answer
  jagpi routine delivers the answer; no direct Slack sends
```

The script is byte-identical to the reviewed reference apart from its name and state directory. Nix's Python writer ignores E501 (long help text) and E265 (the retained original shebang after the writer's shebang). The skill defines the untrusted-feed boundary, evidence and verdict rules, update comparison, backlog review, memory, and per-item acknowledgement. Jagpi's schedule/bot work stays in jagpi#101.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no packaged Zero Wire change detector or repo-owned assessment skill.
  **After:** package builds; built `cloudflare-zero-wire-changes --help` works; live `list` with temporary `--state` returns six briefings. Real state untouched.
- Temporary-fixture smoke tests pass: new/retry, explicit acknowledgement, handled list, unknown GUID, moved section, updated GUID, six-failure alert threshold, and recovery reset.
- `nh os build . --no-nom` passes. No `test` or `switch` run.
- Documented narrow Home Manager check passes: `nix eval --raw '.#homeConfigurations."jordangarrison@normandy".activationPackage.drvPath'`.
- Full `nix flake check` is blocked in the unchanged `tests/hermes-runtime.nix:7`: missing `config.systemd.services.hermes-gateway`. No unrelated fix included.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Adds a CLI and a skill. No schedule, service mutation, configuration apply, or Slack post. Rollback removes both; its state stays in the user's state directory.

**Blast Radius:** agent-tooling


**Follow-ups on this branch:** the tool is now `cloudflare-zero-wire-changes`. It never polls: jagpi's schedule is the only timer, and each run reports what changed since the last ack. State lives in `~/.local/state/cloudflare-zero-wire/`. The skill now tells the bot to post standard Markdown, since jagpi posts `markdown_text`, and to keep only not-exposed verdicts in memory.

## Summary

- bump `onnx-shape-inference` to 0.4.2
- prepare the patch release for bounded symbolic-data propagation on large packed integer tensors
- include the Ruff 0.17.3 maintenance update merged since v0.4.1

## Changes since v0.4.1

### New features

- No new operators, public APIs, or user-facing inference capabilities were added in this patch release.

### Fixes and performance

- Cap internal symbolic integer data materialization and metadata propagation at 1,024 elements, preventing large packed weights and index tensors from being expanded into Python lists and JSON metadata while preserving shape and dtype inference.
- Apply the bound before Concat fallback-symbol allocation and Gather index/data reads, including cumulative and symbolic-length cases.
- Invalidate stale context-generated constants when propagated symbolic data changes, without modifying model-owned or caller-replaced constants.
- Preserve bounded symbolic-data behavior inside local functions and at scalar, empty, and exact-limit boundaries.

### Documentation and maintenance

- Document the 1,024-element symbolic-data propagation bound and behavior for larger tensors.
- Update Ruff from 0.17.2 to 0.17.3.

- `pytest -q`: 3,865 passed, 88 skipped, 84 subtests passed
- `lintrunner -a --output oneline`: passed
- `python -m build`: passed

author: jet-pang
body:
Fixes #229
Refs aster-cloud/aster-lang-ts#273（同名分支 `sweep/rule-call-checks`，parity CI 互相取用）、aster-cloud/aster-lang-ts#266、aster-cloud/aster-lang-ts#268

## 背景
TS 侧（#273）的原则是：类型检查不对能正确运行的代码报错，拿不准时放行。本 PR 让 Java TypeChecker 的规则调用检查向 TS 靠拢。按用户裁决，整数可以传给需要小数的位置。

## 改动
| 项 | 之前（Java） | 现在 |
|---|---|---|
| `half(n)`（Float ← Int）、`big(5)`（Long ← Int 字面量）、`half(m)`（Float ← Long）、`half(1.5)`（Float ← Double） | E001 | 放行 |
| `money(n)`（Decimal ← Int / Long） | E001 | 放行（整数到 Decimal 无损；Double → Decimal 仍拒绝，ADR 0025） |
| `List of Int` → `List of Float`、`Some(n)` → `Option of Float`、`Result of Int and Text` → `Result of Float and Text`、`(Int) -> Int` → `(Int) -> Float` | E001 | 放行（容器协变；函数类型形参逆变、返回协变） |
| `Text` → `Text?`、`None` → `Text?`、`Text?` ↔ `Option of Text`、`Some(n)` → `Option of Int` | E001 | 放行（`Option of T` 等 TypeApp 写法比较前归一为结构化类型） |
| `label("a")`（`given amount` 未写类型）、lambda `function with x` 的 `f(flag)` | E001 `expected Float/String …` | 放行（形参一侧按名字推断的类型视为 Unknown） |
| `inc(amount)`、`Let y be amount. inc(y)`（实参只按名字推断） | E001 `expected Int, got Float` | 放行（实参一侧同样视为 Unknown） |
| `inc(mk(n))`，`mk` 写 `produce:` 且推断失败 | E001 `got String`（按规则名猜的占位） | 放行 |
| `twice(bump, n)`，`bump` 未写类型形参 + `produce:` | E001 `got (Float) -> String` | 放行 |
| `Rule ap given f, n as Int … f(n)` | E001 `expected String, got (Int) -> Int`（调用方） | 放行 |
| 泛型规则 `id of T`：`inc(id(n))`、`twice(id, n)`、`unwrap(Some(n), n)` | E001 `expected T, got Int` | 放行（类型参数不按字面类型名比较，与 TS 放行含类型变量的形参一致） |
| 泛型实参之间的一致性：`inc(id(t))`（t 为 Text）、`pick(t, 1)`（a、b 都是 T） | `inc(id(t))` 报 E001（理由是错的） | **不检查**，会放过真实错误；两引擎一致，待统一实现泛型合一后再收紧 |
| #268 `Rule main given score as Int … score(1, 2)`、`n(1)`、`Let score be 1. score(n)` | 无诊断 | E001 `expected a function, got 'score' of type Int`（与 TS 同码同文案） |
| 局部名与 truffle 单段 builtin 同名：`given add as Int … add(1, 2)`、`Let sub be 3. sub(5, n)` | 无诊断 | 仍无诊断（truffle 在调用位置先分派 builtin，能正常运行；名单见 `CallTargetBuiltins`，与 TS 同一份） |

仍然拒绝（均有守护用例）：`inc("a")`、Float / Long → Int、`Option of Int` → Int、`List of Text` → `List of Int`、`Int?` → `Int`、`Some(t)` → `Option of Int`、Double ↔ Decimal（变量与字面量），以及 E012 / E002 的收窄（Float → Int、`Text?` → Text、`Int?` → Int）。

**唯一变严的方向**：调用一个既不是 builtin、也不是规则的非函数局部名（#268 E001）。生产上发版前由 R55 扫描规则 C 检查这类版本。执行门禁 enforce 下，命中的版本会整体返回 422。

实现：
- `TypeSystem.isSubtype` 承载上述可赋值规则；`checkCall` 改用它比较实参。
- **E012（字段构造）与 E002（Set）也随之放行**数值拓宽和可空：这两处本来就调用 `isSubtype`。字段构造上原注释写的「允许 Int → Float」以前并未生效。TS 的 E012 / E002 待跟进，跟进前会出现 TS 比 Java 严的组合（编辑器红、保存通过）。
- 诊断文本打印原始形参 / 实参类型，比较用的擦除形式（如 `List<Unknown>`）不会出现在消息里。
- `CallTargetBuiltins.NAMES` 镜像 truffle `Builtins` 中不带点的注册名。`CallTargetBuiltinsTruffleSyncTest` 在能找到 truffle 源码时（`-Daster.truffle.dir`、`ASTER_TRUFFLE_DIR` 或同级目录）逐项核对，本地已对 truffle main 核对通过。
- 「只按名字推断」用一张按引用识别的类型实例登记表（`BaseTypeChecker.uncheckedForCalls`）表示，不改 IR。只在实参比较和「调用目标是否为函数」两处换成 Unknown；悬浮提示、函数体内的检查、其余诊断都不变。

## 语料影响（aster-lang-test origin/main，454 份）
AstBuilder → CoreLowering → TypeChecker，main（`6d002ab`）与本分支对比，zh / de / hi 用 locales 1.0.38 语言包规范化：
- **新增诊断：0**
- 消失 206 条，涉及 21 个文件。133 条 E001 `expected String, got <T>`（实参传给未写类型的形参，形参按名字推断为 Text），64 条 E012 `Field … expects Float, got Int/Double`，5 条 E001 `expected Float, got Int`，4 条 E001 `expected DateTime, got String`
- 未纳入对比：31 份 tier1-reject 与 49 份 tier3 TS 专用夹具 Java 解析不了（main 与本分支相同）

## 既有差异
另开 #233：`When Some(v)` 报 E104、未声明的 `add(1, 2)` 报 E101、PII 实参多报 E001。

## 未改动，需另行跟进（名字推断还影响以下诊断，两引擎行为待统一）
- 未写类型的 data 字段，在构造时仍按推断类型比较（语料里仍有约 139 条 E012，例如 `expects String, got Int`）
- `Rule f given amount, produce Int: Return amount.` 报 E003；`If approved_status:` 报 E001 `expected Bool, got Text`；`Set y to amount` 报 E002
- 函数返回位不做数值拓宽：`produce Float: Return 1.` 报 E003，`produce Text?: Return None.` 也报 E003（TS 的 module.ts 同样用 typesEqual，两引擎一致）

## 验证
- `./gradlew check`：2293 项测试，0 失败（新增 `RuleCallArgumentCheckTest` 41 项与 `CallTargetBuiltinsTruffleSyncTest`，均先写测试、确认变红后再实现）
- 语料对比在审查跟进后重跑：仍然新增 0、消失 206
- parity：CI 的 checkout-sibling 会取 aster-lang-ts 的同名分支 `sweep/rule-call-checks`（#273）

## 发版
需要发 core 版本，并和 core#230 / truffle#158 同批。合并前不要跑发版列车（列车会自动部署 aster-api）。

   - 證據狀態嚴格隔離：身分未確認標籤固定為 `身分未確認 · 條件相符之候選`，`identity_verdict: "UNCONFIRMED"`。

2. **追蹤單畫面／多畫面視圖模型（Tracking Single/Multi-view）** (`frontend/workbench-v2/core-search-track-model.mjs`):
   - 實作 `buildCoreTrackingViewModel(trackResponse, options)`：將 `q-core.track-response.v1` 接通播放時間 `tUs` 與播放模式。
   - **單畫面切鏡（Single-view）**：根據 `single_view` 在 `tUs` 判定當前啟用鏡頭；`ON_CAMERA` 顯示 `OBSERVED 追蹤中`，`GAP` 顯示 `盲區間隔（未見目標）`，`LOST` 顯示 `目標遺失（LOST）`。提供切鏡轉換清單 `transitions` 與 `nextSwitchUs`。
   - **多畫面視圖（Multi-view）**：評估 `multi_view` 候選鏡頭，即時計算 `isActive`（目前追蹤鏡頭高亮）、`isPast`、`isFuture`。
   - **倍速支援（Speed）**：支援 1×、1.5×、2× 倍速設定與顯示。
   - **時間截斷**：`tUs` 嚴格限制在 `[0, as_of_us]`，絕不查詢或外洩未來影格。

3. **俯視圖模型與盲區曲線（Topdown & Blind Curve Integration）** (`frontend/workbench-v2/topdown-model.mjs`):
   - 整合 `topdown-model.mjs`：純函式解析 `blind.estimate`，將預測曲線轉為 `INFERRED` 低信心虛線，信心強制壓低為 `LOW` / `UNKNOWN`。
   - 盲區不可用時（`UNAVAILABLE`）維持 fail-closed，標註「預測不可用」且不繪製曲線。

4. **安全守門與資料完整性**：

body:
## 무엇을 바꾸나요

다계정 1단계 계획의 B3 첫 층(B3a)이에요. `authz.jsonl` 의 레코드를 하나의 상태로 모으는 `Authz_state` 를 만들어요.

- **`Authz_state`**: 레코드를 읽는 층마다 필드가 하나씩 있는 record 예요. 지금은 `mode` 필드 하나뿐이에요.
  `step` 은 모든 `Authz_record.Kind.t` 를 하나씩 따져요. 그래서 새 종류가 생기면 컴파일러가 `step` 에서 멈춰요.
  아직 아무 층도 읽지 않는 종류는 거절해요. masc 는 그런 레코드를 쓰지 않으니, 그게 들어 있으면 masc 가 쓴 로그가 아니에요.
  `Fresh_bootstrap` 앞에 온 레코드는 `Before_bootstrap` 으로 거절해요(설계 8.4). `step` 은 mode event 가 아닌 종류를 mode 와 짝지어 match 해요. 그래서 새 층이 자기 갈래를 만들 때 bootstrap 전에 그 레코드가 무슨 뜻인지 함께 적어야 해요.
- **`Authz_mode_state`**: mode event 의 순서를 따져요. 상태 3개 × 이벤트 3개, 9쌍을 모두 직접 적었어요(`_ ->` 없음).
  - 처음에는 `Fresh_bootstrap` 만 받아요.
  - 그다음 `Off` 와 `Reactivate` 를 번갈아 받아요. 둘 다 bootstrap 한 workspace 와 같아야 해요.
  - 나머지 6쌍은 `Out_of_order` 로, workspace 가 다르면 `Workspace_differs` 로 거절해요.
- **외부 저장소**: 저장소도 mode 변경을 같은 `Authz_mode_state.apply` 로 따져요. 예전 저장소는 bootstrap 뒤로 `Off`·`Reactivate` 를 순서·횟수 제한 없이 받았어요. 그래서 로그가 다시 읽을 때 거절할 이벤트도 저장소에는 Committed 로 남을 수 있었어요. 이제 두 파일이 같은 규칙 하나를 따라요. 거절은 `Mode_refused` 하나로 모았고, `Bootstrap_already_committed`·`Workspace_mismatch` 는 없어졌어요. `Authz_bootstrap` 을 부르는 곳이 아직 없어서, 지금 있는 저장소 파일은 없어요.
- **부팅 판정**: `Authz_boot_mode_read` 가 로그를 이 `step` 으로 읽어요. 그래서 따로 세던 레코드 개수와 "레코드는 있는데 mode event 가 없는 로그"를 다루던 별도 분기가 없어졌어요. 그런 로그는 이제 `Before_bootstrap` 으로 거절돼 `Log_unreadable` 이 돼요. 부팅이 멈추는 결과는 전과 같아요.
  `Authz_boot_mode.made_by` 는 `of_mode_state` 로 바뀌었어요.
- **계획 문서**: B3 을 네 층(B3a~B3d)으로 나눴어요. 11-05 에 정한 두 가지도 B3 범위에 적었어요. 첫 Admin 은 bootstrap 명령이 찍는 한 번 쓰는 초대 링크로 만들고, bootstrap 은 서버를 멈추고 BasePath lease 를 쥔 CLI 명령으로 돌려요.

설계: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-multi-account-oidc-runtime-authorization-design.md` 5.1, 8.4, 10.5

## 확인한 것

- `dune build --root . ./test/test_authz_external_store.exe ./test/test_authz_state.exe ./test/test_authz_boot_mode_read.exe ./test/test_authz_boot_mode.exe ./test/test_authz_bootstrap.exe ./test/test_authz_high_water.exe ./bin/main_eio.exe`
- `test_authz_state` 는 9쌍 표 전체, workspace 가 다른 경우, 읽지 않는 종류 10개를 bootstrap 앞과 뒤에서 각각 확인해요. 실제 `Authz_bootstrap.fresh_bootstrap` 이 쓴 로그를 다시 읽으면 그 workspace 의 `Multi_account` 가 되는지도 봐요.
- 시험 결과: external_store 21개, state 8개, boot_mode_read 24개, boot_mode 10개, bootstrap 67개, high_water 33개 모두 통과
- bootstrap 뒤에 사슬이 맞는 `Local_recovery` 레코드를 붙이면, 부팅이 2번 줄에서 그 종류 때문에 로그를 읽지 못함으로 거절하는지도 봐요.
- 변이를 넣어 시험이 실패하는 것도 확인했어요.
  - bootstrap 뒤의 읽지 않는 종류를 통과시키기
  - `Off` 뒤에 `Off` 허용
  - 저장소가 순서 거절을 무시하기(4개 실패)
  - bootstrap 앞 레코드를 `Kind_not_read` 로 거절하기

## 이 PR 에서 하지 않은 것

- append 전에 `step` 을 돌리는 일은 코드로 강제하지 않아요. 지금 로그에 쓰는 곳은 `Authz_bootstrap` 하나이고, 빈 로그에 `Fresh_bootstrap` 하나만 써요. 다음 층(B3b 쓰기 구역)에서 남은 intent 판정, append 전 `step`, 새 상태 발행을 한 구역으로 묶고, bootstrap 도 그 구역을 쓰게 바꿀게요.
- Admin 지정, workspace 멤버십, 초대, 외부 계정 연결은 그다음 층(B3c)에서 각자 `Authz_state` 필드로 들어와요.
