author: robtand
body:
## Summary

Add TL3's first Stateright model as a dev-dependency and integration test of the existing controller crate. S3 checks the delivery contracts under lost responses and duplicate deliveries, with real controller, comment-reconciliation, and epoch-fence conformance replays. Closes #747. Part of #730.

```text
controller -> durable outbox -> network -> upstream record and visible state
                  ^                         |
                  +---- reconcile by key ---+
```

Rob amended #747 during implementation to follow the state table. The model allows temporary duplicate messages and checks their subsequent deduplication. It does not replace that contract with an atomic applied-bit assumption for comments.

| Property | Binding table row |
| --- | --- |
| Once: at most one mutation per key, eventually exactly one for an eligible key under healthy fair delivery | [Submit a PrismaBuild job](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L740), [approval check](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L742), [agent run](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L748) |
| Converges: repeated delivery reaches the target and preserves it | [Withdraw](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L741), [branch, PR, queue, close, and worktree rows](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L743-L747) |
| Message: at least once, a temporary second copy is reachable, the next reconciliation retains exactly one marked copy and never deletes the last copy | [Comment or message to Rob](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L749) |
| Epoch fence: an application older than the current upstream fence makes no mutation | [Epoch paragraph](https://github.com/RobTand/trustladderiii/blob/e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f/docs/state-table.md#L753) |

The model exhausts one or two keys, two total network losses, one duplicate, and two epoch values. It checks all three single-contract cases and all nine ordered pairs, with both shared and different epochs. There is no depth or state-count cutoff. Reachability properties cover two losses, duplication, authoritative absence and retry, stale rejection, successful completion, and the two-copy message state.

Liveness assumes healthy upstreams and fair dispatch and reconciliation. Pending reads and scheduling stutters are collapsed. In-flight requests end before an authoritative absence decision. Message convergence assumes the next reconciliation call, including after a successful response. The model checks that operation's contract; it does not claim that network health schedules a controller look. Keys refer to distinct resources or markers. Epoch cancellation can legitimately prevent an obsolete key from being applied. These assumptions and Stateright's acyclic-path liveness restriction are documented in `docs/stateright-s3.md`.

### Transition mapping

Production references are at the inspected base `e3292d911a6e42c89f1f197b90648419a39a6b3f`; production files are unchanged.

| Model transition | Real code path |
| --- | --- |
| `CommitSent`, `Dispatch` | `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1190`, durable Sent before `execute` |
| `LoseResponse`, `MarkUncertain` | `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1255` and `:1271`, transport errors preserve Sent, then Uncertain |
| `ReadRecord` | `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1298`, reconcile Found, Absent, or Pending under the original key |
| `RetrySameKey` | `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1323`, authoritative absence returns that effect to Intended |
| `CommitConfirmed` | `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1555`, acknowledgement, delivery transition, and observations committed together |
| `Deliver`, Once | `crates/controller/src/adapters/record.rs:33`, per-key records; `crates/controller/src/adapters/github/publishing.rs:297`, approval external-id reconciliation; `crates/prismabuild/src/submit.rs`, action-key submissions |
| `Deliver`, Converges | `crates/controller/src/adapters/github/publishing.rs:297`, PR-state reconciliation; `crates/controller/src/adapters/mergify.rs`, queue-state reconciliation |
| `DuplicateDelivery`, Message | `crates/github/src/client.rs:677`, marker read followed by POST; `crates/controller/tests/crash/upstreams.rs:246`, two visible copies saved before a lost response |
| `ReadRecord`, `ReconcileCopies` | `crates/github/src/client.rs:697`, oldest app-owned marked comment retained, extras deleted |
| `AdvanceFence`, `CancelStale`, rejected `Deliver` | `crates/controller/src/adapters/record.rs:42`, monotonic fence before writes; `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1148`, stale-effect cancellation |
| `LoseRequest` | Failed attempt with no upstream write; only the subsequent Absent branch at `crates/controller/src/lib.rs:1318` authorizes retry |

## Evidence

All four tests executed, with zero skips or filtered tests, in the final-head [green BuildBuddy run](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/fa3ccf00-317a-46db-a90e-adf8abaa7a3c). Its [test invocation](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/8a156471-0a85-4a48-86ea-d0a3c63971e2) reports SUCCESS and exit 0 for `//crates/controller:test_test_stateright_s3`. Read both red and green test.log files with `bb_logs.py`.

### Red, then green

The seeded bug in red commit `888ea635ad000d1abaf233e8677f1ad97d77f104` writes again on the retry path instead of consulting the existing upstream record. Green removes that mutant branch.

| Test | Red evidence | Green evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idempotent_effect_under_lost_response` | [Red](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/b7a11529-de7d-48e7-8f5f-c1cb8de1a673): Stateright reports `once effects mutate at most once per key`, counterexample ending with `mutations: 2` | [Green](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/fa3ccf00-317a-46db-a90e-adf8abaa7a3c): 12 configurations exhausted |
| `lost_response_keeps_the_key_real_trace_conforms` | Same red run: `real upstream record differs from S3`, actual 1, mutant 2 | Same green run: real controller and Postgres trace conforms at every drive, Pending leaves snapshot unchanged, original key confirmed with one execute |
| Real message and fence traces | Same red run: both pass, unaffected by the retry mutant | Same green run: both pass |

Stateright's reported counterexample, including its final acknowledgement and fence step:

```text
CommitSent(0) -> Dispatch(0) -> LoseRequest(0) -> MarkUncertain(0)
-> ReadRecord(0) -> RetrySameKey(0) -> CommitSent(0) -> Dispatch(0)
-> DuplicateDelivery(0) -> Deliver(0) -> LoseRequest(0)
-> MarkUncertain(0) -> ReadRecord(0) -> CommitConfirmed(0) -> AdvanceFence
mutations = 2 for the same key
```

The conformance test separately replays the actual lost-response path: upstream application, transport error, Sent, Uncertain, Pending with no snapshot change, and Found without another execute.

### Proof bounds and cost

| Harness | Properties | Bound | Unique states | Time | Memory | Mutant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S3, `idempotent_effect_under_lost_response` | Once, convergence, message retention and deduplication, epoch fence, eventual settlement, reachability | 1–2 keys, 2 losses, 1 duplicate, 2 epochs; 12 contract configurations with 21 initial states | 42,900 across all runs; largest run 5,533 | 0.291 s model test | Whole test action peak 190,418,944 bytes, including Postgres conformance | [Counterexample](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/b7a11529-de7d-48e7-8f5f-c1cb8de1a673) |

The target is new, so its prior Gate cost was absent. It adds 1.305 s of test-binary wall time; the uncached BuildBuddy TestRunner action took 1.817 s, below 60 s per shard. The execution receipt verified reque

body:
Fixes [OGC-1600](https://uwdigi.atlassian.net/browse/OGC-1600).

## What
A geographic levels file (`*-levels.csv`) with a column the import does not use now lists that column in the preview: "These columns are not imported and were ignored: colour". Organization files already did this.

## Why
The ticket reports an unknown column being ignored without a word. For organization files this was fixed by #4515 and works on develop: the preview names the column and the import goes ahead. A levels file still passed an empty list, so its extra columns disappeared silently.

## How
`LocationsImportServiceImpl.previewLevels` collects every non-empty header other than `level` and `typeName` and returns it in the plan's `ignoredColumns`. The page already shows that list. Values files are unchanged: every header in a values file is a level name, so none can be ignored.

## Tests
- `LocationsImportRestControllerTest.anUnknownColumnInALevelsFile_isListedAsIgnored` fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Live on the dev stack (Admin > Locations > Import / Export, Preview):
  - a levels file with `colour` gives `ignoredColumns: ["colour"]` and the warning;

Step 3 of the cephx aes → aes256k migration (CVE-2025-30156).

Proxmox staged a new aes256k `client.admin` key with `pve-cephx-rotate-service-keys --rotate-admin-key`. Until the rotation is committed (`--confirm-all-clients-refreshed`), **both the old and the new key authenticate**, so this rollout is safe at any point before that.

- Added one spec in tests/e2e and only the four displayed PNGs in docs/ui-review/2026-11-04. No new top-level directories, temporary files, dependencies or unrelated restructuring; no existing code made dead.

author: oisinkyne
body:
# feat(dvpod): hand-off flow for the Obol monitoring token, and a public-safe nickname

In the Obol Stack, the agent now gets the central-monitoring token to the dv-pod without the token ever entering the
chat, the agent's context, a Helm value or a command line:
1. The agent creates an empty `0600` file `~/.config/obol/obol-monitoring-credential`.
2. The user pastes the token into it and saves.
3. The agent checks the file's size and line count only.
4. The agent loads it with `kubectl create secret --from-file` and sets `centralMonitoring.existingSecret` (dv-pod 0.22.1+).
5. It checks the Secret is present by name only, checks Prometheus logs for 401/403, and offers to delete the file.

It also proposes a nickname from context, which the user confirms. For an organisation or enterprise deployment it uses the organisation's own name (e.g. `DV Labs`). For private use it picks a pseudonym (stack id + network), never a hostname, real name or wallet address.

- `dvpod/SKILL.md`: a hard rule that credentials go into a file, then a Kubernetes Secret, then `existingSecret`. Never values, `--set` or the chat.

- `dvpod/obol-stack.md`: new section "Nickname and Obol monitoring".
- `dvpod/examples.md`, `values-reference.md`: `existingSecret` replaces `centralMonitoring.token`, and the docs say why.

Plugin 1.9.0 → 1.10.0. Depends on helm-charts dv-pod 0.22.1.

author: leshwar
body:
## What

You no longer have to type coordinates for weather and sunrise/sunset. **Settings → Location and presence** now has a **Use my location** button. It fills in latitude, longitude and the place name, shows what it found, and waits for you to check it and tap **Save location**. It never saves on its own.

- **Device location first.** When the page can ask for it (`window.isSecureContext && navigator.geolocation`, so HTTPS or localhost), the browser shows its own permission prompt. The coordinates are rounded to 2 decimals in the browser, then the server turns them into a place name with BigDataCloud's free `reverse-geocode-client`.
- **Fallback: approximate, from the internet address.** This covers plain HTTP (e.g. `http://<tailscale-name>:8080` from a phone), and also a denied or failed device lookup. The new `POST /api/v1/location/lookup` asks ipapi.co, then ipwho.is as a backup, through `net.http`. Both are free and need no key. Because the server makes the request, it finds the home's location, not the phone's.
- **What the user sees:** for example "Found Seattle, WA (approximate, from your internet address). Check it and tap Save location."
  - Text under the button says, before anything is sent, which services are asked and what they get.
  - When the services are offline or rate-limited, a plain message says to try again or type the location; typing still works.
- **Privacy:** nothing is sent to these services unless the button is tapped. Coordinates are rounded to about 1 km before being sent or saved. The README privacy notes and `docs/API.md` are updated.

The endpoint returns a neutral `{latitude, longitude, place_name, source: "device"|"approximate"}`. Service names appear only in `app/core/geolocate.py`, and the UI copy names them so users know where requests go.

The browser part lives in its own `web/js/locate.js` (`findLocation()`, `describeFound()`). The Home weather card's **Turn on weather** (from #17) now opens Settings → Location with weather already ticked and a hint to tap **Use my location**.

## Tests

- **Unit, `tests/unit/test_geolocate.py`:** run against faked services. Covers:
  - parsing each service's answer
  - place labels ("Seattle, WA" in the US, "Lyon, France" elsewhere)
  - rounding before sending
  - the fallback order (on HTTP 429, a rate-limit answer, a timeout, or missing coordinates)
  - plain "busy" and "offline" errors
- **Integration, `test_api.py`:** the endpoint against the demo server with a local stub (`tests/helpers.FakeJsonServer`):
  - device coordinates get a place name, and only rounded coordinates are sent
  - a rate-limited first service falls back to the backup
  - nothing is saved, bad coordinates return 400, and offline returns a plain 400
- **Integration, `test_ui.py` (Playwright):**
  - clicks the button with geolocation mocked: fields are filled, the "from this device" message shows, nothing is saved until Save
  - with location blocked: falls back to approximate
  - with the services down: shows the error message, and typing still works
  - Home → **Turn on weather** → **Use my location** → **Save location** saves the location and turns weather on

`make lint && make test && make check-tests` pass locally (215 tests, after merging the latest `main`).

I checked the screens at portrait 720×1280, landscape 1280×720 and phone width 390×844. I didn't call the real ipapi.co, ipwho.is or BigDataCloud from here. The parsers follow each service's documented response format, and the tests use stubs.

body:
## Summary

Open recall (⌘O) in the menu bar app now opens one window with two views, Memory and This Mac. It reads everything through `recall api` (#66), starts the API when it isn't running, and updates from its event stream, with no polling.

```text
apps/menubar/Sources/
├── main.swift      # menu bar, ⌘O, dev flags wired in
├── Panel.swift     # menu bar panel (diffs now in ~/.agents/recall/cache/diffs)
├── API.swift       # unix-socket client + SSE, starts `recall api` on demand
├── Window.swift    # one window: titlebar, sidebar, kept-alive sections
├── Library.swift   # shared state, app.json (the app's only file)
├── Memory.swift    # notes list, category tags, filters, reader
├── Lists.swift     # Chats (pinned find), Projects, Now
├── Markdown.swift  # chat messages as markdown, parsed once and cached
├── Palette.swift   # ⌘K: notes, chats, go to, actions
├── Picker.swift    # themed menus, project picker with filter and pins
├── ThisMac.swift   # counts, sources, last run, storage, model, rules, access
├── Design.swift    # Paper Mono, ink-on-paper tokens, category hues, 3 pt scrollers
└── Dev.swift       # off-screen probes: --shot, --measure, --scroll-chat, ...
```

- The window writes only `~/.agents/recall/app.json` (size, sidebar width, last section, pins, `"ui": "menu"`). No UserDefaults, Caches or window restoration.
- Read-only: editing and forgetting notes come later.
- Bundle id becomes `com.rererecall.app`, and the app gets its own icon, drawn by the app and packed with `iconutil` at build time.
- Every dev flag runs off screen and never takes focus.

## Evidence

Measured on this laptop. Screenshots stay out of the PR because they show a real index.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Section switch, click to first frame | up to 370 ms (rebuilt each visit) | 7 to 30 ms, every section |
| Mouse wheel in a chat | 1 pt per click | 24 pt per click (trackpad unchanged) |
| ⌘O to notes drawn | n/a | 430 to 490 ms, about 250 ms of it the API |
| Idle CPU, 10 min, window open | n/a | 0.05% |
| Footprint: never opened / open / closed | 36 MB (old build) | 31 / 153 to 163 / 53 MB |
| .app size | 0.8 MB | 4.2 MB (189 KB icon) |
| Longest chat (388 messages), wheel speed, mean / p95 frame | 5.3 / 14.9 ms plain | 5.6 / 16.8 ms with markdown |

- Find in chat: 5,914 matches across 388 messages in 29 ms, marked on the rendered text.
- Keeping sections alive costs about 90 MB while the window is open (65 MB without), all freed on close.
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and `tools/changelog.py --check` pass. No unit tests, per the repo.
- Not checked yet: how scrolling, the palette and menus feel on screen with a real mouse and trackpad.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Nothing is migrated or deleted. The old `~/Library/Caches/recall` and the old `defaults` key are left in place, and `/v1/storage` lists them as leftovers.

**Blast Radius:** small

`apps/menubar` is built from source and isn't in the wheel, so PyPI users see no change. Anyone who built the menu bar before gets a new bundle id, so macOS treats the next build as a new app.

## BUTTON-VISUAL / UI-ACT · общие контурные кнопки Nebula

### Доказанная причина
В рабочем `NebulaAction` тихие/опасные контурные кнопки используют обычный divider token `border=#445574` поверх `surfaceElevated=#1D2E51`, контраст **1.79:1**. На 320dp снимках это выглядит как голая цветная надпись, несмотря на CSS `borderWidth:1`. Утверждённый [PersAI_UI_plan.md#button-visual](https://github.com/panasenkof/PersonalAI/blob/main/Plans/PersAI_UI_plan.md) требует отдельного `actionOutline` (dark #7186A8, light #62718B).

### Исправлено
- Только в канонической паре цветов `nebulaPalette.dark/light` добавлен семантический `actionOutline`; passive `border` оставлен для деления панелей.
- `NebulaAction` quiet/danger получает новый заметный контур. Filled primary / danger-solid сохраняют 0-border, а фон и текст не меняются.
- Jest проверяет dark outline/surfaceElevated ≥3:1, light ≥3:1, высоту ≥48dp и реальное применение токена.
- Dark **3.64:1**, light **4.34:1** (WCAG relative luminance), вместо 1.79:1 dark и 2.70:1 light.

### Качество и конформность
C0-A → C3-B: **presentation-only, NO CHANGE NEEDED**: один источник токенов, одна кнопка, без новых файлов хранения, сетевых/LLM writers, навигационных маршрутов, SQLCipher и permission hooks.
PLAN §2 / №89 + UI-ACT BUTTON-VISUAL: **MATCH по токенам и компоненту**, визуальные before/after **NOT VERIFIED** до фактического browser artifact; Android U5/крупный шрифт/TalkBack **NOT RUN**.
Требуются exact-SHA CI, проверка снимков 320/360/390/430 и темы, затем объединение в целевой `#349 → main`.

Stacked **#351 → #350 → #349**: без самостоятельного слияния в main до единого интеграционного гейта.

author: etienne-m
body:
## Problem

A period after a title, rank or saint abbreviation is treated as a sentence boundary in several languages, so the abbreviation ends up alone:

```
$ echo "Je vous passe M. Dupont. Un instant." | sentencex -l fr
* Je vous passe M.
* Dupont.
* Un instant.
```

French is the most affected: `fr.txt` has no entry for `m`, `mme`, `mlle`, `dr`, `st`, `cpt`, `bd`, … (`MM.` happens to work). This matters for consumers that stream text to a TTS engine one sentence at a time (that is how I hit it, through pipecat 1.12): `M.` is sent on its own, spoken as the letter "M", and followed by the pause and falling intonation of a finished sentence. A few other languages have smaller gaps.

Checked on master (`bc75409`, 1.0.33).

## Change

Add the abbreviations that always introduce a name or a place, and that are not common words that could end a sentence:

| lang | added |
|---|---|
| fr | `m mme mmes mlle mlles dr dre pr mgr cdt gén lt cpt sgt pdt st ste bd fg` |
| de | `hrn frl dipl kapt pfr` |
| es | `sras profa dña cnel pdte mons` |
| it | `gent` |
| pt | `srta profa exma ilmo ilma sta av` |

Plus a few cases per language in `tests/<lang>.txt`. The new fixtures fail on master (5 language tests) and pass with this change; `cargo test` is green.

## Left out on purpose

Entries are looked up lowercase, so I skipped words that can legitimately end a sentence and would lose real boundaries: French `col`, `prof`, `me`, `cie`; German `dir` (the pronoun), `abt` (also "abbot"); Portuguese `cel`, `dom`. A `tests/fr.txt` case pins that `Il a franchi le col.` still ends a sentence, and a `tests/de.txt` case does the same for `dir.`.

## Trade-off worth a look

`m` makes French `M.` (Monsieur) work, but because the lookup is lowercase it also keeps `10 m. Il est haut.` as one sentence. I think that is acceptable: the existing English marker file already notes that SI unit symbols are not supposed to take a period, while `M.` is the standard abbreviation of Monsieur. Happy to drop `m` if you prefer the other side of that trade-off.

## Not included

English `Ms.` is still split (`Please speak to Ms. Smith.`), apparently because the case-insensitive `MS` degree marker in `trailing_markers/en.txt` takes precedence over the `ms` abbreviation entry. That looks like a separate fix, so I left it alone.

author: tkhow09
body:
Smooths the first switch to night, makes sound effects recover after a phone suspends audio, and always shows the "click to enter" screen. Nothing visible in the 3D scene changes.

## Stall on the first switch to night (phones and desktop)
`renderer.compile()` only starts a shader. The graphics driver finishes it the first time something is drawn with it.

The fireflies' night shader was never drawn during loading, for two reasons:
- the animation loop, already running during loading, re-hides the fireflies by day;
- they only look their shader up again when something forces them to, so changing the lights didn't make them switch.

So the first switch to night stalled while that shader was finished: several seconds in the emulator, at least a visible hitch on a phone.

**Fix:** after compiling, loading draws a hidden frame in each lighting state, with every night-only object shown. Before each frame every material is told to look its shader up again (`needsUpdate`). That picks the one already built and rebuilds nothing.

**Result:** in the emulator, the switch to night now finishes 0 shaders (it was 1, taking 3–7 s there), and the profile is idle through the transition.

## Sound effects stopping (phones)
Phones can suspend a page's audio (after a notification, switching apps, a long pause). Also, a sound whose silent first start ("priming") was refused stayed blocked until entering the cab re-primed it.

**Fix:**
- every tap now resumes the audio if it's suspended and re-primes any sound that needs it;
- the page also resumes audio when it becomes visible again;
- a sound refused later is marked for re-priming on the next tap;
- the cats' tap sounds are excluded from priming, because priming them during the tap would mute that tap's sound.

## Always show "click to enter"

author: krijos
body:
Fixes #10106
Fixes #9278

## Problem and resulting behavior

Moon Arrow, Starfire Shot, Huntress Shot, Trueshot and Starfire Barrage reached 30 yards and Auto Shot 35, while Lunar Lance and Starcall already reached 45 (#10106, #9278).

Two hidden passives exist in the client's `Spell.dbc` for exactly this and were granted nowhere:

| Spell | Effect | Mask | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 573711 `Starcaller Auto Shot Range` | `SPELL_AURA_ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER` (107), `EffectMiscValue` 5 = `SPELLMOD_RANGE`, `EffectBasePoints` 9 + `DieSides` 1 = **+10** | family 9, word0 `0x1` | Auto Shot `RangeIndex` 114 (35 yd) becomes 45. Its description reads "Matches auto shot range to their abilities." |
| 805527 `Starcaller Range Passive` | same modifier on effect 1, `EffectBasePoints` 14 + `DieSides` 1 = **+15** | family 32, (`0x2c00`, `0x80204`, `0x200`) | Moon Arrow, Starfire Shot, Trueshot, Huntress Shot and Starfire Barrage, every rank, `RangeIndex` 113 (30 yd) becomes 45 |

`AscensionCompatData::ClassSpells` is only taught when `CoA.AutoProgression` is set, so both are granted in `OnPlayerLogin` instead. Because they are player auras, Auto Shot keeps its authored 35 for every other class, and the modifier reaches the client through `SMSG_SET_FLAT_SPELL_MODIFIER`, which `CharacterHandler` re-sends on login. Native consumers are `SpellInfo::GetMaxRange` and `Spell::CheckRange`, both of which call `Player::ApplySpellMod(SPELLMOD_RANGE)`.

Arrow of the Goddess is included because it is the same request: it is a self-cast frontal cone whose reach comes from `EffectRadiusIndex` 23 (40 yd), not `RangeIndex`, so no range modifier can move it. Cone target selection is server side, so the radius becomes index 232 (45 yd) in `ApplyContracts`.

Starcall needed no change: all five ranks already carry `RangeIndex` 36 (45 yd). It did not appear in the original survey because its `DmgClass` is 1, not ranged.

## Validation and remaining limits

`starcaller-ranged-abilities-45-yards` fails on `main` and passes here, with a Hunter control proving Auto Shot stays at 35 for other classes, and both the rank 1 and top rank of Moon Arrow and Starfire Shot asserted since the mask covers every rank. Built and run on its own as well as merged with the other Starcaller fixes, and confirmed in play.

Remaining limits:

- #9278 asks for 5–45. `SpellRange` 113 carries `RangeMin` 0, so the result is 0–45: the maximum matches, and there is no 5 yard dead zone, which is more permissive than requested rather than less.
- Arrow of the Goddess' cone has **no scenario**. There is no radius metric in the harness, so covering it needs a behavioural case with creatures placed inside and outside 45 yards.
- 805527's mask also selects three zero-range passives (Full Moon Hidden, Lunar Phase, Lunar Phase Gen) which have no range to extend; not asserted.
- Across all 115 Starcaller scenarios this branch leaves the same five failures `main` already has, none of them touched here.

## Data/source dependencies

No SQL: applied SQL is unchanged, and nothing is added under `data/sql`. No DBC row is added or overridden and no `*_dbc` world table is written — both passives already exist in the client's own `Spell.dbc`, which is why the range is carried by a spell modifier the client is told about rather than by an edited range index. The Arrow of the Goddess radius is swapped at runtime in `ApplyContracts` and is server side only. No credentials, profiles or game archives are included.

---

Opened from a fork, so labels cannot be set here. Suggested: `Bug`, `Starcaller`, `Script`, `CPP Edit`, `Class Fix`, `Tested`.

author: bardic-inspiration
body:
## What and why

A dev PR that changes content failed `validate` on its first run, every time. The `lane` job read labels from the `opened` event payload, before the labeler added `migration`. The labeler writes with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so its `labeled` event starts no new run, and the re-run §12.4 promised never happened. #182, #183, and `dev/spell-header-forms` all needed `migration` removed and re-added by hand.

Now, when a dev PR changes content and its payload has no `migration`, the `lane` job reads the PR's current labels from the API every 5 seconds for up to a minute. It passes once the labeler's label appears.

- `scripts/lane/index.ts`: `needsMigrationLabel` (the same condition `checkLane` enforces, now shared) and `waitForLabel` (reads until the label appears or attempts run out, and returns the last labels).
- `scripts/lane/cli.ts`: waits only when the rule would fail and a token, repo, and PR number are set, then applies the lane rules to the live labels. A failed API read fails the job with its status rather than passing silently.
- `validate.yml`: grants `pull-requests: read` and passes `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `PR_NUMBER` to the lane step. The header comment describes the new behavior.
- §12.4: the "re-runs when labels change" bullet now describes the wait. Label events from people still re-run, so removing `migration` by hand still fails the PR.

The rule itself is unchanged: a dev PR that changes content still needs `migration`. Only the timing of the check changes.

Closes #184

## Testing

- `tests/lane.test.ts` (written first, failing before the change): `needsMigrationLabel` for dev and content branches, with and without content and the label; `waitForLabel` returns as soon as the label appears, gives up after its attempts with the last labels, and pauses between reads.
- `node scripts/lane/cli.ts` run locally against #183's head with no labels and a bad token: it announces the wait, then fails with "Reading the PR's labels failed: 401 Unauthorized". Without a token it applies the rules to the payload labels as before.
- `npm run validate`, `build`, `check`, `test` (714 passed), and `a11y` pass.
- This PR changes no content, so it doesn't exercise the wait itself. The next dev PR with content (or #183 after a merge from `main`) will.

author: yundi339
body:
修复网络丢包时键盘按键释放后主机端持续重复输入

## Problem

If a key-down is accepted by the client but the key-up is still queued when the control connection fails, the host can keep the key pressed and continue keyboard repeat. The client then needs to remember that the host may still hold the key even after the local physical key state is cleared.

## What changed

- Track successfully forwarded key-down events in a connection-level ledger separate from locally held keys.
- Keep ordinary focus, ungrab, fullscreen, and clipboard cleanup limited to locally held keys, so stale forwarded entries do not generate repeated releases during normal UI actions.
- Include the forwarded-key ledger only at connection boundaries:
  - before reconnect, release both state sets while retaining the ledger for retry;
  - after reconnect, release local state while retaining forwarded entries because the send API only confirms local queueing;
  - during final session teardown, release and clear both sets.
- Deduplicate overlapping local and forwarded keys.
- Retain entries when a release attempt fails.
- Add regression coverage for ordinary cleanup, overlapping keys, successful connection cleanup, and failed releases.

The common-c protocol and Sunshine code are unchanged. Keyboard packets remain reliable; this change closes the client-side state gap around queued releases and connection transitions.

## Validation

- `scripts\\run-test.bat keyboard_state keyboard_state`
- clang-format 21.1.8 diff check
- Windows x64 Release build with `.codex/skills/moonlight-qt-build-windows/scripts/build-local.ps1 -NoDependencySetup`
- MSI and portable package generation

Real network fault-injection with Moonlight and Sunshine is still required to validate the original reproduction end to end.

## Summary

Proposes the M7 (Go parity) written design and decision boundary, per the established milestone workflow.

body:
Reported upstream from AB (its #308 worked around it in the app). Without `handleDrops`, BulkDrop accepted the drag (preventDefault on dragenter/dragover) but its `drop()` only prevented the default when `handleDrops` was set. So a host that owned drops and didn't handle one let the browser open the dropped file and leave the page.

`drop()` now calls preventDefault for any file drop. Propagation is unchanged (only `handleDrops` stops it), so a host's own ancestor drop handler still receives the event.

Test: pending-work.test.mjs checks that preventDefault runs before and regardless of handleDrops, and that only handleDrops stops propagation. It fails with the line removed. Not covered: no browser test drops a real file. A page-wide guard while a dropzone is mounted (AB's ref-counted one) is not in this PR; it can follow if other hosts need it. Re-pins core.

author: incegozmuratcan
body: Vercel Cron now starts the combined BTC+ETH ETF daily X post every 30 minutes through the Istanbul fill window. The GitHub Actions `schedule` is removed so the two timers cannot double-fire. ## What changed - `vercel.json` calls `GET /api/cron/x-btc-eth-etf-daily` on Tuesday–Saturday: - `*/30 5-10 * * 2-6` — 05:00–10:30 UTC (08:00–13:30 Europe/Istanbul) - `0 11 * * 2-6` — 11:00 UTC (14:00 Istanbul), last live dispatch - `45 11 * * 2-6` — 11:45 UTC (14:45 Istanbul), check only, no dispatch - The route requires `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, then calls GitHub `workflow_dispatch` for `x-btc-eth-etf-daily.yml` on `main` with `dry_run` set to the string `false`. - If a run is already queued or in progress (started within the last 45 minutes), the route returns `reason: "already_running"` and does not dispatch again. The workflow concurrency group remains the backstop. - A manual `workflow_dispatch` still defaults `dry_run` to true. - Farside completeness and same-day skip behavior are unchanged. An incomplete table still exits success without posting. - At 14:45 Istanbul the route reads the newest `btc-eth-etf-daily` artifact from the window and logs an error when there is no live post (incomplete Farside, failed run, or no run). It does not send Slack or email. Istanbul is UTC+3 with no daylight saving. The half-hour window is 13 live passes, from 08:00 through 14:00 local time. ## Plan limit This needs **Vercel Pro or Enterprise**. Hobby allows 100 cron jobs, but each expression may run only once per day and only sometime inside that hour. `*/30 5-10 * * 2-6` runs twelve times on a Tuesday–Saturday, so a Hobby deploy fails with `Hobby accounts are limited to daily cron jobs`. Splitting the window into daily expressions would pass that check and still miss the minute. Cron runs on the production deployment only. ## After merge Set these on the Vercel project for **Production** (not Preview for the GitHub token): | Variable | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `CRON_SECRET` | Bearer Vercel Cron sends automatically. At least 16 random characters. The route does not accept `ONCHAIN_REFRESH_SECRET` in its place. | | `GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN` | Fine-grained PAT or GitHub App installation token with **Actions: Read and write** on this repo. A classic PAT needs the `repo` scope. | Leave the GitHub repository variable `X_DRY_RUN` as it is. Cron does not read it. The existing Actions secrets (`ONCHAIN_PUBLISH_SECRET` and the four OAuth 1.0a secrets) still have to be set for the live post itself. Confirm the project is Pro before deploying. A Hobby production deploy will fail on the half-hour expression. Details: `docs/x-automation.md`.

## Repository-wide reliability and security audit

This follows the repository analysis of the 0.5.0 candidate in main. The SonarQube API reported 1,044 open reliability findings and 47 open security findings before this change.

- Reject symlinked Control Center source and output paths before applying the Settings overlay. The patch now runs from the pinned upstream source directory.
- Compile and run the Storage QA binary in a private temporary directory and keep VM checks effective under optimized Python.
- Verify the discovered LocalSend certificate before accepting a self-signed HTTPS peer. Lock development dependencies for Phone Link and parse malformed Bluetooth messages without retrying an unbounded regex search.
- Handle rejected promises in desktop extensions and guard empty window groups in Tiling Assistant.
- Use explicit numeric parsers, sorting and Bash conditionals. Remove 16 duration declarations ignored by GNOME Shell because they lacked units.

The audit found a large number of Web CSS rules applied to valid GNOME St selectors, properties and functions. The project still analyzes those files. The LocalSend multicast address is a protocol constant and the authenticator.json entry in the extension prototype index is a file checksum. These findings should be classified individually after review.

## Verification

- 343 repository tests and 96 Phone Link tests passed locally.
- The native Settings regression and isolated two-monitor GNOME 51 session passed. The latter checked secondary menus and the dock's first appearance.
- The Control Center overlay applied to the real pinned upstream source and rejected a linked target before writing. The LocalSend TLS callback accepted the exact discovered fingerprint and rejected a different one.
- The Phone Link lock verified with uv lock --check.

## Follow-up validation

- The previous 0.5.0 migration job rejected the candidate because the bootstrap script only accepted 0.3.x and 0.4.x. The bridge now accepts supported stable versions from 0.3.0 onward, including 0.5.0, and rejects a remotely supplied managed kernel without a signed manifest. The new cases passed in the full 345-test suite.
- Shared color conversion and texture properties resolved the shader duplication report. The property accessors were exercised through GObject, and the revised desktop harness again passed with two monitors.
- SonarQube Cloud passed the new-code gate with zero open new issues at commit 4e9dffe. The migration, installation and ISO jobs for this head still need to complete.

author: maj0rpain
body:
Closes #588

## Summary

`musicbot/library.py` now owns the local-library URI format in both directions. It already built URIs (`song_uri`). Now it also decodes them (`track_path_from_uri`) and exports the `FILE_SCHEME` constant. The loader keeps only the `SongError` mapping and the `MUSIC_LIBRARY_PATH` gate. `linkutils` imports the scheme instead of keeping its own copy.

```
musicbot/library.py
  FILE_SCHEME = "file://"                 + (replaces LAYOUT_DEPTH)
  song_uri(artist, album, filename)         (unchanged: encode)
  track_path_from_uri(uri) -> Path|None   + (decode, moved from loader)
musicbot/loader.py
  _library_track_path                     - removed
  _load_song  LOCAL_LIBRARY branch        ~ calls library.track_path_from_uri
musicbot/linkutils.py
  _FILE_SCHEME                            - removed, imports library.FILE_SCHEME
```

The depth check no longer reads `LAYOUT_DEPTH`. It unpacks the relative path into exactly the three parts `song_path` takes, then checks that `song_path` rebuilds the same path:

```diff
-        or len(path.relative_to(root).parts) != library.LAYOUT_DEPTH
+    try:
+        artist, album, filename = path.relative_to(root).parts
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+    if song_path(artist, album, filename) != path or not path.is_file():
+        return None
```

The function returns `None` on refusal, and the loader turns that into `LIBRARY_FILE_MISSING`:

```diff
-        path = _library_track_path(track)
+        path = (
+            library.track_path_from_uri(track)
+            if config.MUSIC_LIBRARY_PATH
+            else None
+        )
+        if path is None:
+            raise SongError(config.LIBRARY_FILE_MISSING)
```

## Evidence

Existing tests in `tests/test_loader_local_library.py` cover the moved decode. They now share a `_loads` helper. Two tests were replaced:

- given the library is disabled, when a lower-case `file://` URI is loaded, then `SongError(SONGINFO_UNSUPPORTED)` is raised (replaces the upper-case variant, so the `ENABLE_LOCAL_LIBRARY` gate keeps its `_load_song` coverage);
- given `song_uri("A", "B", "t.mp3")`, when it is checked against `library.FILE_SCHEME`, then the URI starts with it (one owner for the scheme, used by encode and decode).

All the other existing refusals and loads still pass unchanged: wrong depth, `.`/`..` segments, foreign authority, raw `?`/`#` in filenames, symlinked album, artist and root, `localhost` authority, upper-case scheme.

`uv run --group dev pytest` pass

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way
**Blast Radius:** Local-library playback (`file://` URIs) only. A regression would refuse or wrongly accept a library track. The checks were moved, not changed, apart from the depth check now going through `song_path`.

author: lautioliver
body:
Dos detectores de `lib/deviations.py` (los usan `bk monitor` y `bk learn`) daban falsos positivos que terminaron como lecciones propuestas (la persona las retiró el 2026-11-04):

- **Otra credencial**: leía `GH_CONFIG_DIR` dentro del código que un agente estaba editando (`python3 - <<'EOF' … EOF`, `printf '…'`).
- **Decisión atribuida**: tomaba frases de reviews y resúmenes ("you approved the wording", "como decidiste") aunque la persona sí hubiera decidido.

## Qué cambia

- **`shell_part(cmd)`**: lo que el shell ejecuta, sin cuerpos de heredoc (`<<`, `<<-`) ni texto entre comillas; dentro de `"…"` conserva `$(…)` y backticks, que sí corren. `is_credential` e `is_force_push` miran eso y además lo que se pasa a `sh -c` / `bash -c` / `eval`. Un recorrido lineal: 400k caracteres en 0,03 s.
- **`attribution(text, path)`**: no cuenta lo citado (bloques de código, `` `…` ``, «…», "…", líneas `>`), ni una sesión en la que la persona escribió algo que parece una decisión ("sí", "dale", "ok", "aprobado", "go ahead"…). Lee solo los mensajes propios de la persona (no resultados de herramientas, meta ni salidas de comandos) y solo lo nuevo del transcript.
- `bk monitor` usa las mismas funciones.

## Cómo probarlo

`bash tests/run.sh`: `todo ok` (`test_monitor.sh` sigue detectando `gh auth login` y la atribución de su transcript falso). Nuevos (`Detectores`): credencial y force push en pipelines, subshells, funciones, `sh -c`, `eval`, `$(…)` y backticks; nada en heredocs, `printf '…'`, `echo "…"` ni mensajes de commit; lineal con 400k caracteres; atribución solo si la persona no habló y no está citada; lectura incremental del transcript.

author: agilancer
body:
Cuts the GPU work per frame on phones by about 3.5 to 5.5x, and makes the frame-rate governor act on what it sees. The owner's first session on a phone found the frame rate too low.

**This has not run on a real phone**, so it isn't known yet whether it holds 60 fps on one. Settings now has a Frame rate readout to find out.

## What was slowing phones down

- **Too many pixels.** On a Pixel 7-sized screen it drew 1.7 million with expensive shading, then ran a full-screen pass at the screen's 2.6 million.
- **Quality that didn't drop.** On a phone with no GPU timers, the governor could take a GPU stuck at 30 fps for a browser's power cap, and after one test do nothing more.
- **Wasted work.** A 1536² blood map was redrawn every frame with or without blood, each touch button blurred the game behind it, and bodies off screen were still skinned and drawn.
- **Frames piling up.** Nothing stopped frames queueing ahead of the GPU, which on a slow one meant stalls of seconds and input lag.

## What changed

- **Phone tier** (also the Low setting on a PC). About 0.75 million pixels whatever the screen, which the browser stretches at no cost. Every shader has a cheaper `if (LEAN)` path. There are fewer passes, since a tiled GPU pays for each one.
- **Bodies.** Off screen they aren't skinned, and shadows and distant bodies use a coarse mesh built at load.
- **Governor** (`src/gfx/governor.js`). It goes by how often frames come round and how long the GPU takes over one, which any browser can report. It times the GPU under the title, so the first fight starts at a resolution it can hold, then moves from about 0.23 to 1.7 million pixels, dropping effects as it needs to.
- **All tiers.** No frames queued ahead of the GPU, nearest-first draw order, and leaves are the only static geometry that can discard. PC got faster too.
- **Everything else on phones.** A 60 fps cap on 120 Hz screens, cheaper sound panning, HUD bars that don't cause layout, and fewer planner threads during play, to reduce heat. Loading still uses the whole pool.

## What a phone gives up

At normal quality the two builds look close side by side. The grass is thinner and grows in tufts, distant lamp glow is gone, and there's no AO or sun shafts, as before. The ground uses one painting of each kind rather than a blend, so the yard is flatter at mid-range.

The slowest phones drop multisampling, bloom and grass blades, and the field goes to a flat lawn.

## Measured, on one machine (desktop Chrome, AMD RDNA 4, 16 logical cores)

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phone tier, GPU time, this desktop GPU | 1.47 ms | About 0.4 ms |
| Phone tier, software GPU, village view | 3750 ms | 665 ms |
| Phone tier, software GPU, duel | 2860 ms | 550 ms |
| Phone tier, software GPU, fight with crabs and blood | 2880 ms | 700 ms |
| PC, Ultra at 1600x900 on a 144 Hz display | 138.5 fps, 4.8 ms GPU | 143.3 fps, 3.4 ms GPU |
| PC, slowest 1% of frames | 14.2 ms | 7.5 ms |

The phone rows are at a Pixel 7's screen size. Neither GPU is a phone, so only the ratios mean anything, and neither charges for what a tiled GPU pays most for, so a phone's gain could be higher or lower.

On the software GPU, the real boot path did what it should: it dropped multisampling under the title, started at the lowest step, then shed bloom and grass in play. It held about 6 fps with no more than two frames queued and the simulation steady at 90 Hz, where the old build stalled for seconds.

Also run, with no GPU errors: `node tools/test_governor.mjs` (14 simulated phones), every quality and resolution step, the touch test, and no shared memory, Low on a PC, and High on a phone.

## Review

Two critics, both Claude subagents, reviewed side-by-side stills of the old and new builds. Both rejected the first version, with real findings: speckled wood, a blank visor, a mushy shield, blood thinned out and a pool that read as paint. Both approved the second, with notes.

Those notes were then applied without another review: anisotropy back to 2 (it barely helped, and cost 7 to 12% on the software GPU), lamp colour and choice of lamps, grass width, dry meadow patches, and the fine scratches beside a cut.

Left as they are: leaves have no alpha-to-coverage or sample mask at the lowest step, and the yard stays flatter at mid-range.

## Not tested

- **Never run:** a real phone with this version, an integrated GPU, Safari, Firefox.
- **Motion:** only measured. Visor flicker in a camera move scored no worse than the old build, though a softer picture scores lower anyway. Nobody has watched it, including for grass popping at the screen's edges and the coarse mesh switching at 14 to 16 m.
- **Fights:** 12 bot fights with recorded results at phone settings, 7 wins and 5 losses, against 5 of 6 at PC settings. That's too few to read much into, and the bot isn't a person. Most ran before the last look tweaks. A final fight ran on the finished code with no GPU errors, but its result wasn't recorded.

## Known problem

**One unexplained page crash.** One test run on a slightly earlier version had its page crash partway, with no crash report. It didn't recur in three later runs of three full fights each, one with the same script, and the cause is unknown. Other load on the machine at the time might have contributed, but that isn't established.

## To check

1. On a phone: `python tools/serve.py 8443 --lan --cert cert.pem --key key.pem`, with a certificate the phone trusts. Turn on Settings > Frame rate readout, play a fight, and note the fps, GPU busy time, render size and effects, plus the phone model.
2. Watch the grass and the knights' armour while moving, for popping or shimmer.
3. See whether the fight still feels fair, since fewer planner threads run on a phone.

author: alegruz
body:
## What

A first run that talks to people. The raw banner `Setup needs attention: InvalidProject: ...` and the opaque Start Page failure become a guided state.

- **One sentence on what is wrong, in plain words**: `DescribeSetupProblem` turns the controller's problem text into a headline, a detail and a fix (missing SDK, stale tooling, outdated project settings, unreadable settings file and so on). Unknown text is shown as written, never replaced by a guess.
- **One primary action**: **Repair project** (filled button). When repair cannot help (settings file or version problems) the button is **Open Project Settings** instead, so the primary action always does something useful. **Check again** and Dismiss stay secondary.
- **Progress and success**: while a repair or check runs, the notice becomes "Repairing your project…" with the step in words ("Preparing build settings", "Building and testing", "Finishing up") and a progress bar. When it verifies, "Your project is ready." appears and leaves on its own after a few seconds (or on Dismiss).
- **Start Page**: a project that fails to open shows the shared `StateView` (what happened, why, what to do, Choose Another Project…, Copy Details) instead of nothing at all. The raw code is kept only in Copy Details for bug reports.
- **No internal names anywhere on screen**: status bar, tooltips and the notice replace result-code names (`InvalidProject`, `BootstrapStale`…) with descriptions; a test fails if one leaks.

## Design rationale

- *Human-centric*: a person who has just installed Ludus needs "what's wrong, what do I press", not an enum. The banner has exactly one thing to press.
- *Form follows function*: the same banner carries needs-repair, working and ready, so the eye stays in one place for the whole flow rather than hunting across the status bar, a dialog and the Output panel.
- *Performance first*: nothing new runs; the text is derived from state already on the controller.
- The status bar says one thing about a failed check (the setup problem), not two descriptions of the same event.

## Tests

`setup_guidance_tests.cpp` (new): each known problem maps to a headline/fix, unknown text passes through, no result-code name survives sanitising, repairable vs not. `engine_pin_tests.cpp` updated: the notice now shows "Your project is ready." after a verified repair and is dismissible. Existing `[setup]`, `[notice]`, `[state]`, `[recent]` tests pass. Local: format, `source_policy.py` vs develop and main, `check_naming.py`, `check_target_macros.py`, `--tidy-changed`, `--tooling`.

## Screenshots (offscreen, on the build box)

`/workspace/design-impl-shots/round5/4-guided-first-run/`: `before-` and `after-` for `1-start-open-failed`, `2-needs-repair`, `3-working`, `4-ready`.

## Needs a Mac check

The progress bar styling and notice height on macOS, and the real repair on a fresh SDK (the tests use a fake adapter).

author: yasyf
body:
`ccx vcs pr watch` no longer prints `green` for a head whose workflows have not reported. A lane that merges on that event was merging ungraded: cc-skills#2884 read green at a new head with only two Socket checks in and its own CI still pending.

## What changes

A workflow run registers its check suite before its jobs, so the rollup of a fresh head can read `SUCCESS` on other apps' checks alone. The pull request read now also counts the head's unfinished GitHub Actions suites, in the one batched GraphQL query and in the REST fallback.

| Head state | `pr watch` before | `pr watch` now | `pr status` now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Socket checks pass, an Actions suite still open | `green` | no event | `ci pending: 1 running` |
| Every Actions suite finished, every check passing | `green` | `green` | `ci green` |
| A check failed, an Actions suite still open | `red` | `red` | `ci red` |

This carries out the instruction that green requires the head's expected workflows to have registered. It reuses the rule `pr-poll.sh` in the open-pr skill already applies: only Actions suites count, since other installed apps leave theirs queued forever (on #806's head, seven apps sit queued with no runs). The filter is GitHub's `appId` 15368 on both APIs, which I checked against that head.

## Sibling paths

`pr status` shares `prCIOf` and is fixed here. `ccx vcs status` has its own query and its own fresh-head guard, the checks it expects from merged peers, and emits no green event, so it is unchanged. `ship`'s CI watch follows the workflow runs themselves.

## Risk

- A head with no Actions suite yet reads as before, so the window between a push and GitHub creating the suite stays open: another app's check landing inside it can still fire `green`. I did not measure how often that happens. Closing it needs the head's workflow list, parsed per event and path filter, which this PR does not do.
- Each GraphQL pull request gains up to 50 suite nodes per poll, with the other apps' suites filtered out on the server. The REST fallback gains one call per pull request.

## Tests

`TestPRWatchHoldsGreenOnAFreshHeadUntilItsWorkflowsFinish` drives the shape from the report through a stubbed poll: a new head with Socket green and a queued suite emits only `new-head`, and `green` follows once the suite completes. `prCIOf` and the REST read gain cases. CI grades them; no test ran locally.

author: rodboev
body:
A new machine joining a busy team database now pulls its history in time linear in its size, staying further from the 5-minute `doSync` timeout. Pulling 30k jobs and 30k reviews into a fresh SQLite took 75.51s on main and takes 49.04s here, 35% less.

Each 100-row batch stays flat as the cursor advances (jobs 3.9-4.5ms, reviews 3.1-3.5ms), where main's jobs batches climbed from 2.2ms to 66ms and its reviews batches ran 28-89ms. The pull queries compare the cursor as a row, `(updated_at, id) > ($2, $3)`.

`PullReviews` now filters known jobs in Go instead of binding every local job UUID in `ANY($n)`. The cost: reviews whose parent job was deleted locally with `repo delete --cascade` are fetched and dropped while peers keep editing them. Ones after the last known review are refetched each pass. Results stay the same.

| Measurement | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pulling 30k jobs and 30k reviews into a fresh SQLite | 75.51 s | 49.04 s | 1.5x faster |

Substitui o site em HTML/Vue 2 com dados no navegador por um app **Next.js (React)** com **login e banco de dados no Supabase**, publicado na **Vercel**. Cada pessoa vê apenas a própria coleção.

- `supabase/schema.sql` com tabela, políticas e bucket; `.env.example`; `vercel.json` (framework Next.js).

## Testado na prévia da Vercel
Importação dos 21 perfumes do backup, cadastro com foto, edição, troca de foto, nota, favorito, duplicar, excluir, lista de desejos e "mover para a coleção", persistência após recarregar.

- `colecao-perfumes.vercel.app` passa a servir o site novo.
- O GitHub Pages deixa de funcionar (a `main` não terá mais `index.html`) — desativar em Settings → Pages.
- Garantir que a política `perfumes: ver a propria pasta` do `schema.sql` foi aplicada no Supabase (necessária para apagar imagens).

author: iskandr
body:
## Summary
pysam becomes a core dependency on Linux and macOS, so `pip install varcode` includes RNA read phasing (`RNAReadPhasingSource`) without an extra. It is not installed on Windows, which pysam does not support. Version 11.7.0: a minor release, because it changes the install requirements. Part of #640. **Stacked on #698 (11.6.1); merge that first.**

## Why
#640 asks for the common ORF and RNA features to come with a plain `pip install varcode`; any extra that stays needs a stated reason. #695 did the ORF half. `RNAReadPhasingSource` is the only pysam user. pysam publishes wheels only for Linux and macOS (cp39 to cp315) and does not build on Windows, while Varcode is classified as OS Independent. A platform marker gives Linux and macOS users the feature by default and keeps Varcode installable on Windows. Isovar, Varcode's main RNA consumer, already requires pysam, and CI gets it through osteosarc.

## What changed
- `requirements.txt`: `pysam>=0.21; sys_platform != "win32"`. The floor is unchanged from the old extra. The built wheel declares `Requires-Dist: pysam>=0.21; sys_platform != "win32"`.
- `pyproject.toml`: `rna = []`. Like `orf` and `uorf`, it stays so `pip install 'varcode[rna]'` keeps working.
- `varcode/rna_read_phasing.py`: the lazy import stays, because pysam is absent on Windows. Its `ImportError` now says Varcode installs pysam on Linux and macOS, that pysam does not support Windows, and to use WSL there. It no longer says to install the extra.
- Docs (README, `docs/phasing.md`, the getting-started dependency list) drop `pip install 'varcode[rna]'` and say where pysam is installed. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s setup no longer requests the `rna` extra.
- Tests: new `tests/test_rna_phasing_without_pysam.py` blocks `import pysam` and checks that error. The Osteosarc RNA test's skip reason no longer says "install .[rna]".

## Behavior change
On Linux and macOS, installing Varcode now also installs pysam, a 3–4 MB wheel. Nothing changes on Windows.

## Testing
- `./lint.sh` is clean.
- The RNA phasing, haplotype and contig-resolution tests plus the new test: 253 passed.
- I built the wheel and checked its `Requires-Dist` and `Provides-Extra` entries (`orf`, `uorf`, `rna`, `test-data`, `lint`).

author: thehcma
body:
## Summary

Refs #622 (first slice only: the issue stays open for the items listed under "Not done").

A recorded flow was run with whatever values the caller bound, so an agent decided what went into the form. This makes the inputs part of the flow.

- A site-model flow may declare `params`, each with a kind: `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, a real date), `choice` (one of the recorded options), `file` (an existing regular file, not a link) or `text` (1 to 500 printable characters). A `fill` or `upload` step names the parameter it uses with `bind`.
- `ledger apply` checks every declared parameter before the item is staged or the browser is touched: each must be supplied, nothing undeclared may be, and each must be valid. A refusal lists every problem at once, never shows a value (amounts, merchants and paths are private; an undeclared name is shown quoted), and changes nothing in the ledger.
- Model rules: `bind` is only allowed on `fill` and `upload`; an `upload` takes a `file` parameter and a `fill` any other kind; a flow that declares parameters must bind every `fill` and `upload`; a parameter cannot be called `item`; choices are stored in the model, so they may not hold quotes, `=`, `@` or a long run of digits.
- The run's `item` binding is always the ledger item, so a value cannot rename it. A missing model or flow no longer stages an item. The model version recorded for an item is the loaded model's.
- Compatibility: the schema stays at version 1 with `params` and `bind` optional. A model without them loads and is stored exactly as before, a flow without `params` keeps the older unchecked bindings, `model diff` reports a changed flow, and exploring a parameterized model keeps its parameters (it used to drop them).
- Applying a verified item again is still a no-op.

Not done (still open on #622): resolved locators unique at each step, pre- and postconditions with settle waits, declared human hand-off steps, private `verify` steps, stop-and-record on divergence, plan authoring (`model flow add`) and checking that a file is the rehomed receipt of the ledger item.

## Test plan

- Validator tests per kind (dates, choices, files including links and directories, text), the all-problems-at-once message with no value in it, quoted undeclared keys, and the no-parameters passthrough.
- Model tests: parameters and bindings round-trip, an old model keeps its stored shape, and each malformed declaration is refused (bind rules, choices, names, counts, typed data in choices).
- Ledger tests: a refused run stages and runs nothing, a missing model leaves the ledger empty, validated values reach the steps and the default runner, the item cannot be overridden, a verified item is a no-op without parameters.
- Exploring a parameterized model keeps its parameters and bindings.
- Opus review done; its findings (parameters dropped on re-explore, bind not checked against its step, typed data in choices, the item override, ordering) are fixed with tests.
- Local `pre-pr-checks` exit 0.
- CodeRabbit CLI is not signed in locally, so that step was skipped; the PR review runs it.

author: markwgreenlee
body:
Ports everything the VSS scheduler gained today, and fixes the bug that made every icon in the deployed app render as an empty box.

**The icon fix.** The app is served from `/ecvp-2026-scheduler/`, but the icon fonts were fetched at runtime from `/assets/...` at the domain root, where they 404 — so no glyph ever loaded. The base path was set as `expo.web.baseUrl` in app.json, which Expo does not read; it reads `expo.experiments.baseUrl`. Confirmed against the live site before the change: the font URL the bundle requests returns 404, the same path under `/ecvp-2026-scheduler` returns 200.

**New screens.** Home (venue, what is on now, your next starred item, four ways in), Program (a day at a glance with parallel sessions side by side, starred/live edges, a now line, gaps where nothing is on), the session view (header plus contents in order, through to the existing abstract sheet), and Venue Map (every room with what is on there today; floor plans drop into `assets/floors/`). Tab bar becomes Home · Program · Search · Schedule · Settings and the Now tab is removed, its content folded into Home and the Program badges.

**Also:** the icon set the VSS organisers suggested (list for the programme, star for the schedule, flag for the venue); a running app now notices a new release (service-worker update check on returning to the foreground, throttled to once a minute, with a reload prompt when a new build takes over); meeting identity, venue, room labels, brand colour and Home announcements moved into `src/config/conference.js`.

**Shared code stays shared.** `src/utils/program.js`, `src/utils/venue.js`, the four screens and `UpdatePrompt.js` are byte-identical to the VSS build — verified by digest. Two generalisations were needed for this programme and went into all three:
- item counts no longer name a block's items by the block's own kind, so a keynote reads "1 keynote" and a social "1 social" rather than "1 talk"; only a symposium's items are counted as talks
- a session whose presentations carry no individual time shows each row's position instead of repeating the session's start time down the page

**Verified against this programme:** 614 presentations land in 44 session rows with no double-counting, 13 period headers, 8 gap rows across five days; 30 non-poster blocks have a running order and 7 do not; poster blocks group by topic (Poster Session 1: 59 posters in 6 topics, first board M1AM1). Web export builds clean with no root-absolute asset URL left in the bundle.

author: cameronhejazifar
body:
darp-masq is published on host port 53, which some machines can't give up: a VPN client's DNS proxy (Cloudflare WARP, for one) holds 53 too. Moving darp-masq by hand doesn't survive darp. Deploy recreates it on 53 whenever it isn't running, and install rewrites /etc/resolver/test without a port.

`darp config set dns-port <port>` (a global `dns_port`; `darp config rm dns-port` undoes it) moves it. Deploy publishes darp-masq on 127.0.0.1:<port> for UDP and TCP, while dnsmasq still listens on 53 inside the container. It replaces a running darp-masq published anywhere else and keeps a matching `port` line in /etc/resolver/test, using sudo only when the file differs. Install writes the same file, and doctor warns when either one drifts from the setting. The bind is loopback-only on purpose: a moved darp-masq only has to answer the host's resolver. Only macOS reads that `port` line, so the docs point Linux users at urls-in-hosts.

Unset, or set to 53, a stock install behaves as before: the same 53:53 publish, a darp-masq on 53 left running, and a resolver file without a `port` line left alone. The undo that makes `config rm dns-port` work does reach setups made by hand. An unset deploy replaces a darp-masq published off 53 and removes a `port` line, whoever put them there. configuration.md says so and tells anyone who moved darp-masq by hand to set dns-port before deploying.

Deploy now waits for the darp-masq start and the resolver write. If the engine refuses the start (the port is taken) or sudo fails, deploy prints a warning that includes the engine's error, suggests dns-port when 53 was the port taken, and carries on, since names in /etc/hosts still resolve. Install now fails when sudo does, instead of reporting a resolver file it never wrote. darp-masq keeps `--rm`, because Docker rejects `--rm` combined with `--restart`.

The port matching, publish args, resolver rendering and sync decision, the start warning and the sudo-step check are pure functions covered in tests/dns_port_test.rs. The engine and sudo calls around them need a container engine, as cmd_deploy does. A separate commit adds a Test job to ci.yml: ci.yml never ran `cargo test`, and integration.yml runs only the ignored smoke tests, so the unit and integration suites weren't gating anything. The suite passes on macOS and on Linux (rust:1.94-slim). I'm happy to split that commit into its own PR.

Backward compatible: skip_serializing_if keeps `dns_port` out of configs that don't set it, and Config::load sets no deny_unknown_fields, so an older binary ignores the key, including in a pre_config.

author: hashimthearab
body:
`Close` keeps the connection up for `closeLinger` after the peer acknowledges the final message, so a client has time to read it before it sees the closure. This only ran when `drain` had to wait. If the peer acknowledged the message before `Close` started, `Close` returned at once and the client could still lose it.

`Send` now records when it last wrote, and `drain` waits whatever remains of `closeLinger` since then. The time keeps its monotonic reading, so a system clock change cannot stretch the wait. A connection with nothing sent recently still closes at once.

Most callers write and close within microseconds, so they usually reach the existing wait. This affects a caller that leaves more than one round trip between its last write and `Close`.

### Checks

Simulated networks, with a libwebrtc client and 20 joins per row. The gap is the time between the final message arriving and the channel closing.

| Before `Close` | Smallest gap on `main` | Smallest gap with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Final message acknowledged 30 ms earlier | 30 ms | 100 ms |
| Same, at 10 MB/s | 30 ms | 100 ms |
| Idle for 250 ms | 251 ms, `Close` took 0 ms | 250 ms, `Close` took 0 ms |
| Write, then `Close` straight away | 106 ms | 105 ms |

`TestCloseLingersWhenAlreadyAcknowledged` fails if the wait is removed, with `Close` finishing under a millisecond after the final write. `TestCloseSkipsLingerWhenIdle` covers the idle case and `TestSendRecordsLastSend` covers what the wait is timed from. `go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run ./...` pass, and the new tests pass 100 runs out of 100.

User-supplied idea content or an explicitly adopted suggestion suppresses automatic generation across the eligible Person pool. Empty placeholders do not; explicitly planned stubs remain visible while empty placeholders outside the plan stay out of the picker.

When useful ideas and recipient profile/history/idea context are absent, the Occasion Overview immediately shows an inline Add details / Create general ideas prompt. Add details opens the PersonProfile modal; Save persists the supplied details, closes the modal, and starts generation in the same visit. Cancellation returns without generation. General ideas are explicitly requested with only the recipient name as supplied recipient context and are labelled general. Existing usable context bypasses the prompt.

Consider these suggestions remain transient until Add to occasion creates a GiftIdea and OccasionGiftIdea. Other suggestions remain through the visit, including profile/detail/research/modal navigation, then disappear on departure. The exit confirmation applies only to reminder visits with available suggestions and no adoption; saving profile data is not adoption. Hard-close recovery is outside the MVP.

author: dannote
body:
### Summary

Opening and switching pages in a large `.fig` was slow in a visible tab and stalled in a hidden one.

Switching to a page loaded every page holding a component set its instances use, then the pages of the sets those use. Switching a variant needs the rest of its set, but the whole page brings every example and documentation layer with it. On the shadcn/ui kit, a page with six instances pulled in about 18,000 nodes from Input Group, Button, Combobox, Table and other pages, took 6.2 s, and grew the reader worker to 365 MB. Reading a page now brings in each used set whole, and the editor lays out just those sets: the same switch loads 690 nodes in 276 ms with an 84 MB worker.

A hidden tab draws no animation frames. Opening a file waited for one before reading, and the canvas waited for one before starting, so an open begun in a background tab sat idle until the tab was shown, and a page switch drawn there could fail with "The operation was timed out". Now the open runs in a hidden tab and the scene waits to be drawn until the tab is shown.

### What changed

- The reader's dependency closure includes the other variants of a used variant's set, once per set, except Figma's internal library copies; `preparePage` lays out and loads fonts for those sets instead of preparing their pages.
- `nextFrame` (`@open-pencil/vue/shared/frame`) resolves at once while the page is hidden and stops waiting when it is hidden mid-wait, by visibility rather than a timer; the canvas loader and the app's former `yieldToUI` copies use it.
- The presentation timeout pauses while the page is hidden, as it already does while no canvas is attached.

### AI assistance

Models: Claude Opus 5.5

### Validation

- `bun test packages/fig/tests packages/core/tests/editor/pages packages/core/tests/editor/components packages/core/tests/io/formats/fig`: 798 pass, including a new closure test and the page loading test, which now checks that a set's page stays unloaded.
- `bun test tests/app/editor/preparation/controller.test.ts packages/vue/tests/shared/frame.test.ts`: 14 pass, including hidden-page cases for the presentation limit and the frame wait.
- `packages/fig/tests/document/record-headers.test.ts`, which reads every page of `gold-preview.fig`, takes 2.4 s as before; expanding internal library copies made it about 17 s, which is why they are excluded.

author: lognorman20
body:
## TLDR

The cabal chat now shows its pinned messages in one glass capsule floating over the top of the thread, as in v5 frame `03-cabal-chat`. Tapping the capsule cycles through the pins and scrolls to each one. The chevron opens a "Pinned" list, and the message menu gains Pin and Unpin.

## Why

The chat had no pinned area, and the message menu had no Pin or Unpin, even though the pins model from #8277 was in place. That PR left two gaps that this one closes. A deleted pinned message stayed in the pins until the next `pin.updated` event or attach. Pins also ignored the blocked-authors filter.

Closes #7908

## What changed

- **Capsule** (`ChatPinCapsule`): a `safeAreaInset` on the thread, so the thread starts below it and scrolls under it.
  - Shows the pin icon, the pinner's first name in Footnote semibold, the tail-truncated text, "1 of 2" when there are two or more pins, and a chevron.
  - Hidden when there are no pins or while offline.
  - Glass on iOS 26 through the new `monacoGlassCapsule()` modifier, `.regularMaterial` with a hairline on iOS 18, and an opaque sunken surface with Reduce Transparency.
  - Grows instead of clipping at accessibility text sizes, with two lines there.
- **Interaction:**
  - Tapping the text area moves to the next pin, scrolls the thread to that message and plays a selection haptic.
  - The chevron opens the list. Both targets are at least 44 pt tall.
  - VoiceOver reads "Pinned by Christelle: <text>. 1 of 2." as one element, with the actions "Next pin" and "Show all pins".
- **List sheet** (`ChatPinListSheet`): a `monacoSheet` titled "Pinned" with no hand-set detents.
  - Each row shows the author's face, name, up to three lines of text and the time. Tapping a row dismisses the sheet and scrolls to the message.
  - "Unpin" appears for anyone who `canPin`, with an Undo toast.
- **Message menu:** "Pin" or "Unpin" below Copy, for anyone who `canPin`. The model's limit and forbidden errors show as toasts.
- **Soft edge:** `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: .top)` on iOS 26, and a 46 pt gradient mask on iOS 18 while the capsule shows.
- **Model fixes** (mobile-core):
  - Pins skip blocked authors and the masked placeholders (`deleted`) the backend has returned since #8269, so neither uses a slot in the capsule or the list.
  - A deleted message leaves the pins at once, both on the realtime `message.deleted` and on a local delete.
  - Pins now load on `open()` and `reload()` as well as on attach and `pin.updated`, so they show even when realtime has not attached.
  - The capsule line receives the real cabal name.
- **Identifiers:** `chat-pin-capsule`, `chat-pin-next`, `chat-pin-list-button`, `chat-pin-list`, `chat-pin-row-<id>` and `chat-pin-unpin-<id>`.
- **Sample harness:**
  - The `cabal-chat` sample (`SampleAPI`) serves two pins.
  - The `ChatSampleQA` chat sample serves pins by default or with `-MonacoChatSamplePins`.
  - `sample-screens.txt` gains a `chat-pins` line.

## Proof

- **Stage 0:** `cd apps/backend && go run ./cmd/monacoctl agents check` passed on the head commit. The flows, journeys, touches, xcode (build-for-testing) and swift rows were all ok.
- **App build:** `just build mobile` printed `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.
- **Swift tests:** `swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors --filter 'ChatPinsModel|ChatSessionTests|ChatSessionDeleteTests|ChatSessionOpen'` in `packages/mobile-core` executed 72 tests with 0 failures. The new tests cover:
  - the blocked and masked filter (`ChatPinsModelHidingTests`)
  - drop on delete, both realtime and local (`ChatSessionDeleteTests`)
  - pins loading on an open where realtime never attaches (`ChatSessionOpenPinsTests`)
- **Repo rules:** `swift test --filter 'MonacoCoreTests.RepoRulesTests'` executed 9 tests with 0 failures.
- **Screens:** `scripts/qa/screens.sh --check` reported that the manifest covers every sample harness (915 screens). `python3 scripts/qa/journey.py check` found no new warnings.
- **frame | before | after** for `03-cabal-chat`, shot from the `cabal-chat` sample (`MONACO_QA_SCREEN_ONLY`, `scripts/qa/screens.sh`, `scripts/qa/parity.py sheet --design v5`). The before shot comes from parent 720dae20e on the same sim.

  ![03-cabal-chat frame before after](https://github.com/Munyon-Canyon/monaco/blob/evidence/7908-screens/03-cabal-chat-sheet.png?raw=true)

- **xxxLarge** (accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large): the capsule grows to two lines and nothing clips.

  ![03-cabal-chat xxxLarge](https://github.com/Munyon-Canyon/monaco/blob/evidence/7908-screens/03-cabal-chat-xxxl-sheet.png?raw=true)

- **Not verified:**
  - The live staging pin, cycle, unpin, undo and fourth-pin pass, VoiceOver, Reduce Transparency and the iOS 18 render on a device.
  - A recording of the scroll-under.
  - MonacoTests, which run only in the hourly staging indicator by operator rule. `ChatPinCapsuleTests` compiled in stage 0's build-for-testing.

## What came up

- **Masked pins hidden** (product default from monaco-66): a blocked author's pin, which the backend returns as a masked placeholder, is hidden entirely instead of drawing an empty "deleted" row.
- **Pins only loaded on attach:** in the sample, and in the app whenever Ably does not attach before the open timeout, the capsule never appeared. Pins now also load on open and reload.
- **One accessibility element:** the capsule is a single VoiceOver element, as the ticket specifies, so XCUITest does not see the inner `chat-pin-next` and `chat-pin-list-button` identifiers. Lane E journeys can tap `chat-pin-capsule` and use its accessibility actions.
- **Filed #8297:** every `-MonacoChatSampleQA` sample line (`chat-poll`, `chat-thread`, the new `chat-pins`) shoots Home, not the chat. The bug is already on the parent commit, so this PR's proof uses `cabal-chat`.
- **New tokens:** `MonacoTheme.Typo.footnoteStrong` (Footnote semibold had no token), and `MonacoIcon.pin` / `.unpin`.
- **Stage 0 ran several times:**
  - The first run failed because MonacoTests could not reach `ChatPinLine`'s internal initializer. The initializer is now public.
  - Later runs followed fixes that the proof shots exposed: the sample had no pins, the thread started under the capsule, and the capsule was too tall.

## Reviewer focus

- **Gate change:** `RepoRulesAllowlist.txt` gains one `gradient` row for `ChatPinCapsule.swift`. The ticket requires the iOS 18 gradient fade, and the `gate-changes` job warns on this row.
- **Open latency:** `ChatSession.open()` now waits for the pins request before it drains the open buffer.
- **Shared list:** `ChatList` (`GroupChatParts.swift`) gains a `scrollRequest`, and the thread view passes it through.

## Needs from Logan

Nothing.

Generation time of one job alone (generateClockAlternatives, quiet machine, load 0.3, one job at a time, node `--max-old-space-size=4096`):

author: achubaty
body:
`docker-publish.yml` had no `concurrency` group, so merges close together started parallel runs that all push the same tags (`main`, `ubuntu-<version>`, `ubuntu-latest`, `latest`). The tags end up on whichever run finishes last, which can be an older commit's images. This adds:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: docker-publish-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

At most one run per branch is in progress. A newer push waits for it, so it publishes last. A run in progress is never cancelled. GitHub keeps one waiting run per group, so if a second push arrives while one is waiting, the waiting run is cancelled and the newest commit is built. Scheduled runs share the group; they build the same `main`.

Caveat: a release's `.sif` job (`apptainer-publish.yml`, #82) waits for the Docker run of the release's commit and fails if that run doesn't succeed. That run can only be cancelled if it is still waiting and two more pushes to `main` follow before it starts.
