author: arminazimi
body:
## The gap, measured on current `main` (`bb92ae76`)

`main` still holds **46 non-null assertions** in the nine files this issue names — confirmed with the AST walk (`ts.isNonNullExpression`), not the allowlist:

| file | assertions | file | assertions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/fix/runtime-pins.ts` | 8 | `src/fix/codemods/python-imp.ts` | 6 |
| `src/fix/codemods/python-utcnow.ts` | 8 | `src/fix/codemods/python-renames.ts` | 6 |
| `src/fix/codemods/dockerfile-legacy.ts` | 4 | `src/fix/codemods/terraform-legacy.ts` | 5 |
| `src/fix/codemods/node-buffer.ts` | 4 | `src/fix/codemods/node-renames.ts` | 1 |
| `src/fix/codemods/node-util-is.ts` | 4 | | |

`benchmarks/quality-allowlist.json` after this PR: non-null **83 entries / 320 sites → 74 entries / 274 sites**. The nine `#2223` entries are deleted; no entry is added anywhere, and `complexity`, `functionLength`, `fileSize` and `asUnknownAs` keep their counts.

## What replaced them

- **41 `required(...)` calls** (`src/required.ts`, the house idiom) covering 42 assertions — one call in `python-utcnow.ts` replaces the two `last!.endIndex` reads on a single line by making the binding itself a `Node`.
- **1 `split(sep, 1).join()`** for `child.text.split(".")[0]!` in `python-renames.ts:493` — same value, no assertion, no decision point.
- **3 assertions folded into a null-aware read of a value the removed condition already tested**: `shape?.fromImport !== undefined` + the narrowed `shape.fromImport` (`python-utcnow.ts:118-119`, which replaces `shape!.fromImport` twice), and one bound field read in `directImportsFor` (`python-renames.ts:430`).
- **1 new file-local helper**, `namedChildNodes(node)` in `python-utcnow.ts`, which replaces two copies of the identical `namedChildren.filter((child): child is Node => child !== null)` predicate; one of those copies feeds `.at(-1)`, so the list now has a type that needs no assertion.

`required` is a call, not a condition, and `?.` is not a decision point in `tools/check-quality.ts:209` (`cyclomaticComplexity` counts `if`/`for`/`while`/`case`/`catch`/`?:` and `&&`/`||`/`??` only), so the conversions add no branch. The two functions that were restructured — `directImportsFor` and `isTestcaseBase`, neither capped — each give up an `&&` and gain one `if`/`||` in the same place, so their measured complexity is unchanged.

No `as T`, `as any`, `as unknown as`, `@ts-ignore`, new `any`, new assertion or new allowlist entry appears in the diff. Behaviour is unchanged: no expected value, golden file or corpus output is edited.

## Ceilings

These nine files carry **17 `complexity` entries (sum 345) and 14 `functionLength` entries (927 lines)**, all exact-match. Every one still measures its recorded value:

```
$ node dist/tools/check-quality.js
quality: 395 files, all targets hold
```

That is the load-bearing claim of the PR — `plan`, `targetsFor`, `rewriteFor`, `utilBindings`, `classify`, `inspectDatetimeImports` and the rest are capped, so each conversion had to be same-line and same-branch. The two functions that grew (`directImportsFor` +1 line, `isTestcaseBase` +1 line) have no entry and stay well inside the limits. `complexity` and `functionLength` entries for these files are byte-identical to `main`'s.

`benchmarks/corpus-affected.ts` is untouched: `tests/corpus-affected.test.ts:130` walks `src/detectors` only, and this PR adds no detector import of `src/required.ts`.

## Tests

Brief step 3 asks for a test for any path that was unguarded and is now reachable. **None is**: every `required` throw sits behind a guarantee the surrounding code already enforces —

- an index bound the loop proves (`text[index]` with `index < text.length`, `declaration.arguments[index]` inside `index < length` with the even-length check above it);
- a mandatory capture group (`match[1]`/`match[2]` of `^(\s*)MAINTAINER\s+([\s\S]*)$` and of the `ENV` and `from … import …` patterns, `ENGINES_NODE`'s three groups, `NODE_BELOW_MAJOR`);
- a `Map` built from the very key set it is read with (`reported.get(rule.id)` over `rules.map(...)`);
- an earlier refusal of the `undefined` case — `runtime-pins.ts:101` refuses a line-less finding before the target map is built, `terraform-legacy.ts:222` skips an empty `lineTargets` before `targets[0]` is read, and `checkArguments` returns a reason for `utcfromtimestamp()` with no arguments before `.at(-1)` runs.

The findings that reach `terraform-legacy.ts` are the detector's own: `index.ts:298` sets `location: { path, line: declaration.line, column: … }` and `parseTerraformLegacy` declares `line: number`, so `required(target.finding.location.line, …)` cannot fire either. `required`'s own throw stays covered by `tests/required.test.ts:8`.

## Coverage

I am not quoting a before/after coverage percentage for this branch. Local coverage runs on this machine are not repeatable — two runs of one byte-identical `dist/` gave 94.745% lines / 87.715% branches and 94.655% / 87.648%, with individual files swinging by up to 18 lines. CI's `coverage` job, which compares against `main`'s stored artifact (`tools/coverage-thresholds.ts:115`), is the authoritative measurement, and structurally this diff adds no branch site in any capped function.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — exit 0, `ℹ tests 4286`, `ℹ pass 4286`, `ℹ fail 0`
- [x] `node dist/tools/check-quality.js` — `395 files, all targets hold`
- [x] `npx biome format` over the nine files — no changes requested
- [x] AST re-count of non-null assertions in the nine files — 0
- [x] `eslint-suppressions.json` untouched — none of the nine files carries an entry, and the file still lists 168 files
- [x] `git diff --stat` — 10 files, +68/−112 (the 63 deleted allowlist lines are the nine entries)

No changelog fragment: `changes/README.md` says not to add one for `refactor` changes, and this preserves behaviour.

**Merge order**: #2409 and #2410 delete other `nonNull` entries in the same JSON array and edit the `src/required.ts` ecosystems line in `benchmarks/corpus-affected.ts`. Whichever of the three merges last will need a rebase; the deletions are of disjoint entries.

Closes #2243

author: mopalio
body:
Ports the `design/` prototype into the real app: full bleed hero with the pressure washer, a swipeable pricing rail, the before/after gallery, the design's booking form, and the water loader, now also playing when you move between sections.

## What changed

**Hero.** The car fills the viewport edge to edge, copy sits lower left behind a scrim. Hold the pointer anywhere on it and a lance fires from the bottom of the frame: narrow high power footprint, mist, the paint coming clean under it. Past 60 percent coverage the rest rinses off on its own, a shine sweeps across, and the stamp lands.

Two constraints from the prototype are load bearing and kept:

* Progress is tracked with a coverage grid (`Uint8Array`, 46 x 32), not `getImageData`. Canvas pixel reads throw once a cross origin image has been drawn.
* The canvas sizes from `offsetWidth`, not `getBoundingClientRect`, so a fractional layout width cannot drift the backing store.

**Pricing.** Three cards above the breakpoint, a swipeable rail below it. Native scroll snap carries touch and trackpad momentum; pointer drag is layered on for mouse. A drag never fires a click on the card underneath. The breakpoint (976px) was measured rather than picked: a card's feature line starts wrapping at 254px, so with a 280px floor plus gaps and padding the grid stops fitting just under 976.

**Palette.** Sampled from the MDETAILING wordmark. There is no logo file, so the wordmark is the mark: a chrome ramp off its gradient, no accent hue, white as the only bright. Defined as tokens in `globals.css` under `@theme inline`, with the old token names kept as aliases so untouched sections stay styled.

**Gallery.** The prototype's generated cars, with a wipe handle you drag across the dirty and clean states.

**Cards and buttons.** Cards tilt toward the pointer. Buttons fill with water on hover: a wave crest on a data URI mask riding up over a fill.

**Booking form.** The design's form, posting to the existing route. Date only, no time field.

**Section transitions.** Clicking any in page link drops the foam sheet, moves the page behind it, and pulls it off. Links that leave the page, open a tab, or are clicked with a modifier are untouched.

## Fixes carried along

* **The build failed without a mail key.** `new Resend(...)` ran at module scope, so `next build` threw while collecting page data on any machine without the key. Built on first request now; the build passes with no key at all.
* **Hydration mismatch** from `Math.random()` ids in `Input.tsx`, replaced with `useId`.
* **Email HTML injection.** Customer typed fields went unescaped into the outgoing mail. Escaped now.
* **Key naming.** The route reads `RESEND_API_KEY` first and falls back to `NEXT_PUBLIC_RESEND_API_KEY`. Anything prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` is meant to be readable in the browser, which a mail API key should not be. Nothing leaked, since only the server route ever read it, but the name invites it.
* **A prototype bug.** The jet loop and the auto rinse shared one rAF handle, so releasing the trigger after crossing 60 percent cancelled the rinse at its first frame and the shine and stamp never ran. That is what people actually do, so it was reliably broken. Separate handles now.

## Before merging

* **Set `RESEND_API_KEY` in Vercel** or the booking form fails at runtime. The old name still works as a fallback.
* This branch sits on top of `fix/securityUpdate`, so merging carries `5a408a8 update nextjs to be more secure` along with it.

## Testing

`next build` passes clean. The hero wash, pricing rail, tilt, button fill, gallery wipe and intro loader were all exercised in a browser.

The section transition was verified functionally rather than by eye: cover reaches 100, the scroll lands exactly on the target section's `offsetTop` behind the curtain, the hash updates, and with rAF driven on timers the wipe completes and clears. It was never watched running, because the browser pane in that session was hidden and `requestAnimationFrame` is frozen outright in a backgrounded page. Worth one look in a real browser.

## Research only — parallel #30, no deployment

Exact tested parent PR #594: `77d5c760c847d6e2f544512e80fd8598fd610dad`. This research branch adds only a genuine signed browser-to-disposable-local-Supabase end-to-end harness, safety/CI contract tests, a reproducible README, and a dedicated no-deploy workflow. Chromium + WebKit at 320/390/430, two separate genuine signed password users, 3 confirmed regions per synthetic JPEG, real IndexedDB, private cloud uploads, signed HTTP RLS, cross-account denials, recovery from private cloud in fresh browsers, 60 audited PNGs and full Node regression. Failure/race cases not yet independently proven include token expiry and refresh failure, interrupted uploads/backup commits, stale decode and crop-editor logout, queued preflight, missing/corrupt cloud photos, concurrent CAS conflicts and source-region duplicate retry. author: teemow
body:
Fixes https://github.com/giantswarm/beekeeper/issues/3265

## Problem

The merge-result validation builds base + head with `git merge --no-ff` in a temporary worktree. That merge used the machine's git config, so with `commit.gpgsign=true` and no usable key every validated merge was refused with `merge-result validation unavailable: creating merge result: ... gpg failed to sign the data`.

## Change

- `cmd/reviewedmergecheck.go`: the merge runs with `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. The commit is thrown away with the worktree, so it needs no signature.
- `TestMergeResultIgnoresCommitSigning`: configures `commit.gpgsign=true` and a failing `gpg.program` on the repository and expects a clean validation. It sets `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0` because `testenv` turns signing off through the environment, which outranks repository config and would otherwise hide the bug.
- Changelog entry.

## Origin

No change merged tonight introduced this.

- The merge line dates from https://github.com/giantswarm/beekeeper/pull/2163 (2026-11-03) and has never set signing.
- https://github.com/giantswarm/beekeeper/pull/2291 (2026-11-04 00:58 CET) changed how the failure reads. Before it, any failed merge was reported as `branch conflicts with its base`; since then only unmerged index entries count as a conflict, and this failure is a tooling refusal.
- Of the commits from 2026-11-04 12:00 CET on that touch the merge path, none changes signing, git config or this merge. The only one touching this file, https://github.com/giantswarm/beekeeper/pull/3248, adds entries to a host-failure diagnostic list.

The check runs only when the base has moved past the head, so it needs both a signing config and a behind head to appear.

## Verification

- Plain git, signing on with a failing signer: the merge exits 128 with `gpg failed to sign the data`; the same merge with `-c commit.gpgsign=false` exits 0 and the commit is unsigned.
- `gofmt` is clean. The Go test was not run locally (no local builds for this change); CI runs it.

author: stephanbaum
body:
Ports the owner-approved liquid-glass reveal from `docs/design/holo/reveal-studies.html` into the app (ADR-0032).

- **Unlock:** the live vault DOM is revealed through a `clip-path` lens that grows from the click point. A WebGL2 canvas (no pointer events) draws only the glass rim and bevel band. The owner's tuned values are fixed in `reveal/timing.ts`. The app stays clickable during the animation.
- **Lock:** `lock` IPC first; in the same task the vault is painted into a sealed snapshot and unmounted, so revealed secrets leave the DOM before the first lock frame. The painter never reads `[data-secret]` content (only the static `data-mask`), never reads input/textarea values, and skips dialogs and visually hidden text.
- **Instant swaps:** idle, sleep, screen and tray locks, plus onboarding and kit transitions.
- **Fallbacks:** no WebGL2, a lost context, a texture that is too big or slow frames → lens only; reduced motion → 250 ms crossfade; jsdom → instant.
- **Focus and inert:** the non-target layer is `inert` + `aria-hidden`; focus goes to the vault `main` on unlock and to the password field on lock.

Tests: vitest for timing, lens, frames, choreography, phase reducer, driver, painter secret exclusion (incl. the real SecretField/TotpCode/Generator components), RevealStage and lock ordering; `e2e/reveal.spec.ts` (off-centre click, clicking mid-animation, lock path, end state, reduced motion). Locally: desktop vitest 657 passed, e2e 39/39, lint + typecheck clean.

Known fidelity limits of the snapshot: no box shadows, gradients, pseudo-elements or ellipsis; foil canvases are frozen during lock.

body:
## What changed

The analyze sub-boards draw the flags, then the verdict, then the sanity check as a chain. That chain is the order `analyze` runs them in; none of the three feeds the next. This PR adds the same top-level `execution_order` note to `analyze-flags.d2`, `analyze-verdict.d2` and `analyze.d2` (on the last, between sections 8 and 9):

> Execution order, not dependency: the margin of safety and the verdict read the value after the governance discount and the latest close; the sanity check reads the latest close, net income, diluted shares and revenue, the discounted cash flow's intrinsic value per share and enterprise value, and the sector multiples. The flags change none of them, and the sanity check does not read the verdict.

The statechart, the edges, `models/` and `src/` are unchanged.

## Decisions

- **The copy corrects the Agent Brief's sentence.** The brief said the three "read the DCF result and the price only". That is not what the code does:
  - The margin of safety reads the value after the governance discount (`analysis.py`).
  - `_sanity_check` also reads net income, diluted shares, revenue and the sector multiples.
  - Since #219, `_sanity_check` also reads the intrinsic value per share.
- **"discounted cash flow" is spelled out.** Writing "DCF's" failed `test_acronyms_are_expanded` on the flags and verdict boards, where the acronym is not expanded earlier.
- **A guard test backs the note.** `test_flags_change_neither_the_verdict_nor_the_sanity_check` forces every flag red and asserts that the margin of safety, `margin_verdict` and `sanity_check` do not change. I checked its red state by temporarily making `analyze` depend on the flags; that edit was reverted.
- **Only three SVGs were re-rendered.** The three SVGs and `rendered.sha256` come from the `pipeline-render` CI artifact, because d2 is not installed locally. The other SVGs are untouched.
- **Rebased onto #219.** That change made the render files conflict and gave `_sanity_check` a new input. I took master's render files and changed the note copy, then took a fresh CI render.

Plan, with its assumptions and grilling: `docs/plans/2026-11-04-221-execution-order-notes.md`.

- Pinned note text: `_ANALYZE_TEXT` / `_ANALYZE_NODES` entries in `test_pipeline_diagram.py` and `test_pipeline_subboards.py`.

- No web UI is involved, so there was no browser script. No manual verification is pending.
